# QA Audit

## 2026-07-30 Asia/Shanghai - Temporary Worker Model Discovery Ingress Propagation Retry

- Root cause: temporary Worker readiness and pre-browser model discovery use different Node processes and fresh connections. Two consecutive exact Worker signatures therefore prove the probed route but cannot guarantee that the next connection reaches an edge where the anonymous deployment has propagated. The observed next request returned an HTML 404 with no trusted ZeroChat response-source header, while the preceding browser-shaped, models-shaped, and host-management probes had passed.
- Fix: the shared provider network boundary retries only an idempotent model-list GET when a proxy is configured and the bounded observation is exactly canonical `/proxy`, HTTP 404, HTML, not redirected, and `responseSource: none`. It makes at most five attempts one second apart, cancels only discarded bodies, and leaves the final response readable for the existing failure classifier. Direct-provider responses and Worker responses carrying trusted `upstream` or `transport-error` provenance are never retried.
- Evidence: three focused tests failed first because the retry boundary did not exist, then passed 16/16 with the existing network trace tests. They prove recovery after one untrusted ingress response, no retry for trusted Worker failures or direct-provider traffic, and bounded exhaustion with the final response preserved. The real anonymous Worker drill then reached readiness on probe 24 and passed with the current-source credential-confirmed browser-origin attempt at 9,166 bytes / SHA-256 `899A0F049FFD2C5F356D44114626AEF92B6E0EDC58EA3121D6E31D1098AEF2FC`; the later no-credential current diagnostic correctly remains `skipped`. Both bind to 254 source files / 2,761,413 bytes / SHA-256 `8F735F678227EB9CAC96D50EAB2363AB825271193C1653A59CD7880596E02700`. The passed attempt proves models, Node chat, and browser chat all reached canonical `/proxy` with trusted `upstream` HTTP 200, selected `gpt-5-6-pro`, kept the Provider key out of the browser, and captured the exact marker. The validated and manually inspected 758x482 screenshot is 45,680 bytes / SHA-256 `053E8DE57014962FAF7C0921E6876811016E00B0802765E3E9CCF4A3A6D6AF64`. Final cleanup found no ZeroChat processes, QA harnesses, browser profiles, or temporary credential environment.
- Boundary: this closes the current-source browser-origin Provider UI blocker. It does not prove the relay's missing speech, transcription, embedding, moderation, or realtime capabilities, and trusted Provider failures remain release blockers rather than retry candidates.

QA marker: Temporary Worker model discovery retries only exact untrusted ingress HTML 404s.

## 2026-07-30 Asia/Shanghai - Sync Passphrase Draft And Active Runtime Isolation

- Root cause: the controller kept separate draft, committed, and active refs but exposed one React value that changed on every draft keystroke. Auto-sync and automatic pull effects, managed proxy host scheduling, and composer readiness subscribed to that draft while actual work read the still-active ref. An uncommitted draft could therefore trigger old-credential network work and make a proxied composer look ready when generation would still reject it.
- Fix: the visible draft remains available to Settings and the derived access-key preview. Active runtime state is now exposed only as a non-secret availability bit and monotonically changing revision. Composer readiness consumes the active bit; auto-sync and managed host maintenance consume the revision; host scheduling uses a non-secret marker and derives the real key only inside the delayed runner from the active ref. Starting a new draft access-key derivation clears the old preview before the asynchronous digest can complete.
- Evidence: six focused suites failed first on the missing active boundary and then passed 58/58. They cover boolean generation requirements, proxied composer readiness, a draft-only app-chrome regression, active status rotation revisions, secret-free host scheduling, and stale preview clearing. TypeScript and focused ESLint pass.
- Boundary: this is Web/PWA/WebView credential-state correctness. It does not prove disposable live sync, Provider full capability, native target runtimes, trusted MSIX installation, or hosted CI.

QA marker: Sync passphrase drafts never drive active runtime credential effects.

Tab must dismiss the menu and advance to `.chat-sync-strip`; after reopening, Shift+Tab must dismiss it and restore focus to `.provider-model-trigger`. Existing Escape, outside-click, and selection assertions continue afterward, and the browser smoke passes.

QA marker: Provider model menus preserve document focus order when Tab dismisses them.

## 2026-07-30 Asia/Shanghai - Temporary Worker Host-management CORS Readiness

- Root cause: the browser-origin Provider drill considered a temporary Worker ready after only an Origin-bearing GET `/proxy` signature and a no-Origin models-shaped GET `/proxy` signature. The real first-run flow must first preflight PUT `/proxy/hosts`; a Cloudflare edge response of HTTP 403 therefore escaped readiness and failed only after the expensive Chrome workflow started.
- Fix: every readiness round now sends the browser-equivalent OPTIONS request to `/proxy/hosts` without an access-key value. A round passes only for HTTP 200/204 with the exact app Origin, PUT in the allowed methods, and both `content-type` and `x-zerochat-access-key` in the allowed headers. The existing two GET signatures and consecutive-pass requirement remain mandatory.
- Evidence: the focused regression first failed because the production probe consumed only two responses per round and misclassified the observed 403. It now passes 12/12, including three stable request shapes across two consecutive rounds and a fail-closed fixture where both GET signatures pass while every host-management preflight returns 403.
- Boundary: readiness proves only that the deployed Worker exposes the browser request surface required before Provider traffic. It does not prove a successful upstream Provider request or replace relay full-capability, Apple/Linux target runtime, trusted MSIX, or hosted CI evidence.

QA marker: Temporary Worker readiness requires the browser host-management CORS preflight.

## 2026-07-30 Asia/Shanghai - Keyboard Message Menu Invocation Position

- Root cause: keyboard `Context Menu` / `Shift+F10` invocation has no pointer location, and the real Chrome harness models that path with `(0,0)`. The controller treated those values as pointer coordinates, so viewport clamping placed the menu at the page's top-left instead of near the control that opened it.
- Fix: a pure positioning contract now substitutes the invocation target's bounding-box left/bottom only when both pointer coordinates are absent. Mouse right-click and touch/pen long-press coordinates are unchanged, and the existing viewport margin and menu-size bounds still apply. The controller reads layout only for the coordinate-less keyboard path.
- Evidence: the focused regression first failed because the invocation-position function did not exist, then passed 5/5. The real Chrome message interaction smoke now calculates an independent expected anchor and requires the rendered menu position to match within one pixel while retaining copy, long-press, arrow/Home/End navigation, viewport containment, and exact Escape focus restoration.
- Boundary: this is Web/PWA/Windows WebView keyboard-menu evidence. It does not replace Apple/Linux target runtime, trusted MSIX, hosted CI, or Provider full-capability release evidence.

QA marker: Keyboard-invoked message context menus anchor to the invoking control.

- Root cause: an outer command timeout terminated `check:live-provider-smoke` while its `pnpm -> live-provider-smoke-check -> live-provider-ui-smoke --validate-inputs-only` process tree remained alive. Local cleanup enumerated Node processes but classified only Vite and browser runtimes; relative script commands contained neither the workspace's absolute path nor `zerochat`, so the gate incorrectly passed.

Local cleanup now fails with the remaining harness PIDs and prints `NO_ZEROCHAT_QA_HARNESS_PROCESSES` only on a clean path. ## 2026-07-30 Asia/Shanghai - Apple Runtime Permission-independent Window Discovery

- Root cause: exact child-process attribution still queried the app's windows through `System Events` UI scripting. Apple documents that Accessibility access for UI scripting is disabled by default and must be granted manually per controlling app, so a clean hosted macOS runner could fail before capture even when the exact ZeroChat child rendered correctly.
- Fix: a checked-in Swift probe now calls `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` for the current GUI session, filters on the exact child PID, on-screen/non-desktop options, normal layer, positive alpha, and positive bounds, then chooses the largest candidate. The title remains optional. The shell compiles the probe once, removes it through the existing `EXIT` trap, and contains no `osascript` or `System Events` path. Runtime JSON declares `windowDiscovery: coregraphics-owner-pid`, which both local and hosted validators require from the shared contract.
- Evidence: the focused contract suite failed first on the missing probe and metadata contract, then passed all four tests. Repository health's hosted release fixture emits and validates the new semantic field; repository health and completion audit require the probe wiring and reject restoration of Accessibility UI scripting or name-based PID lookup.
- Boundary: the current Windows host cannot compile or execute CoreGraphics code. This hardens the checked-in hosted/target-host harness but does not replace the first real macOS hosted run or iPhone, iPad, macOS visual, interaction, sync, Keychain, and package evidence.

QA marker: Apple runtime smoke discovers the exact child window through CoreGraphics without Accessibility UI scripting.

## 2026-07-30 Asia/Shanghai - Apple Runtime Exact Process Attribution And Cleanup

- Root cause: the macOS runtime smoke launched an app through `open -n` and then selected the first process returned by `pgrep -x`. An existing ZeroChat instance could therefore supply the captured window while the report hashed the newly built app bundle, creating internally inconsistent evidence. Any failure before the old explicit post-screenshot kill also left the launched app running.
- Fix: the script resolves `CFBundleExecutable` inside the current app bundle, starts that exact executable as its own background child, and records `$!` as the only accepted runtime PID. An `EXIT` trap verifies that PID is still one of the shell's running background jobs, then performs bounded TERM/KILL cleanup and `wait` on success and every failure path. Runtime JSON declares `processAttribution: exact-bundle-child-pid` and `cleanupPolicy: bounded-exit-trap`; both local and hosted artifact validators require those shared contract values.
- Evidence: three focused contract tests failed against the prior `open`/`pgrep` and unversioned-metadata implementation and now pass. Git Bash syntax validation passes; repository health's hosted release fixture exercises the new fields, while repository health and completion audit reject restored name-based PID selection, missing exact-bundle launch, missing cleanup trap, downgraded metadata, or missing contract coverage.
- Boundary: this improves Apple runtime evidence attribution and harness cleanup only. macOS/iOS target-host builds, visual interaction, sync, Keychain, package-size QA, and the first hosted CI artifact run remain required.

QA marker: Apple runtime smoke binds evidence to the exact launched bundle process and always cleans it up.

## 2026-07-30 Asia/Shanghai - Exact Worker-hosted Key Mapping And Proxy Roots

- Root cause: deriving a Worker secret environment-variable name from a host collapsed punctuation, so distinct domains could collide and receive the same hosted Provider key. Separately, clients accepted a valid Worker `/proxy` URL but appended another `/proxy`, producing a broken route.
- Fix: the Worker now resolves hosted Provider keys only from the exact `PROVIDER_KEYS` JSON host mapping and ignores legacy host-derived bindings. Web, Android, Apple, Linux, and Windows normalize a terminal `/proxy` or `/proxy/hosts` input to the Worker root while preserving deployment subpaths before constructing requests or `/proxy/hosts` maintenance calls.
- Evidence: the Worker runtime security check sends a collision-domain request with both an exact-map key and a legacy-shaped binding, requires HTTP 401, and proves no upstream request occurs. Focused Web tests cover root normalization, request construction, connectivity host preparation, and host-list management; Android, Apple, and Linux endpoint suites cover the same accepted inputs. This is source and local-contract evidence, not a claim that an external relay has every capability.

QA marker: Worker-hosted Provider keys use exact host mappings and proxy roots normalize endpoint suffixes.

## 2026-07-30 Asia/Shanghai - Browser Smoke Failure Context

- Root cause: `verify-release` captured selected release-artifact failures but omitted Browser smoke. An intermittent end-to-end failure therefore reached the checkpoint only as an exit code, without its assertion or the last Chrome DevTools operation needed to distinguish an application regression from harness timing.
- Fix: Browser smoke now reports only its last CDP operation sequence and method before rethrowing, never request parameters. The verifier captures Browser smoke output and routes it through the shared release-report sanitizer with dynamically supplied sensitive environment values of at least eight characters plus disposable smoke fixture values before writing the checkpoint. Short control flags such as `1` are excluded so they cannot corrupt strict-preflight MSIX run-id linkage; token, URL, and path redaction remains mandatory in the shared sanitizer.
- Evidence: sanitizer unit coverage proves caller-provided ephemeral credentials are removed. The verify-release check-order suite locks the capture allowlist, shared sanitizer wiring, redacted-values handoff, and no-parameter CDP context marker. Repository health and completion audit protect the same contract.
- Boundary: this makes a local browser QA failure actionable without weakening its assertion, timeout, or external release-evidence requirements.

QA marker: Browser smoke failed-run context stays redacted and captured.

## 2026-07-30 Asia/Shanghai - Browser CDP Connection Budget

- Root cause: shared Chrome readiness waited up to 30 seconds, but the WebSocket connection opened by a newly created DevTools target used a separate 10-second default. Under the complete Web release chain, `/json/version` could be ready while the target socket was still opening, which made Axe fail as a transport timeout before its accessibility assertions ran.
- Fix: the shared `DEFAULT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` is now an exported 30-second contract, aligned with Chrome readiness and covered by the CDP unit suite. HTTP requests remain at 10 seconds, ordinary commands at 20 seconds, and heavy Axe/Settings commands retain their explicit bounded 60-second overrides.

- Boundary: this only stabilizes local DevTools transport timing. It does not relax application network timeouts or promote any external release evidence.

QA marker: Browser CDP connection budget matches Chrome readiness.

## 2026-07-30 Asia/Shanghai - Web Current-page Refresh Window

- Root cause: `verify:web-local` correctly places diagnostics immediately after the production build, but its source-bound current-page Web report can only be regenerated later by the required browser/visual current-page QA. A source edit therefore made the bootstrap reject its own pending refresh as an unexpected runtime-artifact blocker and stopped the run before the repair step.
- Fix: the verifier now passes an explicit `--allow-refreshable-web-current-page-stale` flag only with `--write-current-summary --validate-current-sources`. The parser rejects every other mode. The runtime-artifact policy remains fail-closed by default and, in that single window, accepts only the current-page file-count and digest stale bullet prefixes; every other runtime-artifact bullet remains unexpected. The mandatory current-page QA follows, and the ordinary pre-checkpoint diagnostic rewrite audits the renewed evidence without the exception.

QA marker: Web-local diagnostic bootstrap permits only the exact pending current-page source stale pair.

## 2026-07-30 Asia/Shanghai - IndexedDB Abort Failure Causality

- Root cause: synchronous store-operation failures in secret batch mutations, AppData writes/replacements, and local AES-key installation tried to abort their IndexedDB transaction. A synchronous `abort()` failure was either discarded or replaced the primary operation error, and some paths rejected before an otherwise successful abort was confirmed by the transaction event. That left the durable outcome unknowable while exposing only a partial failure chain.
- Fix: `abortIndexedDbTransactionOrReject(...)` is the shared boundary. It preserves the primary error when no transaction exists, waits for `onabort`/`onerror` when `abort()` starts successfully, and otherwise rejects one localized `AggregateError` ordered as operation error then abort error with the abort error as `cause`. Secret storage, AppData write/atomic replacement, and AES-key installation now all use it. All 10 locales tell the user to close and reopen the current ZeroChat tab or window when durable state cannot be known.
- Evidence: three public API red/green regressions force a synchronous store error plus a synchronous abort error for complete secret replacement, atomic AppData replacement, and local key installation. The old code returned only the operation error; each now exposes an ordered aggregate and invokes the abort probe. The focused secret/db/localCrypto suites pass 87/87, with TypeScript, focused ESLint, and i18n completeness also passing.
- Boundary: this closes local IndexedDB failure causality and transaction completion ordering on Web/PWA/WebView. It does not replace trusted-MSIX runtime, Apple/Linux target-host, disposable live-sync, hosted CI, or live-provider capability evidence.

QA marker: IndexedDB abort failures preserve operation and abort causes.

## 2026-07-30 Asia/Shanghai - Credential Transition Compensation Causality

- Root cause: recoverable Provider/full-secret and AppData transitions compensate after a failed Windows Locker stage or failed AppData persistence. When that compensation also failed, the compensation error replaced the primary failure. Conversely, when AppData persistence and the durable-state read used to choose completion or rollback both failed, only the primary persistence error escaped. The encrypted transition journal remained retryable in both cases, but the caller and support evidence lost half of the causal chain.
- Fix: `rethrowAfterCredentialCompensation(...)` rethrows the original error unchanged after successful compensation and otherwise raises one localized `AggregateError` with the primary error first, the compensation error second, and the compensation error as `cause`. A failed durable-state read uses the same ordered aggregate constructor with a distinct localized unknown-state message. Windows Provider/full-secret staging and AppData failure reread/completion/rollback share this boundary. Browser passphrase fail-closed handling also reuses the aggregate constructor; all 10 locales describe complete credential-state restoration and provide separate close-and-reopen guidance when durable state cannot be verified.
- Evidence: three public API regressions failed against the old implementation: the first two returned only `WindowsSecretBridgeError`, while the durable-read case returned only the AppData write error. They now preserve staging-plus-rollback, AppData-write-plus-rollback, and AppData-write-plus-durable-read failures in order, assert that the encrypted transition journal remains, and verify the Locker or canonical IndexedDB secret still reflects the operation that actually committed. The complete secret-storage suite passes 53/53.
- Boundary: this closes local credential failure causality and startup recoverability on Web/PWA/WebView and Windows PasswordVault. It does not replace trusted-MSIX runtime, Apple/Linux target-host, disposable live-sync, hosted CI, or live-provider capability evidence.

QA marker: Credential transition compensation failures preserve primary and rollback causes.

QA marker: Credential transition durable-state read failures remain recoverable and fully causal.

## 2026-07-30 Asia/Shanghai - Browser Sync-passphrase Compensation Failure

- Root cause: complete browser secret replacement and AppData transition staging update the session sync passphrase before their IndexedDB mutation. If that mutation and restoration of the prior passphrase both failed, the restoration error was swallowed and the session could retain a new, uncommitted password over old durable data.
- Fix: both transaction paths now delegate to `rethrowAfterBrowserSyncPassphraseRestore(...)`. A failed restoration first removes the uncommitted session value; if removal fails, it overwrites that value with an empty string. One localized `AggregateError` retains the primary, restoration, removal, and overwrite failures. If the browser refuses every clearing operation, the user is told to close the current ZeroChat tab or window and reopen it because reload preserves sessionStorage.
- Evidence: four red/green fail-closed regressions cover complete secret replacement, AppData transition staging, empty overwrite after failed removal, and the fully blocked path with all four causal errors. The suite proves the persistent tombstone remains empty, and all 10 supported locales carry the close-and-reopen boundary.

QA marker: Browser sync-passphrase compensation failures clear uncommitted session state.

QA marker: Browser sync-passphrase compensation overwrites uncommitted session state when removal fails.

## 2026-07-29 Asia/Shanghai - Linux Sync Secret Snapshot Transaction

- Root cause: sync passphrase and GitHub token writes need one failure boundary across Secret Service and the local snapshot. A successful secret enqueue followed by a rejected snapshot must not leave the secret ahead of committed state.
- Fix: `save_sync_passphrase`, `reset_sync_passphrase`, and `save_github_token` now call the Linux Secret Service set/clear APIs explicitly, retain the prior value in a `SecretValueTransaction`, publish through snapshot compare-and-save, and conditionally roll back the applied value on snapshot rejection or write failure. Idempotent password saves use the normal `save()` path and check its storage error state before reporting success; successful changed-value commits update GTK committed state and enqueue auto-sync.
- Evidence: direct-write rollback tests for the sync passphrase and GitHub token, native parity, Linux rustfmt, and the Linux Node contract suite pass. Windows cannot execute the GTK cargo test because the host lacks Linux `pkg-config` and `libadwaita-1`; Linux target execution remains required.

QA marker: Linux sync secrets and snapshot publish share a CAS rollback transaction.

## 2026-07-29 Asia/Shanghai - Android Async Settings Latest-snapshot Reducers

- Root cause: model catalog refresh, Provider connectivity checks, and Skill file import captured the full `AppSnapshot` at request start. After an I/O await, their success callbacks passed that stale snapshot back through `onSnapshotChange`, so a user edit made during the request could be overwritten by the late result.

QA marker: Android async Settings results reduce against the latest snapshot.

## 2026-07-29 Asia/Shanghai - Clear-cloud Confirmation Sync Drain

- Root cause: clear-cloud checked `syncingRef` only before opening the danger prompt. Auto-sync could start while the prompt was open, and the confirmed clear operation then replaced the runtime abort controller without cancelling or draining the upload that still owned its original signal. That upload could finish after the remote clear and publish the old ciphertext again.
- Fix: after confirmation, clear-cloud checks for newly claimed sync ownership and reuses `cancelSyncRuntime()` to increment the generation, abort the active request, and await `activeRuntimeDrain` before taking exclusive clear-cloud ownership. The clear operation then re-reads the current snapshot and keeps the existing durable-publish boundary.
- Evidence: `syncRuntimeController.test.ts` passes 43/43, including a real confirmation-window auto-sync start that is aborted and drained before `clearRemoteSyncData(...)` runs. No remote clear success is published from the stale upload.

QA marker: Clear-cloud drains auto-sync started during danger confirmation.

## 2026-07-29 Asia/Shanghai - Local Skill Transaction-isolated Content Refs

## 2026-07-29 Asia/Shanghai - Stable Border-box Virtualization Geometry

- Root cause: runtime height caching measured each message with `getBoundingClientRect()` but observed the default ResizeObserver content box. Padding or border changes could alter the measured row geometry without guaranteeing a callback. The smoke also captured its bottom baseline after one top-window visit, so later fallback-to-measured corrections from newly rendered rows could hide the target row's growth. The full verifier reproduced `-463px` and standalone retries reproduced `-223px`; nominal passes still varied from 135.75px to 187px instead of isolating the 240px mutation.
- Fix: the viewport and every rendered message are observed with `{ box: 'border-box' }`, matching the cached geometry. Before mutation, the browser smoke now cycles between top and bottom until their complete virtual-window signatures match for two consecutive cycles. After mutation it aligns the same virtual start, waits for a stable state, and requires spacer growth to equal the directly measured row growth within 2px. The old `dynamicSpacerDelta > 50` assertion is gone.
- Evidence: the focused 13-test suite, TypeScript, ESLint, and script syntax pass. Five independent real-Chrome smokes each converged in three cycles, delivered four target-stage observer callbacks, and reported exactly 240px for both row and spacer growth. The bounded DOM remained at 9 rows at the top, 15 in the middle, and 12-13 at the bottom.
- Visual evidence: the final 1280x820 screenshot is 100,440 bytes / SHA-256 `169317ADD8003F8281759E1740D3D444C4289E82FAFC976BD59FF0364923DB01`. Manual review confirms message bubbles, row actions, scroll boundaries, and the composer remain visible without overlap or clipping.
- Boundary: this repairs Web/PWA/WebView long-conversation geometry and its release proof. It does not replace Provider, sync, native target-host, trusted-package, or hosted release evidence.

## 2026-07-29 Asia/Shanghai - Image Preview Object URL Ownership

- Root cause: `setImageSource(...)` used the rendered `imageSourceUrl` state value as its cleanup owner. Multiple replacements before a state commit could each observe the same stale URL, leaving an intermediate newly created blob URL outside both final state and effect cleanup. Normal replacements also revoked the previous URL once in the callback and again in effect cleanup.
- Fix: `replaceOwnedImageSourcePreviewUrl(...)` creates the next URL before mutation, atomically swaps a dedicated ref owner, and then performs contained cleanup of the previous owner. Creation failure leaves the current owner and visible image unchanged. `releaseOwnedImageSourcePreviewUrl(...)` clears ownership before best-effort unmount cleanup.

Real Chrome instruments native object URL creation/revocation around the existing drop-then-paste flow and records two created URLs, revoke counts `[1, 0]`, and the second URL as the current preview. The formal coverage gate passes without changing thresholds at 195 files / 1,761 tests and 6,609/9,217 covered branches.

## 2026-07-29 Asia/Shanghai - Inpaint Pointer Capture-Loss Recovery

- Root cause: the mask owner was released only by `pointerup` or `pointercancel`, while the controller deliberately contained `setPointerCapture()` failures. When an uncaptured pointer left the canvas and was released outside, the canvas never received the stop event and retained the old pointer id forever. Browser-initiated capture loss had the same ownership leak.
- Fix: `abandonUncapturedMaskPointerStroke(...)` preserves a matching owner only while the canvas still reports capture. A direct canvas `pointerout` and `lostpointercapture` both route through the focused controller; owner mismatches remain inert, and capture-state API failures abandon the stale owner.
- Evidence: 15 focused controller tests cover owner mismatch, retained capture, unavailable capture, and capture-state exceptions. The component test requires both DOM boundary handlers. Real Chrome forces `setPointerCapture()` to fail, paints with one pointer, moves it out without a stop event, and then proves a second pointer acquires ownership: undoing the second stroke preserves the first stroke's painted pixels. TypeScript and focused ESLint pass.
- Boundary: this closes a Web/PWA/WebView inpaint interruption defect. It does not replace Provider image capability, native target-host, trusted package, or release evidence.

## 2026-07-28 Asia/Shanghai - Inpaint Mask Pointer Ownership

- Root cause: the mask controller tracked drawing with one boolean. It accepted secondary-button and non-primary pointers, did not bind moves to the pointer that started the stroke, and let any pointerup/cancel terminate another pointer's stroke. Right click, a second finger, or a second pen could therefore mutate the mask and undo history.
- Fix: a stroke now has one `pointerId` owner. Only an idle primary pointer with `button === 0` can acquire ownership; move/up/cancel events must match that owner. Starting generation, replacing the source image, rebuilding the canvas, or changing generation lifecycle invalidates prior ownership. Owner-only stop/capture release is isolated in `stopOwnedMaskPointerStroke(...)`, so the hook commits one tested ownership transition and capture API failures remain best-effort.
- Evidence: 15 focused image-composer tests cover primary/secondary/non-primary start decisions, existing ownership, move/stop identity, absent capture, successful release, capture API failure, and capture-loss recovery. The real Chrome browser smoke first dispatches a secondary-button primary pointer and a left-button non-primary pointer; both keep painted pixels at zero and leave undo/clear disabled. A valid primary pointer then paints successfully; a forced capture failure followed by `pointerout` releases ownership for the next pointer; stroke undo, clear, clear undo, keyboard cursor movement, and keyboard painting all pass. The formal coverage gate passes without changing `branches: -2611`: 195 files / 1,759 tests and 6,609/9,217 covered branches.
- Boundary: this closes a Web/PWA/WebView inpaint input-integrity defect. It does not replace Provider image capability, native target-host, trusted package, or release evidence.

## 2026-07-28 Asia/Shanghai - Cross-Tab Secret Transition Ownership

- Root cause: `secretMutationTail` serialized only one JavaScript realm. ## 2026-07-18 22:46 Asia/Shanghai - Native Image Generation Cancellation Ownership

- Android root cause: image generation was launched directly from the Compose scope without an owned Job, so Stop only cancelled `chatStreamingJob`; the image request could continue without a Stop state and publish a late attachment.

- Linux fix: image requests now use `AtomicBool + watch` ownership; request execution and retry waits are selected against cancellation, active generation ownership is shared with text, and Retry/Done events are ignored after the message id leaves ownership. `check:linux-fmt`, native parity, repository health, and completion audit passed; Linux target-host build/runtime remains unavailable on this Windows host.
- Scope: this closes Android and Linux native image-request cancellation and late-publication gaps. It does not close Android current runtime refresh, Linux/Apple target runtime, Windows trusted MSIX, hosted native CI, disposable live sync, or live-provider release evidence.

## 2026-07-18 Asia/Shanghai - Apple Image Generation Cancellation Ownership

- Root cause: Apple image generation created an unowned `Task`, so `stopGenerating()` cancelled only the text stream. Image requests could continue after the user changed state and publish a late generated attachment.
- Fix: Apple now stores image generation in `imageGenerationTask`, includes it in the shared `isChatStreaming` generation lock, cancels it from `stopGenerating()`, and converts `CancellationError` into a localized stopped image message with cleared attachments and provider error state. A shared `generationSerial` also prevents an older chat/image task's late `defer` from clearing a newer task's handle or streaming state.
- Evidence: native-parity, repository-health, and completion-audit guards require the task ownership, dual cancellation path, and stopped-image terminal cleanup. Apple target-host compilation and runtime QA remain unavailable on this Windows host.
- Scope: this closes the Apple image-request cancellation and late-publication lifecycle gap. It does not replace Apple target runtime, Linux runtime, trusted MSIX, hosted native CI, disposable live sync, or live-provider release evidence.

QA marker: Apple image generation is owned by a cancellable task and cancellation terminalizes the pending image message.

## 2026-07-18 Asia/Shanghai - Linux Native Provider Stop Wakes Network Reads

- Root cause: Linux Stop previously set only an `AtomicBool`; request establishment and an idle SSE read could still wait for the full 60/90-second provider timeout, leaving the underlying request alive after the user stopped generation.
- Fix: the GTK chat worker now owns a Tokio `watch` cancellation channel. `AiClient.stream` selects cancellation alongside request establishment and every streaming idle read, so Stop wakes the network path immediately while retaining the atomic state for retry/UI decisions.
- Evidence: the async cancellation regression is source-locked, `cargo fmt --check` passes, and the Windows host correctly reports Linux Cargo tests blocked by missing `pkg-config`/`libadwaita-1`; no Linux target runtime evidence is claimed.
- QA marker: Linux native Provider stream cancellation wakes request and idle-read waits.

## 2026-07-18 Asia/Shanghai - Native Provider Terminal Publication Rechecks Cancellation

- Root cause: Apple and Android checked cancellation during the Provider request, but had no final cancellation arbitration between a returned Provider result and the synchronous local publication of a `done` text or generated-image message. A Stop or lifecycle cancellation winning in that gap could be overwritten by stale success.
- Fix: Apple now calls `Task.checkCancellation()` before both chat and image terminal publication; Android calls `currentCoroutineContext().ensureActive()` before text and image terminal state construction. Linux removes active stream ownership before Stop terminalization, and Web already arbitrates the final response signal before publishing.
- Evidence: native-parity, repository-health, and completion-audit source guards require the post-return checks. Android JVM validation must be refreshed for the current source; Apple/Linux target-host builds remain unavailable on this Windows host.
- QA marker: Native Provider terminal publication rechecks cancellation after Provider return.

## 2026-07-18 Asia/Shanghai - Gist Raw URLs Stay Inside GitHub Gist

- Root cause: truncated GitHub Gist file metadata supplied `raw_url`, and Web, Android, Apple, and Linux previously used that URL directly while attaching the GitHub Bearer token. A malicious or corrupted metadata response could therefore redirect the token-bearing request to an arbitrary HTTPS host.
- All four clients now require HTTPS, the exact `gist.githubusercontent.com` host, no user info, no password, no explicit port, and a non-root path before issuing the raw-file request. Web and Android regressions prove an attacker URL is rejected after only the metadata request; Apple and Linux have unit-level URL validation coverage in their native test sources.
- `vitest` Gist sync 15/15, Android `check:android-unit`, `tsc --noEmit`, `check:native-parity`, `check:repo`, `check:completion-audit`, and Linux `cargo fmt --check` pass. Linux Cargo tests remain target-host blocked on Windows by missing `pkg-config`/`libadwaita-1`; Apple/Linux runtime evidence is not claimed.
- QA marker: Native and Web Gist raw-file requests validate the GitHub Gist host before attaching credentials.

## 2026-07-18 Asia/Shanghai - Web Sync Rejects Automatic Redirects

- Root cause: Android, Apple, Linux, and Windows credential-bearing transports already rejected automatic 30x responses, but the Web shared `fetchSync` primitive still inherited the browser default `redirect: "follow"`. Cross-origin browser redirects usually strip `Authorization`, but the encrypted sync request could still be sent to an unverified target and the attacker-controlled response would enter sync parsing.
- Fix: every Web Cloudflare/Gist request now passes through `fetchSync`, which overrides caller input with `redirect: 'error'`; the focused `syncHttpBody.test.ts` regression proves a caller-provided `redirect: 'follow'` cannot reopen automatic redirects.
- Evidence: focused Web sync transport tests, TypeScript, repository health, completion audit, and the full local release gate passed after the change. The full gate still stops only at the external Windows trusted MSIX host AppX lock-holder blocker; no external platform release evidence is claimed.
- QA marker: Web sync fetches reject automatic redirects before sending credential-bearing requests.

- Fix: the shared Provider request primitive and managed proxy-host update both force `redirect: 'error'` after caller options, so request callers cannot reopen automatic redirects. Focused chat and providerProxyHosts regressions lock the Provider credential and Worker access-key boundaries.

## 2026-07-18 Asia/Shanghai - Web Provider SSE DONE Readers Are Released

- Root cause: OpenAI-compatible and OpenAI Responses stream readers returned immediately after `[DONE]` without cancelling unread tail bytes or releasing the `ReadableStreamDefaultReader` lock. Repeated long-lived generations could retain the response stream and reduce connection reuse.
- Fix: early DONE paths now best-effort cancel the reader, while normal EOF and all DONE/exception exits release the reader lock. The focused chat regression covers both protocols that stop on `[DONE]`; TypeScript, ESLint, and `chat.test.ts` 34/34 pass.
- This closes a Web/PWA/WebView stream-lifecycle defect only. It does not claim live-provider full capability, browser-origin Worker, native target runtime, trusted MSIX, hosted CI, or disposable live-sync release evidence.

## 2026-07-18 Asia/Shanghai - Windows Native Provider Readers Are Closed

- Root cause: Windows `AiClient.cpp` only closed bounded `DataReader` instances on response-byte overflow. `[DONE]`, normal EOF, and read/parse exceptions otherwise relied on object destruction, which can delay release of the underlying provider response stream during repeated generations or capability calls.
- Fix: bounded ordinary responses and SSE responses now use the exception-safe `CloseProviderDataReader` helper on normal completion, early `[DONE]`, and exceptional exits. The Windows Node native contract suite covers both bounded body and SSE cleanup paths with 2/2 passing tests.
- This closes a Windows native Provider connection-lifecycle defect only. It does not claim live-provider full capability, browser-origin Worker, Apple/Linux target runtime, trusted MSIX, hosted-CI, or disposable live-sync release evidence.
- QA marker: Windows native Provider DataReaders close on every bounded response exit.

## 2026-07-18 Asia/Shanghai - Android Native Provider SSE Readers Are Closed

- Root cause: Android `BoundedAiProviderSseLineReader` previously had no explicit close operation. When `AiClient.stream` stopped after `[DONE]`, reached EOF, or raised while reading/parsing, cleanup depended on the outer Ktor statement lifecycle rather than the reader's actual ownership boundary.
- Fix: the reader now exposes an idempotent `close()` that marks it exhausted and cancels the underlying `ByteReadChannel`; `AiClient.stream` calls it from `finally`, covering early DONE, normal EOF, and exceptional exits. The regression asserts that repeated close calls cancel an observable response channel.
- Evidence: Android `check:android-unit` rebuilt production Kotlin and passed all 308/308 JVM tests. Repository-health and completion-audit guards require the source, cleanup test, and current documentation marker. This closes an Android native Provider stream-lifecycle defect only; Apple/Linux target runtime, trusted MSIX, hosted CI, disposable live sync, and live-provider release evidence remain external blockers.
- QA marker: Android native Provider SSE readers cancel response channels on DONE, EOF, and exceptional exits.

## 2026-07-15 Asia/Shanghai - Cross-platform Incremental Upload Cancellation

Incremental upload cancellation bypasses rollback across Web, Android, and Apple.

- Root cause: Web reused an already-aborted signal for rollback DELETE requests, so cleanup rejection could replace the original `AbortError`. Apple treated `CancellationError` as an ordinary upload failure and serially attempted remote deletes before returning cancellation.
- Web now rethrows immediately when the caller signal is aborted or the upload reports `AbortError`. Ordinary publish/write failures still use the existing release-blocking rollback and cleanup-failure reporting.
- A deterministic Web test blocks `PUT /sync/head` until source abort, then proves no incremental-object DELETE is issued and `AbortError` remains the rejection. The focused Cloudflare suite passed 13/13; TypeScript and focused ESLint passed.
- Apple now routes upload writes through `runWithIncrementalRollbackOnFailure`. `CancellationError` bypasses rollback, while an ordinary error runs rollback once and remains the thrown error. Two async SwiftPM tests lock those semantics; this Windows host has no Swift toolchain, so target execution remains part of the macOS prerequisite pass.
- Android already has the same tested boundary. Linux task cancellation drops the upload future before its ordinary-error branch. Windows currently uses the snapshot protocol and has no incremental upload catch to align.
- Scope: this closes cancellation delay and error replacement. It does not provide orphan-object garbage collection after cancellation/crash and does not replace Apple/Linux target runtime, Windows incremental protocol, disposable live-sync, trusted MSIX, hosted CI, or live-provider full-capability evidence.

## 2026-07-15 Asia/Shanghai - Sync Response Deadline And Runtime Cancellation

Sync response bodies remain inside timeout and cancellation ownership.

- Root cause: Web `fetchSync(...)` returned a `Response` as soon as headers arrived, so its 60-second signal and source listener were disposed before Cloudflare/Gist JSON, error, snapshot, or incremental bodies were consumed. A reader that ignored fetch abort could hang forever. Oversize paths also awaited cleanup, allowing `cancel()` itself to hang.
- `fetchSync<T>(..., consumeResponse)` now owns fetch, status handling, bounded body consumption, final cancellation arbitration, unconsumed-body cleanup, and timeout disposal as one lifecycle. Timeout and caller cancellation remain distinct; a caller abort is never mislabeled as timeout.
- `readSyncResponseText(...)`, JSON parsing, and error extraction receive the composed signal. Pending reads reject immediately on abort even when `reader.read()` never settles. Body/reader cancellation and lock release are best-effort and cannot replace timeout, abort, size, decoder, or HTTP failures.
- Root cause at runtime: `cancelSyncRuntime()` invalidated generation ownership but did not abort the active transport, so destructive data replacement could still wait for the full network deadline before rollback/finally drained.
- Active sync and clear-cloud runs now own an AbortController. `SyncContext.signal` reaches every Gist and Cloudflare request, including snapshot, bulk clear, incremental head/object/manifest, conversation/Skill chunk materialization, ordinary-failure rollback, and stale-object cleanup. Cancellation aborts first, incremental upload bypasses rollback on `AbortError`, and runtime still awaits the operation's final drain before durable replacement.
- Controlled coverage includes non-settling reads, non-settling and throwing cleanup, headers timeout, stream TimeoutError, pre-aborted and active source cancellation, late consumer success, Gist/Cloudflare request propagation, a transport that rejects on runtime abort, and a service that ignores abort but loses final generation ownership.

## 2026-07-14 Asia/Shanghai - Unexpected Assistant Runner Durable Fallback

Direct text, image, and rerun runner rejects terminalize durably without overwriting settled results.

Sync runtime persists local baselines before remote requests.

## 2026-07-13 Asia/Shanghai - Cross-Platform Sync Request Timeouts

Root cause: Windows native sync already shared one 60-second deadline across response headers
and bounded body reads, but Web fetches, Android's sync Ktor client, Apple's resource transfer,

that dripped bytes indefinitely could therefore hold manual sync, auto-sync, clear-cloud, and
later state publication for an unbounded period.

`AbortSignal.timeout(60_000)` remains active through bounded response-stream completion and maps
header/body aborts to a client-owned actionable timeout. Android installs Ktor `HttpTimeout` on
the shared sync client with 60,000 ms request, connect, and socket budgets. Apple clones the
injected URLSession configuration and caps both `timeoutIntervalForRequest` and
`timeoutIntervalForResource` at 60 seconds. Linux sets both reqwest connect and total request
timeouts to 60 seconds. Windows keeps its existing single deadline across headers and body reads.

Evidence: focused Web sync tests passed 3 files / 23 tests, including fetch-signal and
response-stream timeout classification. Android's full `testDebugUnitTest` passed and the new
MockEngine test proves a delayed transport throws `HttpRequestTimeoutException`. Linux rustfmt
passed, and the current Windows Release x64 build compiled the existing 60-second streaming
deadline with zero warnings and errors. Native-parity, repository-health, and completion-audit
guards cover all five transport implementations, the focused tests, and this marker.

QA marker: Sync HTTP requests stay bounded to one 60-second transport deadline across Web and native clients.

Residual scope: Apple and Linux still require target-host timeout/runtime probes. Disposable
Worker/Gist runs must prove real cancellation and cleanup, and the current trusted MSIX release
pass remains pending after the UAC elevation request was cancelled. These source/unit boundaries
do not replace hosted CI, signing, package-install, or remote-service SLA evidence.

## 2026-07-13 Asia/Shanghai - Cross-Platform Sync Body Limits

Root cause: Web, Android, Apple, Linux, and Windows sync clients could fully buffer a
remote snapshot, incremental object/head, Gist response, or error body before validating
its size. A `Content-Length` check alone would still permit a chunked or lengthless response
to cross the intended memory boundary. Outbound ciphertext also lacked one uniform preflight
before publication.

incremental objects and aggregate Gist responses, and 16,384 bytes for incremental heads and
client error bodies. Web `ReadableStream`, Android Ktor channels, Apple `URLSession.AsyncBytes`,
Linux reqwest streams, and Windows WinRT input streams now check declared length, count actual
bytes incrementally, and cancel or close immediately on overflow. JSON decoding happens only
after a bounded UTF-8 body completes. Snapshot/object/head uploads are byte-checked before the
request starts. The Worker/OpenAPI contract carries the same snapshot/object/head/error
budgets, including the new incremental-head PUT 413 boundary.

Evidence: focused Web sync transport tests passed 3 files / 21 tests, including declared-length
rejection, chunked-stream cancellation, UTF-8 byte accounting, bounded JSON parsing, and error
redaction. Android `testDebugUnitTest` rebuilt production Kotlin and passed the full JVM suite,
including a chunked snapshot response that proves the Ktor channel is cancelled immediately.
Windows Release x64 compiled with the shared deadline plus 8 KiB bounded reads; Linux rustfmt
and the Worker security check passed. Native-parity, repository-health, and completion-audit
guards lock the constants, transport primitives, call sites, forbidden unbounded readers, and
this marker.

QA marker: Sync transports enforce declared and streamed body limits before parsing or publishing data.

Residual scope: Apple and Linux still require target-host compile/runtime probes. Disposable
live Worker/Gist runs must also exercise real oversized declared and chunked responses before
release completion; these source and unit boundaries do not replace that evidence.

stream read. Each watchdog cancels only an operation still in `Started` state; cancellation
maps to a stable local timeout error, and stack unwinding releases the RAII sync lease.

cancellation, header-only completion mode, bounded stream acquisition/read helpers, all five

does not prove Worker availability, disposable live-sync success, or target-host release
evidence.

## 2026-07-13 Asia/Shanghai - Windows Native Sync Envelope Validation

positive JSON-safe integers. Base64 must round-trip canonically, salt and IV are fixed at 16
and 12 bytes, AAD must equal the encoded `zerochat:vault:v1:<updatedAt>` value, and payloads
must contain more than the 16-byte GCM authentication tag. Local JSON is validated and
serialized before any HTTP request; a remote callback is reachable only after validation.

require the strict shape reader, allocation-free canonical base64 validator, timestamp-bound AAD check, shared
validator, and pre-network local serialization. The current Windows Release x64 build and
WebView runtime smoke validate the compiled boundary.

replace incremental sync, disposable live-sync, trusted MSIX, or external target-host proof.

## 2026-07-13 Asia/Shanghai - Windows Native Persistence Missing/Error Separation

overwritten. `SecretStore` similarly used `PasswordVault::Retrieve` plus catch-all blocks,

completion, then publishes with `MoveAndReplaceAsync`; if the main file is missing after an
interruption, a valid completed temp snapshot is verified and renamed before publication.

resource/account before reading or removing; absence returns an empty value, while Vault
enumeration, password retrieval, deletion, and writes still fail visibly. A disposable
C++/WinRT probe confirmed that adding the same resource/account again atomically stores the
new password, so non-empty updates now call `Add` directly; only explicit clearing removes
the previous credential. Probe cleanup left zero test credentials.

Evidence: Windows shell, repository-health, and completion-audit guards require the
non-throwing presence queries and reject reintroduced `catch (...)` blocks in either
persistence source. The Windows native build and shell checks compile and validate these
boundaries in the current workspace.

QA marker: Windows native persistence distinguishes absent data from storage failure.

QA marker: Windows native snapshot saves publish only complete temporary files.

QA marker: Windows PasswordVault updates never delete the previous value before replacement.

blank snapshot and overwrite the original on the next save. Windows `UserSkillChunk` also
lacked the shared v1 `contentRef` and `contentPreview` fields used by Web, Android, Apple,
and Linux, so a valid ref-only Skill chunk lost data during a Windows round trip.

nulls, and uses strict scalar/object/array readers. Numbers must be non-negative safe JSON
integers; malformed array elements, unknown provider/message enums, invalid ranges, and
non-canonical model values fail with one data-free format error. The decoded model is
validated again, and serialization refuses an invalid in-memory model before touching the
temp file. Windows Skill chunks now preserve `contentRef` and `contentPreview`; ref-only
chunks omit empty inline `content` when serialized.

Evidence: the Windows Release x64 C++/WinRT build passed with zero warnings and zero errors.
Windows shell, native-parity, repository-health, and completion-audit guards require strict
shape/model validation, reject the old invalid-JSON `return {}` path, and require Skill ref
fields across all native model contracts.

QA marker: Windows native snapshots reject non-canonical data before load or save.

QA marker: Windows native Skill chunks preserve content references and previews.

Residual scope: this is native codec integrity and schema-parity evidence, not trusted MSIX

## 2026-07-13 Asia/Shanghai - Release Report Lock PID Reuse Recovery

Root cause: the release-report lock treated a PID as owner identity. After an interrupted

contention, the lock queries OS process details and rejects an owner when the PID belongs
to a different process generation or command. Legacy owners also use purpose-to-entrypoint
matching, so the observed stale lock recovered automatically without manual deletion.

reentry, dead-owner cleanup, reused-PID cleanup with the correct script name but a different
start time, and final lock cleanup. A real interrupted `release-diagnostics-refresh` lock
whose PID had been reused by Edge was automatically removed, after which the complete
sanitized diagnostic refresh passed.

QA marker: Release report locks reject reused PIDs by process identity.

Residual scope: this hardens release evidence writer concurrency. It does not turn any
diagnostic into release evidence or close target-host/external-service blockers.

## 2026-07-12 Asia/Shanghai - Android Canonical Sync Vault Decoder

Root cause: Android encrypted-backup import checked only `data.version`, while backup,
Cloudflare, and Gist decryption all relied on Kotlin serialization defaults. Missing
current fields, unknown fields, explicit nulls, or invalid nested state could therefore
cross different trust boundaries for the same `SyncVault` wire format.

Fix: `CryptoEngine.decryptVault(...)` now routes every decrypted snapshot through one
structured canonical decoder before returning data to any caller. It validates required
and allowed keys for the vault, snapshot, secrets, Providers, conversations/messages/
attachments, Skills/chunks, sync, and preferences, then applies semantic value checks.
The backup-only version check is removed and format failures retain localized UI copy.
Android Provider data now also preserves speech, transcription, embedding, moderation,
and realtime model selections during cross-platform vault round trips.

Guard coverage: Android JVM `testDebugUnitTest` passed 29 test classes / 204 tests. The
focused suite accepts a complete vault, rejects missing current fields, unknown fields,
and an invalid nested message status, and proves advanced capability model fields survive
decode. Repository and completion audits prevent the shallow backup check from returning.

QA marker: Android backup and remote sync reuse one canonical vault decoder before state mutation.

## 2026-07-12 Asia/Shanghai - Canonical Vault Shape For Backup Import

Root cause: remote snapshot sync validated the complete decrypted `SyncVault`, while
local encrypted-backup import checked only `data.version` and whether conversations was
an array. The same wire format therefore had two trust boundaries, allowing malformed
Provider, Skill, preferences, sync, attachment, or secret shapes to reach later import
code or surface raw technical failures.

Fix: after authenticated envelope decryption, backup import uses the existing cached
`loadSyncService()` boundary and its canonical `isSyncVaultShape(...)` validator. A bad
vault reports the localized format-invalid notice before generation pause, sync cancel,
local-save draining, external Skill persistence, Provider secret replacement, or visible
AppData publication. The former shallow check and optional secrets fallback are gone.

Guard coverage: the focused test decrypts a vault containing only version and an empty
conversations array, then proves canonical validation rejects it without sanitization,
runtime ownership changes, Skill writes, secret application, or AppData publication.
The production bundle reuses the existing sync lazy entry and remains under the fixed
300 KiB total-static gate.

QA marker: Backup import reuses the canonical sync vault shape before runtime mutation.

## 2026-07-12 Asia/Shanghai - Complete Encrypted Envelope Shape Guards

Root cause: `isEncryptedSnapshot(...)` claimed a complete snapshot after checking only
kind/version, and the object guard added only `objectType`. Malformed JSON missing
timestamps, crypto fields, payload, or compression therefore passed the type boundary
and could throw a raw property-access `TypeError` before normal envelope validation.

Fix: both guards now require numeric top-level timestamps, a string payload, and the
complete cipher/kdf/iterations/salt/iv/aad structure. Encrypted objects also require a
string object type and supported structural compression tag (`gzip` or `none`). Existing
semantic checks still own safe timestamps, exact algorithms/KDF iterations, base64
decoding, AAD binding, payload length, and authenticated decryption.

Guard coverage: focused tests accept complete snapshot/object fixtures and reject
missing crypto, non-string payload/object type, unsupported compression, and a
non-numeric timestamp before any decryption path runs.

QA marker: Encrypted envelope guards require complete structural fields before decryption.

## 2026-07-12 Asia/Shanghai - Atomic Scoped Provider Secret Cleanup

Root cause: predicate-based Provider secret cleanup first enumerated IndexedDB keys in
a readonly transaction, then opened one readwrite transaction per matching record. A
failure in the middle could leave provider/proxy cleanup partially committed and made
every retry perform unnecessary database reopen work.

Fix: `deleteSecretsMatchingNow(...)` now opens one readwrite transaction, enumerates
keys, and queues every matching delete while that transaction is active. Full Provider
cleanup and id-scoped cleanup share this boundary; unrelated records remain untouched,
and legacy localStorage cleanup runs only after the IndexedDB transaction commits.

Guard coverage: the focused storage test supplies target provider, target proxy, and
unrelated Provider records, then proves exactly one readwrite transaction performs both
target deletes and leaves the unrelated key alone.

QA marker: Scoped Provider secret cleanup uses one IndexedDB transaction.

## 2026-07-12 Asia/Shanghai - Exact Provider Secret Id Semantics

Root cause: scoped secret cleanup parsed `provider:<id>` and `proxy:<id>` with
`split(':')`, so an id containing a colon compared only its first segment and left
orphan secrets behind. Secret loading also assigned dynamic ids into a plain empty
object, where reserved names such as `__proto__` do not reliably become own key-map
properties.

Fix: cleanup now recognizes each fixed namespace prefix and compares the complete
remaining id string. Secret loading resolves `[providerId, value]` pairs and builds
the map with `Object.fromEntries(...)`, which creates own data properties for reserved
names without invoking the legacy prototype setter.

Guard coverage: focused storage tests migrate and return a `__proto__` Provider key as
an own property, and prove one colon-containing id removes both its provider and proxy
legacy records. Repository/completion audits reject delimiter splitting and require the
pair-based key-map construction plus both tests.

QA marker: Provider secret ids remain exact across storage maps and scoped cleanup.

## 2026-07-12 Asia/Shanghai - Atomic Provider Secret Snapshot Storage

Root cause: complete Provider secret replacement was serialized at the controller
level but still used one IndexedDB transaction per key write and per stale-record
delete. A mid-commit failure triggered another sequence of compensating writes; if
that recovery also failed, the secret store could retain a mixed old/new snapshot.

Fix: `replaceProviderSecretSnapshot(...)` encrypts every non-empty next Provider key
before opening storage, then uses one `zerochat-secrets/records` readwrite transaction
to enumerate and delete all existing provider/proxy records and put the complete next
Provider snapshot. Other secrets remain untouched. Sync/import snapshot ownership stays
serialized, but the controller now calls one atomic storage API instead of replaying
individual keys and stale-id cleanup operations.

Guard coverage: `src/storage/__tests__/secrets.test.ts` proves old provider/proxy
records are deleted and the complete non-empty next snapshot is written under one
readwrite transaction while the GitHub token is retained. Sync runtime tests prove an
atomic write failure leaves visible keys unchanged, complete snapshots cannot
interleave, rollback merging preserves later edits, and orphan cleanup failure occurs
before snapshot publication.

QA marker: Provider secret snapshots replace IndexedDB records atomically.

## 2026-07-12 Asia/Shanghai - Remote Sync Provider Secret Snapshot Commit

snapshot write failed, current AppData stayed visible while one of its existing

pruned complete snapshot; otherwise sanitized Provider ids are filtered from the
current snapshot. `applySyncedSecrets(...)` commits that snapshot through the atomic
replacement boundary and is the final awaited operation before AppData publication.

Guard coverage: the focused failure test forces orphan sanitized-secret cleanup to
reject before replacement, then proves runtime keys remain unchanged, remote AppData
is not published, and unpublished isolated Skill refs are reclaimed. Active removed
Provider records are removed inside the complete atomic replacement transaction.

QA marker: Remote sync commits one rollback-safe Provider secret snapshot before AppData publish.

## 2026-07-12 Asia/Shanghai - External Skill Snapshot Storage Isolation

Root cause: backup import and cloud-sync readback reused snapshot-provided Skill

with matching Skill/chunk ids could overwrite currently visible Skill content before

only inline Skill content to newly allocated, controlled `skill-chunk:external:*`

sync, and local-save ownership before writing these isolated chunks. Failed unpublished
imports/syncs delete only the new refs; local Skill editing retains stable refs.

Guard coverage: the IndexedDB test passes a malicious `contentRef: "app"` and proves
the existing AppData key is untouched. Focused settings/sync tests and repository plus
completion audits require the dedicated external persistence entry point and import
ownership order.

QA marker: External Skill snapshots never reuse local document keys.

## 2026-07-12 Asia/Shanghai - Atomic Local Reset Storage

Root cause: AppData and Skill chunks share one IndexedDB `documents` store but

whose Skill refs had already been deleted. Full secret wipe also deleted records

committed produced a broken rollback boundary.

`store.clear()` transaction. The 2026-07-14 upgrade now encrypts fresh AppData first,

canonical transaction. A later 2026-07-14 cross-store correction moved secret wipe

secret snapshot, while secret failure leaves documents and runtime untouched.

transaction and that a failed write aborts it. Settings tests prove secret failure

QA marker: Full secret wipe clears its IndexedDB store atomically.

## 2026-07-12 Asia/Shanghai - Data Replacement Generation Drain

Root cause: aborting a provider request did not mean its async generation task had
exited. A stale catch/finally path could run after reset or backup import published
new AppData, and matching conversation/message IDs could let the old stream mutate
the imported snapshot. Import also failed to cancel sync or drain local saves, while
its rollback baseline was captured before long decrypt and pause boundaries.

Fix: generation now has one explicit runtime gate. Data replacement pauses admission,
aborts active generation and speech, waits for the admitted task to settle, then
cancels sync, captures the final previous snapshot, and drains local persistence
before reset/import publication. Failed import/reset immediately requeues that final
snapshot; every path releases the generation gate.

Guard coverage: focused tests prove pause blocks new work and waits for active task
settlement. Settings tests prove generation pause precedes sync/local-save takeover.
Real Chromium smoke holds both the exact AppData AES-GCM save and a provider request
that has received abort but has not rejected. Releasing persistence alone keeps the
Settings dialog inert/busy without success; reset commits only after generation exits,
and reload proves the old conversation cannot return.

QA marker: Data replacement waits for generation, sync, and local-save ownership.
QA marker: Backup import captures rollback state after runtime pause.

## 2026-07-12 Asia/Shanghai - Local Reset Persistence Drain

Root cause: local reset cleared IndexedDB, Skill chunks, and secrets without
cancelling the debounced local-save queue, waiting for an encrypted write already
in flight, or invalidating active and queued sync work. An old AppData snapshot or
remote result could therefore write back after the reset and resurrect user data.

its notice reporter identity changed with the active Settings tab, so an Appearance

ownership. `discardPendingLocalSaves()` rejects and clears timers and queued snapshots,
waits for the active write, then restores the queue. Sync runtime cancellation
invalidates the active generation and clears scheduled, active, and pending work.
The hook constructs one queue and updates its reporter and save implementation in
place, preserving ownership across notice-target changes.
Confirmed reset switches `dataRef` to a fresh local snapshot, cancels sync, drains
persistence, then clears storage. Cleanup failure restores and immediately persists
the previous snapshot; success publishes and immediately persists the fresh snapshot.

Guard coverage: deferred queue and reset tests prove storage clearing waits for the
active save and stale queued snapshots never run. Sync tests prove a cancelled remote
completion cannot publish data or drain pending work. Real Chromium smoke switches
from Appearance to Data, holds the exact `app-data` AES-GCM call by AAD, verifies the
whole Settings surface remains inert/busy without early success, releases the write,
then reloads and proves the fresh first-run snapshot survives.

QA marker: Local reset drains stale persistence and sync ownership before clearing storage.
QA marker: Local save queue ownership survives notice-target changes.

## 2026-07-11 Asia/Shanghai - Serialized Local Secret Mutations

Root cause: secret writes encrypted before opening their IndexedDB readwrite
transaction. A slower older encryption could therefore create its transaction
after a newer edit and overwrite the persisted Provider key or GitHub token;
controller-level draft guards only protected UI completion state. Secret cleanup
could race the same pre-transaction window.

Fix: one failure-recovering storage tail serializes every secret set,
Provider-scoped delete, Provider clear, and full wipe. Each caller still receives
its own success or failure, while the next mutation begins only after settlement.

Guard coverage: a controlled IndexedDB test holds the first transaction open,
starts a newer Provider key write, proves no second transaction exists, then
releases both and verifies invocation-order execution.

Additional controlled tests prove Provider cleanup waits behind a pending write
and a rejected mutation does not prevent the next queued mutation from running.

QA marker: Secret mutations stay serialized across encryption and cleanup.

## 2026-07-11 Asia/Shanghai - Provider Capability Result Handoff Ownership

Root cause: a capability helper could validate its controller and resolve, then
lifecycle cleanup could run in the microtask before the caller displayed or
aggregated that result. Abort rejection could also become an ordinary failed
capability result before the caller observed stale ownership.

Fix: capability helpers verify ownership before converting failures, and every
awaited single/full capability result is verified again immediately before its
show or results push. A stale finalizer cannot clear a replacement operation.

Guard coverage: a controlled test resolves the capability helper, queues cleanup
ahead of the caller continuation, and proves no stale notice, UI cleanup, or
replacement-operation overwrite occurs.

QA marker: Provider capability result handoff rechecks lifecycle ownership.

## 2026-07-11 Asia/Shanghai - Adaptive Indexed PWA Icon Encoding

Root cause: the public install PNGs and favicon used a bounded indexed palette,
but forcing 4-bit packed rows did not guarantee the smallest final zlib stream.
For the current brand pixels, 8-bit byte rows compress repeated indexes better.

Fix: the generator compacts each image palette to colors actually used, builds
both 4-bit packed and 8-bit byte scanlines, deflates both at the same level, and
emits the shorter IDAT with the matching IHDR bit depth. Dimensions, alpha, and
rendered pixels remain unchanged.

Guard coverage: repository and completion audits require palette compaction,
both indexed row candidates, compressed-size selection, adaptive IHDR output,
and the shared indexed favicon path.

QA marker: Indexed PWA icons choose the smaller lossless row encoding.

## 2026-07-11 Asia/Shanghai - Provider Check Lifecycle Ownership

Root cause: Provider connectivity, capability, selected-model, and model-refresh
operations shared only a busy ref and unconditionally cleared it in finally.
Disposal or a late lazy-chunk resolution could therefore publish stale models,
results, notices, or clear a newer operation.

Fix: each request module run uses one top-level AbortController as both request
signal and ownership token, then registers its cancel callback on the shared
lifecycle ref. Hook cleanup marks that ref disposed and calls cancel. A lazy
module resolving afterward sees the disposed ref before any network work.
Every important await checks controller ownership; stale runs exit silently and
only the current controller finalizes UI state.

Guard coverage: focused deferred tests prove cleanup aborts the first model-list
signal, its late result cannot publish or clear a newer run, and loaded-module
cleanup reaches the request cancellation boundary.

QA marker: Provider connectivity lifecycle cleanup aborts stale checks.

Residual scope: this hardens Web/PWA/WebView Provider checks. It does not replace
browser-origin provider success, full-capability release evidence, native target
runtime, trusted MSIX, hosted CI, or disposable live-sync evidence.

Root cause: the Service Worker cached both the registration scope URL and

Fix: App Shell install, current-shell discovery, and offline navigation fallback

Guard coverage: repository and completion audits reject a scope-URL cache

QA marker: PWA shell cache uses one canonical index response.

## 2026-07-11 Asia/Shanghai - First-Run Completion Ownership

Root cause: `finishGuide(...)` trusted a render-captured success boolean. Two
clicks before the shared store rerender could both start Provider validation,
save setup, and schedule sync. A completion waiting on its success-close delay
could also close a guide that the user had closed and reopened meanwhile.

Fix: the focused controller now owns one app-level active token. Completion
claims a unique opaque token before its first await and checks ownership after
Provider validation and the success delay. `closeGuide()` and hook disposal
cancel that token, so stale work cannot save, publish success, or close a later
guide session.

Guard coverage: controlled Promise tests prove duplicate completion runs one
validation and one commit, a Provider result after close has no side effects,
and a stale success delay cannot close a reopened guide. Repository and
completion guards lock the root wiring, synchronous claim, navigation cancel,
async ownership checks, and test names.

QA marker: First-run guide completion owns a cancellable run token.

## 2026-07-11 Asia/Shanghai - Markdown Worker Timeout Recovery

Root cause: a timed-out Markdown render removed only its own pending request.
The stalled singleton worker stayed alive, so every later message reused it and
waited another eight seconds; concurrent pending renders timed out one by one.

Fix: `failMarkdownWorker(...)` now owns worker errors, timeouts, and synchronous
request postMessage failures. One timeout
clears all pending timers, rejects every concurrent render into the plain-text
fallback, contains worker termination failure, and resets the singleton. The
next render creates a fresh worker and can return rich Markdown normally.

Guard coverage: a controlled fake-timer test starts two concurrent stalled
renders, proves one timeout settles both without residual timers, and proves the
next render uses a second worker successfully. The postMessage failure test also
proves immediate fallback terminates the failed worker and the next render
recovers through a fresh worker. The focused file passes 4 tests;
full coverage passes 138 files / 1084 tests at 393/393 statements, 373/373
branches, 124/124 functions, and 382/382 lines. TypeScript, ESLint, production
build, and bundle checks pass; the lazy client is 0.68 KiB gzip and total
static output is 299.88 KiB.

QA markers: Markdown worker timeouts reset the worker before retry.
Markdown worker postMessage failures reset the worker before retry.

Residual scope: this hardens Web/PWA/WebView Markdown failure recovery. It does
not replace rich Markdown visual evidence, native target runtime QA, trusted
MSIX, hosted CI, disposable live-sync, or live-provider evidence.

Root cause: the online-state effect deferred reconnect replay with an

## 2026-07-11 Asia/Shanghai - Offline Replay Trigger Scope

Root cause: the data-load replay effect also depended on `data.updatedAt`, so
every streaming token, stopped-state commit, title edit, or settings write
scheduled another online queue flush. A user cancellation could therefore
persist its stopped state and immediately trigger a new replay run.

Initial loaded data still gets one replay attempt, while the independent browser
online listener still owns reconnect replay. Ordinary AppData writes no longer

generation owner or an already-running replay.

dependency list and reject the old `data.updatedAt` dependency. The full 138

## 2026-07-11 Asia/Shanghai - Offline Replay Pre-Credential Cancellation

Root cause: reconnect replay entered the visible sending lifecycle before it
had an abort controller, then awaited proxy access-key derivation and mutated
the queued assistant before cancellation became reachable. Cancelling a
streaming item also let the drain loop continue into the next queued turn, and
unconditional cleanup could clear a newer generation controller.

Fix: replay first defers when another generation already owns the shared abort
ref. Each queued turn that passes synchronous preflight then claims its
controller before the first credential await. Credential completion checks that signal.
Cancellation before Provider dispatch closes the current assistant with the
localized stopped state and terminates the whole replay run, leaving later
turns queued. Requirement, save, failure, cancellation, and success exits clear
the shared ref only when it still points to the controller they own.

Guard coverage: the focused offline queue file passes 16 tests. A controlled
pending credential proves Stop is already reachable, no Provider stream starts,
the current turn becomes stopped, and the next turn remains queued. A separate
completion test proves stale cleanup preserves a replacement controller. An
active-owner test proves scheduled replay does not enter sending, derive
credentials, or mutate queued state while an online request owns cancellation.
Full coverage passes 138 files / 1084 tests at 393/393 statements, 373/373 branches,
124/124 functions, and 382/382 lines; TypeScript and focused ESLint pass.

QA markers: Offline replay defers to active generation ownership.
Offline queue replay claims cancellation before async credentials.
Cancelled offline replay stops before the next queued turn.
Offline replay cleanup preserves newer generation ownership.

Residual scope: this hardens Web/PWA/WebView reconnect cancellation and queue
ownership. It does not replace live Provider/browser-origin evidence, native
target runtime QA, trusted MSIX, hosted CI, disposable live-sync, or
live-provider full-capability evidence.

new confirmation request or programmatic prompt replaced it without settling
the previous Promise. Overlapping destructive actions could therefore leave
the first caller suspended forever. Controller disposal also left the current
resolver, return-focus target, and Zustand prompt state alive.

programmatic show, requested confirmation, confirmed close, and cancellation.

meaningless no-op resolver. Hook disposal settles the current request as false
and clears return-focus and global prompt state.

preserves the new resolver, applies confirmed close, registers an idle resolver
without invoking it, and proves clearing the resolver settles pending work.

and disposal call sites, prompt/focus cleanup, removal of the no-op overwrite,
tests, and these markers.

Root cause: `useChatGenerationController` disposed speech synthesis and audio
playback, but did not abort the shared request controller used by text, image,

reload, or future routed unmount could leave provider work running and allow its

boundary. It normally uses `crypto.randomUUID()`, then combines a per-runtime

creation both use this helper; keeping it in the already shared AppData module

## 2026-07-09 Asia/Shanghai - Hosted Native CI Artifact Stat Failure Clarity

Root cause: `scripts/hosted-native-ci-evidence-report.mjs` used
`stat(...).catch(() => null)` for the downloaded hosted-native-CI artifact root
and each expected artifact directory. Permission failures, locked directories,
or other file-system errors were therefore indistinguishable from a normal
missing artifact directory.

Fix: the report generator now uses `statOptionalEvidencePath(...)`. Only
`ENOENT` and `ENOTDIR` are classified as missing artifact evidence; any other
stat failure fails closed with a repo-relative evidence path and file-system
error code while preserving the existing `gh run download --dir` remediation for
real missing directories.

## 2026-07-09 Asia/Shanghai - Speech Object URL Registration Ordering

## 2026-07-07 Asia/Shanghai - Service Worker Registration Failure Observability

browsers with service worker support, registers after `window` load, and reports
