## 2026-07-06 Asia/Shanghai - Local Cleanup Bounded Listener Inspection

Root cause: on Windows the local cleanup gate used `Get-NetTCPConnection`
without an internal timeout to enumerate watched preview ports. When that
network cmdlet stalled on the host, `check:local-cleanup` could only die by an
outer timeout, leaving neither a clean residue verdict nor a precise stale-port
failure.

Fix: Windows listener inspection now parses bounded `netstat -ano -p tcp`
output, then queries process details only for watched-port PIDs with the same
command budget. PowerShell, POSIX `ps`, `lsof`, and `ss` probes also share a
bounded command timeout so the cleanup gate fails with a verdict instead of
hanging.

Guard coverage: `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the bounded command budget, the
Windows netstat parser, the removal of the unbounded Windows network cmdlet,
and this marker.

QA marker: Local cleanup Windows listener inspection stays bounded.

## 2026-07-07 Asia/Shanghai - Sync Compact Access-Key Scroll Range

Root cause: at 320px width the Settings sticky header and segmented tabs take
more than half of the modal height, and the Sync feature hint adds more sticky
chrome before the actual form. The Sync panel first kept only 220px of trailing
scroll range; the later 560px panel range plus 420px modal spacer still left the
Cloudflare access-key field near the bottom of the Sync content clamped below
the sticky header at maximum `scrollTop`. The Cloudflare mode switch also posts
a deferred config scroll, so the visual audit could assert after its own
target-field scroll and then capture after the deferred app scroll moved the
modal back to the Worker URL area.

Fix: the compact Settings dialog now exposes the active tab on the actual modal
scroll container. At `max-width: 360px`, Sync keeps a 960px trailing panel
range and `.settings-modal-sync::after` adds 720px of modal-level scroll
range, so the access-key field can be anchored under the sticky header instead
of being clamped at maximum `scrollTop`. The visual audit now waits for deferred
settings scroll work to settle before scrolling to the target field; it still
requires the access-key field to sit near the visible top before capture.

Guard coverage: `scripts/ui-accessibility-check.mjs`,
`scripts/repository-health-check.mjs`, and

## 2026-07-09 Asia/Shanghai - Auto-Sync Foreground Pull Listener Installation Containment

Root cause: foreground pull wiring installed the `focus`, `online`, and
`visibilitychange` listeners directly inside the React effect. Those listeners
are optional background pull triggers. If a constrained WebView, browser policy,
or hostile test host threw during listener installation, the effect could fail
startup/refresh work and leave partially installed listeners or timers behind.

Fix: `autoSyncController` now routes foreground pull listener setup through
`installAutomaticRemotePullListeners(...)`. The helper contains listener
installation failures so a broken foreground trigger cannot throw through the
effect. The owning effect still starts the startup and interval pull timers, and
cleanup removes any registered listeners, so a broken optional foreground
trigger cannot poison the main app path or disable the broader automatic pull
loop.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/autoSyncController.test.ts` covers
`contains foreground pull listener installation failures`.

## 2026-07-06 Asia/Shanghai - Lazy Service Import Retryable Cache

Root cause: `src/services/lazy.ts` cached each dynamic import Promise forever.
Idle warm-up callers caught rejected imports, but the cached Promise stayed
rejected. A later real user action could therefore receive the same failed
Promise without retrying the chunk load.

Fix: all lazy service loaders now use `loadCachedLazyService(...)`. Pending and
resolved imports still reuse the cache, but a rejected import clears the cached
Promise when it is still the active one. Chat, Crypto, Markdown, Skills, and
Sync lazy services can retry after a transient chunk/import failure.

and resolved lazy service loads` and `clears rejected lazy service loads so
later actions can retry`. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and

loader usage, focused tests, and this marker.

## 2026-07-06 Asia/Shanghai - Markdown Worker PostMessage Failure Fallback

Root cause: `src/services/markdownWorkerClient.ts` registered a pending render
and an 8-second timeout before calling `worker.postMessage(request)`. If
`postMessage` threw synchronously, the pending render stayed alive until the
timeout, delaying the plain-text fallback.

Fix: the postMessage boundary now catches synchronous failures inside the render
Promise. It clears the timeout, removes the pending render, and rejects
immediately so `renderMarkdown(...)` can fall back to escaped plain text without
waiting for the worker timeout.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/markdownWorkerClient.test.ts` covers

## 2026-07-08 Asia/Shanghai - Markdown Worker Termination Cleanup Containment

## 2026-07-13 Asia/Shanghai - Browser Smoke Retained Awaited Promise Handles

Root cause: `scripts/browser-skill-smoke.mjs` sent long-running page waits to
`Runtime.evaluate` with `awaitPromise: true` and `returnByValue: true`. During
the 90-second streaming, sync, and local-reset smoke, Chrome could collect the
temporary Promise because the harness held no explicit remote object handle.
The release gate then failed with `Promise was collected`. Retrying that error
would be unsafe because many expressions send messages, click controls, or
reset data.

Fix: the shared `evaluate(...)` helper now creates each asynchronous expression
through `Runtime.evaluate` with `awaitPromise: false`, `returnByValue: false`,
and a dedicated `objectGroup`. The returned Promise object id remains retained
while `Runtime.awaitPromise` observes the result. A `finally` block releases the
object group after completion, so every action executes once without leaking
remote handles. The focused `pnpm run check:browser-smoke` pass completed in
90.1 seconds.

Guard coverage: `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` require the two-stage CDP protocol,
per-evaluation object groups, explicit release, this marker, and reject the old
one-step awaited `Runtime.evaluate` pattern.

QA marker: Browser smoke awaited Promise handles stay retained.

## 2026-07-06 Asia/Shanghai - Cloudflare Remote Cleanup Failure Gate

Root cause: Web/PWA incremental Cloudflare sync wrote the new head and then
treated stale incremental object cleanup plus legacy snapshot deletion as
best-effort work. Clear-cloud fallback had the same issue after deleting the
incremental head. That let sync or clear report success while older remote
ciphertext could remain in the Worker backing store.

Fix: `syncCloudflare.ts` now sends post-publish stale object cleanup and legacy
snapshot deletion through a release-blocking cleanup gate. `syncCloudflareClear`
uses the same gate for fallback cleanup and aggregates all known cleanup targets,
so a failed incremental object deletion still leaves legacy snapshot deletion
attempted before the clear reports failure. A failed cleanup request is a visible
sync/clear failure instead of a fake success. The gate observes every cleanup
request in the batch and raises the localized
`error.syncCloudflareCleanupFailed` message.

incremental sync when legacy snapshot cleanup fails after publish` and `fails
fallback clear when incremental object cleanup fails`, plus `attempts legacy
snapshot cleanup when fallback object cleanup fails`.

and this documentation marker.

## 2026-07-06 Asia/Shanghai - Provider Secret Cleanup Queue Corruption Gate

Root cause: `getPendingProviderSecretCleanupIds()` returned an empty list when
the pending Provider-secret cleanup tombstone was malformed. Bad JSON, non-array
JSON, empty ids, and non-string ids could all be treated as "no cleanup pending."
That made startup treat retryable Provider key cleanup as nonexistent, then
continue to load local secrets with a potentially orphaned Provider key still
present.

Fix: persisted pending cleanup tombstones now pass through a strict parser that
only accepts arrays of non-empty strings. Corrupted pending cleanup tombstones
fail closed with the localized `error.pendingProviderSecretCleanupFormat`
message. Startup does not catch this path, so hydration stops before
`loadZeroChatSecrets(...)` and the load-error surface remains redacted. The
corrupted tombstone is left intact instead of being overwritten by a later queue
operation.

Guard coverage: `src/storage/__tests__/secrets.test.ts` covers `rejects
corrupted pending provider deletion tombstones instead of dropping cleanup`.
`src/services/__tests__/appBootstrapController.test.ts` covers `blocks startup
secrets loading when pending provider deletion tombstones are corrupted`.
`scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs`
guard the strict parser, fail-closed throw, no `catch { return [] }` regression,
locale key, focused tests, and this documentation marker.

QA marker: Provider secret cleanup queue corruption blocks startup secrets.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - OpenAI Realtime Advanced Model Family Selection

Root cause: Realtime model selection was tied to legacy names. Web/native model
helpers only treated ids containing `realtime` as Realtime session models, so
the newer `gpt-audio-*` session family could be ignored, and automatic defaults
still preferred older `gpt-realtime`/`gpt-4o-realtime*` aliases.

Fix: the OpenAI preset now defaults Realtime to `gpt-realtime-2`. Web,
Android, Apple, Linux, and the live-provider smoke share the same preference:
`gpt-realtime-2`, `gpt-audio-1.5`, then older realtime aliases. The Realtime
classifier recognizes `gpt-audio-*` session models but still keeps
`gpt-4o-audio-preview` out of the Realtime endpoint bucket. Web provider
request bodies, Web capability request/check planning, and Android/Apple/Linux
native protocol/runtime tests now exercise `gpt-realtime-2` for Realtime
request and client-secret session payloads instead of leaving the real request
path on the legacy alias.

Evidence: focused Web provider model/request/capability tests, Android
ProviderRegistry/AiProtocol/AiClient capability tests, Apple ProviderRequest and
AiClient capability tests, Linux providers/ai_protocol tests,
`scripts/live-provider-smoke-check.mjs`, and
`scripts/native-parity-check.mjs` cover the model family and request payloads.
The credentialed live-provider diagnostic selected `gpt-realtime-2`; the relay
still returned 404 for `/realtime`, so live-provider full-capability release
evidence remains blocked by the external provider/relay routes.

Guard coverage: `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` require the Web/native source markers,
focused tests, PRD marker, and this QA marker.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Cloudflare Worker proxy upstream special-use host guard

Root cause: the Web/native/live-drill Provider URL safety boundary already
rejected special-use IPv4/IPv6 hosts, but the Cloudflare Worker runtime still
used a narrower upstream host guard. The Worker is the component that actually
holds the access key and forwards `/proxy` traffic, so its runtime boundary must
not be weaker than the client-side validators.

Fix: `cloudflare/sync-worker.js` now uses the same class of IPv4/IPv6 parsing
guards for upstream proxy hosts: documentation, benchmarking, multicast and
reserved IPv4 ranges, IPv6 documentation/multicast ranges, IPv4-mapped IPv6,
NAT64, and 6to4 embedded special-use addresses are rejected before proxying or
being stored through `/proxy/hosts`.

Guard coverage: `scripts/worker-security-check.mjs` sends real Worker requests
through both `/proxy` and `/proxy/hosts` with special-use host fixtures and
expects rejection. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` require the Worker source guard, focused
Worker security fixtures, PRD marker, and this QA marker. This is Worker proxy
runtime safety hardening; it is not browser-origin or full-capability
live-provider release evidence.

QA marker: Cloudflare Worker proxy upstream special-use host guard.

## 2026-07-01 Asia/Shanghai - Cloudflare Worker Proxy CORS Header Contract

Root cause: the live-provider Web UI release path fails at the browser
preflight/CORS boundary. The previous Worker security check proved upstream
proxy forwarding, but it did not bind the Worker's
`access-control-allow-headers` list to the headers actually emitted by the Web
provider request builder. A missing header would keep Node-side diagnostics
green while the browser never sends the provider request.

Fix: `scripts/worker-security-check.mjs` now owns an explicit
`expectedProxyCorsHeaders` contract. It extracts the Worker CORS allow header
list from `cloudflare/sync-worker.js`, extracts Web provider/proxy request
headers from `src/services/providerRequests.ts`, compares both against the
contract, and sends a real `/proxy` OPTIONS preflight that requests the full
header set.

Guard coverage: `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` require the CORS contract extraction,
comparison, and preflight assertions. This is browser-origin AI proxy CORS
hardening; it is not a live-provider browser-origin release pass and does not
replace the required Worker/proxy deployment rerun.

QA marker: Cloudflare Worker proxy CORS header contract.

## 2026-07-01 Asia/Shanghai - OpenAPI Worker Proxy Header Body and Response Contract

Root cause: the Worker runtime, Web request builder, and Markdown provider
contract knew about Worker-hosted provider-key headers, but the machine-readable
OpenAPI `/proxy` schema still documented only a subset of the headers. A client
or audit generated from that schema could omit `x-zerochat-provider-id`,
`x-zerochat-provider-name`, provider auth headers, or browser preflight headers
that are required for hosted-key matching and browser-origin proxy use. The same
schema also omitted the POST request body, so the JSON capability calls and
multipart image-edit/audio-transcription routes were not machine-readable. It
also omitted real Worker error statuses for access-key/provider authorization,
method/action mismatch, and oversized payloads.

Fix: `shared/sync-api.openapi.yaml` now declares a `/proxy`
`x-zerochat-cors-allow-headers` extension with the full CORS header set. The
GET and POST `/proxy` operations list provider auth headers, Anthropic browser
headers, provider id/kind/name, the Worker access key, Base URL, and proxy
action headers. POST `/proxy` also declares `application/json` and
`multipart/form-data` request bodies. `content-type` stays in the CORS extension
because OpenAPI owns it through request bodies, not header parameters. GET and
POST `/proxy` responses now declare `200/400/401/403/405/413/501`.

Guard coverage: `scripts/worker-security-check.mjs` extracts the OpenAPI CORS
extension, `/proxy` header parameters, and POST request body content types,
plus GET/POST response statuses, compares them with the explicit Worker/Web
contract, and still validates real Worker preflight behavior.
`scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` require those extraction and comparison
guards. This is a machine-readable Worker AI proxy contract fix; it is not
live-provider browser-origin release evidence.

QA marker: OpenAPI Worker proxy header/body/response contract.

## 2026-07-01 Asia/Shanghai - AI Provider Worker Proxy Content-Type Contract

Root cause: the OpenAPI schema, Worker runtime, and Web request builder now
preserve both JSON and multipart `/proxy` request bodies, but the Markdown AI
provider contract still described Worker proxy requests as
`Content-Type: application/json`. Human implementers could therefore break
`image-edits` and `audio-transcriptions`, which require multipart form-data
uploads.

Fix: `shared/ai-provider-contract.md` now documents
`Content-Type: application/json or multipart/form-data`. It states that `chat`,
`image-generations`, `image-responses`, `audio-speech`, `embeddings`,
`moderations`, `realtime`, and `realtime-client-secrets` use JSON, while
`image-edits` and `audio-transcriptions` use `multipart/form-data` and must
preserve the form-data boundary.

Guard coverage: `scripts/worker-security-check.mjs` isolates the Markdown
Worker Proxy section, extracts documented proxy content types, and verifies the
documented multipart action pair against the explicit Worker/OpenAPI/Web
contract. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` require those guards plus this QA marker.
This is contract hardening; it is not live-provider browser-origin or
full-capability release evidence.

QA marker: AI provider Worker proxy content-type contract.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Managed Proxy Host Remembered Allowlist Survives Controller Recreation

Root cause: `managedProxyHostController` remembered the last successfully
maintained Worker `/proxy/hosts` allowlist in controller-local state. The React
hook can recreate that controller when UI callback identities change, so a later
empty local host list could look empty both locally and remotely, skipping the
remote cleanup that should clear stale Worker allowlist entries.

Fix: `createManagedProxyHostController(...)` now accepts a stable
`previousGroupsRef`, and `useManagedProxyHostController` owns that ref across
controller lifetimes. The remembered allowlist still advances only after
`replaceHosts(...)` succeeds, preserving the existing non-optimistic failure
boundary.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/managedProxyHostController.test.ts`
proves a recreated controller still clears previously remembered remote hosts.
`scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the stable ref ownership, successful
replacement update, focused regression test, and PRD marker. This is Cloudflare
AI proxy allowlist consistency hardening; it is not browser-origin or
full-capability live-provider release evidence.

QA marker: Managed proxy host remembered allowlist survives controller recreation.

## 2026-07-06 Asia/Shanghai - Managed Proxy Host Reporter Containment

Root cause: the managed Worker `/proxy/hosts` maintenance path runs from a
timer-discarded Promise. It caught access-key derivation, host derivation, and
Worker replacement failures, but then called the injected `onError(...)`
reporter directly. If formatting or Sync notice delivery threw, the abandoned
runner rejected a second time and surfaced as an unhandled Promise.

Fix: `runManagedProxyHostReplacement(...)` now owns the replacement flow and
advances remembered remote host groups only after `replaceHosts(...)` succeeds.
Replacement failures route through `reportManagedProxyHostSyncFailure(...)`,
which contains secondary reporter failures; the timer discards only this
contained runner.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/managedProxyHostController.test.ts`
covers `contains managed proxy host failure reporter failures`.
`scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the focused runner, contained
reporter, timer call, focused test, and this marker.

QA marker: Managed proxy host failure reporter failures stay contained.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Web Startup Hydrate Stale AppData Guard

Root cause: startup hydration was tied to volatile UI callback identities from
the guide/notice visibility path. Completing first-run local-only setup could
set in-memory AppData to `firstRunDone: true`, then a later hydration effect
could read an older IndexedDB snapshot and reopen the first-run guide.

the `hydrate` boundary and reads latest setters/callbacks through a ref.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Auto-Sync Detached Runner Failure Containment

Root cause: debounced automatic uploads and foreground remote pulls are
fire-and-forget calls. The old auto-sync queue used bare `void runSync(...)`
calls, implicitly assuming `runSync` would never throw synchronously or reject a
promise. That contract was not local to the queue and could leak unhandled
errors if future sync wiring changed.

Fix: `autoSyncController` now routes detached automatic uploads and foreground
pulls through `runDetachedAutoSync(...)`. The helper contains synchronous throws
and rejected promises at the queue boundary. The 2026-07-06 follow-up tightened
the contract so those failures also call the injected `onDetachedSyncError`
reporter, which `ZeroChatAppRoot` maps to the existing
`notice.syncConfigErrorLocalSaved` sync notice.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/autoSyncController.test.ts` proves
synchronous runner failures and rejected runner promises are contained and
reported. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the helper, reporter, Root wiring,
both call sites, focused tests, and this QA marker.

QA marker: Auto-sync detached runner failures stay reported.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Remote-Accepted In-Flight Sync Requeues Latest Local Snapshot

Root cause: an automatic sync clears the scheduled sync timer before uploading
the current snapshot. If the user changed local data while that upload was in
flight and the remote accepted the older snapshot, the runtime only warned that
local data was kept. It did not itself guarantee that the latest local snapshot
entered the next pending upload.

Fix: when `changedWhileSyncing` and `result.remoteAccepted` are both true,
`syncRuntimeController` now queues `queuePendingSync(latest, { silent: true })`.
This reuses the existing pending-sync coalescing and pending-generation upload
deferral, then the `finally` block runs the latest local AppData through the
normal sync path.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/syncRuntimeController.test.ts` proves a
remote-accepted older in-flight upload triggers a second `performSync(...)` with
the latest local snapshot while preserving the local-kept warning.
`scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs`
guard the source marker, focused test, and this QA marker.

QA marker: Remote-accepted older in-flight sync requeues latest local snapshot.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Pending Sync Drain Uses Latest AppData Snapshot

Root cause: the pending-sync `finally` drain checked the latest `dataRef`
snapshot for pending-generation deferral, but still called `runSync(...)` with
the older queued `pending.snapshot`. If local data changed again before the
pending run started, the queue could upload a stale AppData snapshot.

Fix: `syncRuntimeController` now computes `pendingSnapshot` once from
`context.dataRef.current ?? pending.snapshot`, uses that same snapshot for
deferral, and passes it to `runSync(pendingSnapshot, pending.options)`. The
older queued snapshot is still checked for pending-generation deferral so a
generation already present on the queued run remains respected.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/syncRuntimeController.test.ts` proves a
pending run queued with an older snapshot drains with the latest `dataRef`
snapshot. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the source shape, focused test, and
this QA marker.

QA marker: Pending sync drain runs latest AppData snapshot.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Remote-Accepted Sync Stale Skill Cleanup After Publish

Root cause: remote-accepted sync published `resultData` only after Skill content
persistence, removed-provider secret cleanup, and synced Provider secret
application, but it still awaited stale Skill ref cleanup after publishing. If
that post-publish cleanup failed, the already visible and locally queued sync
success was reported as a sync failure.

Fix: `syncRuntimeController` now uses
`cleanupPublishedSyncStaleSkillContentRefs(...)` for stale Skill cleanup after
publish. The cleanup is launched best-effort with `void`, reports a focused sync
error if it fails, and does not roll back visible data, cancel the immediate
local save, suppress passphrase-synced marking, or replace the Windows complete
status with a failed status.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/syncRuntimeController.test.ts` proves
published sync remains complete when stale Skill cleanup fails after publish.
`scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs`
guard the helper, the `void` call, the absence of the old awaited cleanup shape,
focused tests, and this QA marker.

QA marker: Remote-accepted sync stale Skill cleanup stays after publish.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Sync Runtime Published AppData Immediate Local Save

Status: superseded on 2026-07-14 by the durable commit ownership boundary above.

Root cause: sync runtime paths published remote-accepted AppData, merged sync
identifiers, and clear-cloud results through `dataRef` / `setData`, then relied
on the outer `data` effect debounce to persist them. A user could see sync
success and refresh or close before the published AppData entered the local save
queue.

The 2026-06-30 fix added `queueLocalSave(..., 0)` after publication to close the
outer-effect debounce window. It did not make publication contingent on a
successful IndexedDB/CAS commit. The current implementation therefore no longer
uses this API in sync runtime: remote sync, identifier merges, and clear-cloud
must await `persistLocalSnapshot(...)`, revalidate ownership, and only then
publish or report success.

The historical immediate-queue tests and marker were replaced by durable
commit, ownership-race, secret rollback, and clear-cloud cancellation coverage.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Local Save Queue Failed Snapshot Retention

Root cause: `flushLocalSaveQueue()` cleared `queuedLocalSave` before the
AppData write was durably successful. If `save(snapshot)` failed and no newer
snapshot arrived during the write, the visible in-memory data stayed ahead of
local storage and the failed snapshot was no longer retryable after refresh.

Fix: the local save queue now tracks whether a newer snapshot arrived during an
in-flight save. A failed save without a newer snapshot restores the failed
snapshot to the queue for a future flush, while a failed save with a newer
snapshot continues to flush the latest value. The queue does not spin an
unbounded retry loop after a lone failed save.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/localSaveQueueController.test.ts`
proves failed snapshots remain retryable and failed saves without newer
snapshots do not spin retry loops. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the in-flight marker, retention
branch, retry-loop gate, focused tests, and this QA marker.

QA marker: Local save queue retains failed AppData snapshots without retry spin.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Sync Passphrase State Persistence Gate

Root cause: sync passphrase commits updated the active refs and visible value
before writing the local session secret. If `sessionStorage` / `localStorage`
threw during persistence, the app could keep using a passphrase that was not
actually saved and would disappear after reload.

Fix: `commitSyncPassphraseState(...)` now owns the passphrase state commit
boundary. It writes the local secret first, reports
`notice.syncPasswordSaveUnavailable` on failure, and only applies refs/UI state
after persistence succeeds. Hydration remains explicitly read-only for storage,
and blur/reset side effects stop when persistence fails.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/syncPassphraseController.test.ts`
proves state is applied only after successful persistence, failed persistence
does not apply state, and hydration does not touch storage. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs`
and `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the helper, source ordering,
failure branch, tests, and this QA marker.

QA marker: Sync passphrase state waits for secret persistence.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Local Data Reset Sync Passphrase Runtime Clear

Root cause: local data reset already clears the full ZeroChat secret store via
`clearZeroChatSecrets()`, then called `clearSyncPassphrase()` again. After the
sync passphrase persistence gate, that second call repeated secret persistence
and could leave stale passphrase UI state or overwrite the reset result if the
no-op storage write failed.

Fix: `clearSyncPassphrase(...)` now has an explicit persistence boundary. The
normal reset-sync-password action still persists the cleared secret, while local
data reset calls `clearSyncPassphrase({ persist: false })` only after
`clearZeroChatSecrets()` succeeds. It queues the fresh AppData snapshot before
that optional runtime clear, so a `false` result suppresses success reporting
without leaving already-cleared storage empty. The danger action reports success
only after the runtime passphrase state is cleared.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/settingsDataController.test.ts` proves
local data reset uses `{ persist: false }` and does not report success when the
runtime clear fails, while still persisting the fresh snapshot. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the source shape, focused test, and
this QA marker.

QA marker: Local data reset clears sync passphrase runtime state without duplicate secret persistence.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Full Secret Wipe Clears Provider Cleanup Tombstones

Root cause: provider deletion cleanup tombstones are stored beside local
secrets, but full ZeroChat secret wipe relied on broad legacy-prefix cleanup to
remove them. That made reset semantics depend on an incidental key prefix
instead of an explicit tombstone lifecycle boundary.

Fix: `clearZeroChatSecrets()` now explicitly removes
`PENDING_PROVIDER_SECRET_CLEANUP_KEY` when wiping all local secrets, before it
clears the sync passphrase session secret. This keeps local reset and secret
wipe paths from carrying stale provider cleanup tombstones into the next
startup.

Guard coverage: `src/storage/__tests__/secrets.test.ts` proves full secret wipe
clears pending provider deletion tombstones. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs`
and `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the explicit storage delete,
focused test, and this QA marker.

QA marker: ZeroChat secret wipe clears provider cleanup tombstones.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Secret IndexedDB Transaction Completion Gate

Root cause: local secret storage resolved `secretTransaction(...)` from
`request.onsuccess`. IndexedDB can still abort the transaction after an
individual request succeeds, so Provider key, GitHub token, provider cleanup,
and full secret wipe callers could report success before the write/delete was
durably committed.

Fix: `secretTransaction(...)` and the local-crypto `keyTransaction(...)` now
record the request result on `request.onsuccess`, but resolve only from
`tx.oncomplete`. `tx.onerror`, `tx.onabort`, request errors, and synchronous
request construction failures all reject the same promise and close the
database.

Guard coverage: `src/storage/__tests__/secrets.test.ts` simulates request
success followed by secret-store transaction failure and proves
`setProviderKey(...)` rejects instead of reporting success.
`scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs`
guard both transaction-complete source shapes, the focused test, and this QA
marker.

QA marker: Secret IndexedDB writes wait for transaction completion.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - AppData IndexedDB Synchronous Failure Cleanup

Root cause: AppData and Skill chunk IndexedDB helpers already resolved from
`tx.oncomplete`, but synchronous request construction failures such as
`store.delete(...)` throwing could reject the promise without closing the opened
database handle. That made local reset, Skill cleanup, and AppData delete
failure paths depend on browser cleanup instead of an explicit resource
boundary.

Fix: `src/storage/db.ts` now uses `rejectOnce(...)` in the single-request
transaction helper and the batched put/get/delete helpers. Synchronous request
construction failures, request errors, transaction errors, and aborts all close
the database exactly once and reject.

Guard coverage: `src/storage/__tests__/db.test.ts` proves both
`clearAppData()` and batched Skill content delete close the database when
request construction throws. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the source shape, focused tests, and
this QA marker.

QA marker: AppData IndexedDB helpers close on synchronous request construction failures.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - IndexedDB Transaction Construction Cleanup

Root cause: storage helpers closed databases for request and transaction
runtime failures, but `db.transaction(...)` / `tx.objectStore(...)` themselves
could still throw synchronously before handlers were attached. That left AppData,
Skill chunk, local secret, and local crypto key databases without an explicit
close on construction failure.

Fix: `src/storage/db.ts`, `src/storage/secrets.ts`, and
`src/storage/localCrypto.ts` now create the transaction and object store inside
the same `try` block that feeds `rejectOnce(...)`. Transaction construction,
object-store lookup, request construction, request errors, transaction errors,
and aborts all close the database exactly once and reject.

Guard coverage: `src/storage/__tests__/db.test.ts` covers AppData and batched
Skill delete transaction-construction failures; `src/storage/__tests__/secrets.test.ts`
covers secret-store transaction-construction failure. Repository and completion
audits guard the AppData, Skill, secret-store, and local-crypto source shapes,
focused tests, and this QA marker.

QA marker: IndexedDB helpers close on transaction construction failures.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Legacy AppData Migration Read-First Startup

Root cause: `loadAppData()` coupled reading valid legacy plaintext AppData with
writing the encrypted migration back to IndexedDB. If the migration save failed,
startup failed even though readable user data already existed locally.

Fix: `loadAppData()` still normalizes legacy plaintext AppData and attempts to
save it back through the encrypted `saveAppData(...)` path, but migration
failure is now best-effort and retryable. The valid local data is returned so
startup remains usable; later local saves or the next launch can attempt
encrypted persistence again.

Guard coverage: `src/storage/__tests__/db.test.ts` proves valid legacy AppData
still loads when encrypted migration save fails. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs`
and `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the read-first source shape,
focused test, and this QA marker.

QA marker: Legacy AppData encrypted migration failure does not block startup.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Legacy Skill Chunk Read-Through Encryption Migration

Root cause: Skill chunk reads accepted legacy plaintext IndexedDB records for
compatibility, but returned them without scheduling an encrypted write-back.
That left uploaded Skill content in plaintext indefinitely unless the Skill was
edited or re-imported later.

Fix: `getEncryptedString(...)` and bulk `getEncryptedStrings(...)` still return
valid legacy plaintext content immediately, but they now queue a best-effort
`putEncryptedStrings(...)` migration for those plaintext records. Migration
write failures are swallowed so readable Skill content remains available; later
reads or saves can retry the encrypted write.

Guard coverage: `src/storage/__tests__/db.test.ts` proves legacy plaintext Skill
chunks are migrated after a successful read and remain readable when migration
write-back fails. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the source shape, focused tests, and
this QA marker.

QA marker: Legacy plaintext Skill chunks migrate after read without blocking content.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Legacy Skill Chunk Compare-And-Migrate

Root cause: read-through encryption migration for legacy plaintext Skill chunks
was queued as an unconditional background write. If the Skill was deleted,
local data was reset, or a newer value won the race before the migration write
completed, the background migration could recreate stale content.

Fix: legacy plaintext migration now encrypts the original plaintext, then runs a
readwrite compare-and-migrate transaction. It writes the encrypted record only
when the current IndexedDB value still equals the same plaintext string that was
read. Deleted, reset, or replaced chunks are left untouched.

Guard coverage: `src/storage/__tests__/db.test.ts` proves a deleted legacy
plaintext Skill chunk is not resurrected by delayed migration writeback.
Repository and completion audits guard the compare-before-put source shape,
focused test, and this QA marker.

QA marker: Legacy Skill chunk migration does not resurrect deleted plaintext chunks.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Provider Key Sync After Secret Persistence Gate

Root cause: Provider key edits are local-secret writes, but the controller
updated the Provider timestamp and queued immediate AppData sync before the
encrypted secret write succeeded. A failed key persistence could still produce a
synced Provider metadata bump, making the failed edit look committed. A stale
successful write could also race after a newer draft and queue sync for the
wrong edit.

Fix: `updateProviderKey(...)` now keeps the input optimistic for responsiveness,
but commits the Provider timestamp and immediate sync only after
`setProviderKey(...)` succeeds and the current draft still matches that write.
If secret persistence succeeds but the AppData timestamp commit fails, the
persisted local key remains visible and the user gets the existing Provider-list
save failure instead of a false sync.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/providerSettingsController.test.ts`
proves sync is queued only after secret persistence, failed persistence does not
commit AppData, stale successful writes do not commit timestamps, and timestamp
commit failure keeps the persisted key visible. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs`
and `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the success gate, stale-draft
check, save-failure branch, tests, and this QA marker.

QA marker: Provider key sync waits for secret persistence.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Secret Draft Rollback After Persistence Failure

Root cause: Provider API key and GitHub token inputs optimistically updated
visible draft state and refs before the encrypted local secret write finished.
If IndexedDB/local secret persistence failed, the UI could keep using and
showing a value that was not actually stored and would disappear after reload.

Fix: Provider key and GitHub token writes now capture the previous value before
the optimistic edit. If the secret write fails and the user has not typed a
newer value, the controller restores the previous draft/ref before surfacing the
existing targeted secret-write error. If a newer edit is already present, the
older failed write does not overwrite it.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/providerSettingsController.test.ts`
and `src/services/__tests__/syncSettingsController.test.ts` cover rollback on
failed persistence and stale-failure protection for newer drafts.
`scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the previous-value capture, catch
rollback, newer-draft check, tests, and this QA marker.

This 2026-06-30 entry covers visible draft/ref rollback only. Durable Provider
key and GitHub token compensation is specified by the current 2026-07-14
sections above.

QA marker: Secret draft rollback after persistence failure stays guarded.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Provider Deletion Secret Cleanup Tombstone Retry

Root cause: Provider deletion removed the Provider from AppData and then fired
local secret cleanup as an asynchronous best-effort write. If IndexedDB/local
secret cleanup failed after the AppData commit, the removed Provider id was no
longer present at startup and the old Provider key could become an orphaned
local secret with no retry path.

Fix: committed Provider deletion now records a local pending Provider-secret
cleanup tombstone before firing `clearProviderSecretsById([providerId])`. The
tombstone is cleared only after that cleanup promise succeeds. Startup
hydration reads pending deletion tombstones, merges them with provider ids
removed by safety sanitization, clears those local secrets before loading any
secrets, and keeps startup retryable if cleanup fails.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/providerSettingsController.test.ts`
proves successful deletion queues and clears the tombstone, and failed cleanup
leaves it retryable. `src/services/__tests__/appBootstrapController.test.ts`
proves startup retries pending deletion cleanup before loading secrets and
keeps it retryable on failure. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the storage tombstone API, Provider
delete source order, startup retry order, focused tests, and this QA marker.

QA marker: Provider deletion secret cleanup tombstone stays retryable.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Provider Deletion Tombstone Before AppData Delete

Root cause: Provider deletion committed the AppData row removal before writing
the pending secret-cleanup tombstone. If tombstone persistence failed at that
point, the Provider no longer existed in AppData and startup could not infer
which local secret needed retryable cleanup.

Fix: `removeProvider(...)` now persists the cleanup tombstone before committing
the AppData deletion. If tombstone persistence fails, deletion stops with a
`providers-danger` error and the Provider/key remain visible. If the AppData
delete commit then fails, the prewritten tombstone is cleared best-effort.
Startup filters pending tombstones through active provider ids so a stale
prewritten tombstone cannot clear a still-active Provider secret.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/providerSettingsController.test.ts`
proves tombstone queue failures block deletion and failed delete commits clear
the prewritten tombstone. `src/services/__tests__/appBootstrapController.test.ts`
proves active-provider tombstones are ignored during startup. Repository and
completion audits guard the source order, tests, and this QA marker.

QA marker: Provider deletion tombstone is persisted before AppData delete commit.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Active Provider Tombstone Cleanup

Root cause: startup ignored pending Provider cleanup tombstones that still
belonged to active providers to avoid clearing live secrets, but a tombstone
left behind by a failed delete commit could remain forever.

Fix: startup now splits pending tombstones into active-provider tombstones and
retryable deleted-provider tombstones. Deleted-provider tombstones still gate
secret cleanup before local secrets load. Active-provider tombstones never touch
the secret store; they are cleared best-effort and failures do not block
startup.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/appBootstrapController.test.ts` proves
active-provider tombstones are cleared without clearing live secrets and that
cleanup failures keep startup usable. Repository and completion audits guard the
source split, tests, and this QA marker.

QA marker: Active-provider pending tombstones are cleared without clearing live secrets.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Live Provider UI Structured Remediation Contract

Root cause: live-provider browser-origin UI diagnostics preserved
`failureKind`, `failureSummary`, and `proxyPreflight`, but the actionable

`scripts/repository-health-check.mjs`, and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the UI smoke writer, release blocker

QA marker: Live-provider UI requiredRemediation contract stays structured.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Encrypted Backup Import Stale Skill Cleanup Publish Gate

Root cause: encrypted backup import published imported AppData to `dataRef` /
`setData`, then awaited stale Skill content cleanup before queueing the local
save, immediate sync, and success notice. If stale cleanup failed, the UI could
already show the imported data while the imported snapshot was not saved or

Fix: `importData(...)` treats stale Skill cleanup after visible publish as
best-effort. The 2026-07-14 durable-publication upgrade first awaits

`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the durable-commit-publish-sync-
before-cleanup source order, reject the old awaited stale cleanup shape,
require the focused test marker, and require this QA marker: Encrypted backup
import stale Skill cleanup stays after publish.

QA marker: Encrypted backup import stale Skill cleanup stays after publish.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Skill Delete Commit-Before-Content Cleanup Gate

Root cause: Skill deletion cleaned local Skill chunks before the AppData row
removal commit. If the AppData commit failed, the visible Skill row stayed in
the UI while its local content had already been destroyed.

Fix: `deleteSkill(...)` now commits the AppData row removal first with
`{ autoSync: false }`. A commit failure keeps the Skill content untouched and
reports `notice.skillSaveUnavailable`. After a successful commit, the app queues

proves Skill deletion commits AppData before content cleanup, keeps Skill

## 2026-07-30 Asia/Shanghai - Startup Repair Tombstone-First Provider Cleanup

Root cause: cleanup-before-save prevented an orphan secret when a repaired
AppData save succeeded but secret cleanup failed. It introduced the inverse
data-loss path: a failed repaired AppData save left the old durable Provider row
while its canonical key had already been deleted.

Fix: `hydrateAppBootstrap(...)` now writes a pending cleanup tombstone for
`sanitized.removedProviderIds`, persists repaired AppData, and only then clears
canonical Provider secrets. A repaired AppData save failure leaves the key
untouched; on the next startup the old active Provider makes the stale marker
safe to remove without clearing its live key. Canonical cleanup failures retain
the marker for retry, while marker finalization after canonical cleanup remains
best-effort.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/appBootstrapController.test.ts` proves
tombstone -> AppData save -> canonical cleanup ordering, save failure without
secret deletion, cleanup retry retention, and fail-closed journal writes.
`scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the tombstone-first source order and
ban parallel startup repair tasks.

QA marker: Startup repair journals removed provider cleanup before durable AppData save.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Startup Repair Empty Removed-Provider Secret Cleanup Gate

Root cause: startup hydration repaired empty or normalized AppData and then
called removed-provider secret cleanup even when sanitization removed no
providers. A no-op cleanup should not touch local secret storage; if the secret
store was unavailable, first startup or harmless startup repair could fail
before the app rendered.

Fix: `hydrateAppBootstrap(...)` now computes whether startup data needs saving
and only calls `clearProviderSecretsById(...)` when sanitization removed a
Provider or a pending Provider deletion tombstone exists. Real removed-provider
cleanup is journaled before repaired data is saved, then completes only after
that data is durable and before local secrets are loaded.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/appBootstrapController.test.ts` proves
Startup repair skips empty removed-provider secret cleanup and still cleans
actual removed-provider secrets.
`scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the non-empty cleanup gate, focused
test marker, and this QA marker.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Encrypted Backup Import Removed-Provider Secret Cleanup Publish Gate

Root cause: encrypted backup import already rebuilt imported Skill chunks and
applied imported provider secrets before switching visible AppData, but it still
cleared provider secrets removed by sanitization after `dataRef` / `setData`
published the imported data. If removed-provider secret cleanup failed, the UI
could already show the imported data while stale local provider secrets remained.

Fix: `importData(...)` now applies imported provider secrets, then clears
`sanitizedImport.removedProviderIds`, and only after both steps succeed does it
publish `context.dataRef.current = imported`, `context.setData(imported)`, the
selected provider, local save, and immediate sync. If removed-provider secret
cleanup fails, the current visible data stays in place, the import reports a
`data-backup` error, no save/sync is queued, and newly written unpublished
import Skill refs are best-effort cleaned without deleting old visible refs.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/settingsDataController.test.ts` proves
Encrypted backup import removed-provider secret cleanup gates visible publish
and keeps current data visible on cleanup failure.
`scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the import order, focused test
markers, and this QA marker.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Sync Passphrase Bump Immediate Sync Single Queue

Root cause: cloud sync passphrase rotation commits first bump shared `AppData`
so the encrypted sync timeline observes the credential change before the new
secret state is treated as committed. That bump used the default debounced
auto-sync path, unlike the rest of the user-visible Sync settings commits. A
later manual immediate sync without disabling the default path would also
double-queue the same snapshot.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Feature Hint Dismiss Immediate Sync Single Queue

Root cause: feature-hint dismissals are stored in shared
`AppData.preferences.dismissedFeatureHints`, so they are cross-device
preferences. The dismiss helper persisted the local AppData update, but did not
queue the explicit immediate sync used by the rest of the user-visible settings
paths. Because it still used the default `updateData(...)` behavior, adding an
immediate sync later without changing the commit options would also double-queue
the same snapshot through debounce and immediate timers.

Fix: `dismissFeatureHintPreference(...)` now commits with
`{ autoSync: false }` and calls `context.scheduleAutoSync(saved, 0)` only after
the dismissal preference is locally persisted. Save failures still show the
localized settings-save error and do not queue sync. The app root passes the
shared auto-sync scheduler into `useFeatureHintController(...)`.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/featureHints.test.ts` proves
Feature hint dismissals queue immediate sync after local persistence and that
failed dismiss saves do not queue sync. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs`
and `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the root wiring, single-queue
source markers, test marker, and this QA marker. Feature hint dismissals queue
immediate sync after local persistence.

Residual scope: this is Web/PWA first-entry hint preference sync hardening. It
does not replace disposable live-sync release-pass evidence, native target
runtime QA, hosted native CI, live-provider release evidence, or trusted MSIX
release evidence.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Visual Audit Large Skill Fixture Idempotent Open

Root cause: the current-page visual audit switched the Settings UI through every
locale, then immediately dispatched the large Skill-library smoke event once.
Changing locale can remount the lazy visual-smoke controller listener; a one-shot
`zerochat:smoke-large-skills` dispatch can therefore land during the listener
handoff and leave the audit waiting for `Visual bulk skill 001` even though the
product UI is otherwise healthy.

Fix: `scripts/visual-audit.mjs` now uses
`window.__zeroChatVisual.openLargeSkillLibrary(241, ...)`, a focused helper that
idempotently re-dispatches the large Skill fixture event while polling for the
rendered first generated skill. The helper still fails if the skill row never
appears; it only removes the listener-remount race.

Guard coverage: `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` require the helper, its retry cadence, the
clear failure message, and the call site. Fresh `D:\Node.js\pnpm.CMD run
qa:web-current` passed afterward with 118/118 screenshots and browser smoke.

Residual scope: this is Web visual-audit harness stability. It does not reduce
the visual coverage, and it does not replace native runtime QA, live-provider,
live-sync, hosted CI, or trusted MSIX release evidence.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Audio Drag Drop Broad MIME Acceptance

Root cause: Web audio drag hover and Web audio drop acceptance used different
acceptance boundaries. `dragHasAcceptedAudioSource(...)` treated broad
`audio/*` and `video/*` browser MIME types as acceptable, while
`acceptedAudioSourceFromDrop(...)` went through `isAcceptedAudioSourceFile(...)`,
which only accepted a fixed MIME allowlist or known filename extension. A user
could therefore see an accepted drag affordance for files such as `audio/x-wav`
or `video/quicktime`, then have the same file silently ignored on drop.

Fix: `src/services/audioAttachments.ts` now has a single
`hasAcceptedAudioSourceType(...)` predicate shared by picker/drop file
acceptance and drag affordance. Broad `audio/*` and `video/*` MIME types are
accepted consistently, while extension fallback remains for browsers that omit
the MIME type.

Guard coverage: `src/services/__tests__/audioAttachments.test.ts` now proves
`audio/x-wav` and `video/quicktime` are accepted by both the drag affordance and
drop selection paths. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the shared predicate, both call sites,
and the broad-MIME regression test marker.

Superseded on 2026-07-28: sharing one predicate fixed the inconsistent UX but
did not make arbitrary `audio/*` and `video/*` inputs valid for the transcription
endpoint. The current strict format and 25 MB contract below replaces the broad
acceptance policy; this section remains only as historical root-cause evidence.

Residual scope: this is Web/PWA audio source selection UX hardening. It does not
replace live-provider audio transcription route evidence, native target runtime
QA, disposable live-sync release-pass, hosted CI, or trusted MSIX release
evidence.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Windows Trusted MSIX Stale Evidence Expected-Blocker

Root cause: after the current source and `dist` changed, the latest trusted MSIX
install/update success JSON could be stale while the host preflight was already
clear and the current shell was not elevated. The runtime-artifact gate must not
bury that state under old `distWebAssets` hash/byte diffs or Web source noise;
the fundamental blocker is that trusted MSIX QA has to be rerun from an elevated
disposable Windows shell against the current package candidate.

Fix: `scripts/runtime-smoke-artifact-check.mjs` now compares the trusted MSIX
success-report `distWebAssets` and `windowsOutputWebAssets` manifests against
the current `dist` via `manifestsMatch(...)`. When host preflight is clear,
`currentShellElevated` is false, and either manifest is stale, it emits only the
actionable elevated-rerun blocker lines for current-source trusted MSIX QA and
returns before reporting stale success-report hash noise.

Guard coverage: `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` now require the manifest comparison, the
clear-host/non-elevated branch, and both elevated-rerun failure messages.
`node scripts/release-diagnostics-refresh.mjs` has validated the current
expected runtime-artifact blocker as Windows trusted MSIX release-pass evidence
missing because an elevated rerun is required.

Residual scope: this is blocker classification hardening only. It does not
replace trusted MSIX release evidence; the release pass still requires a
successful elevated `pnpm run qa:windows-msix-trusted:elevated` on the current
package candidate.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Manual Immediate Sync Repository Guard

Root cause: the Web/PWA single-queue fixes were guarded by focused source
markers and tests, but the repository still lacked a generic rule for the real
failure mode. A future service could call `updateData(...)` or
`updateProvider(...)`, then manually queue `scheduleAutoSync(..., 0)` without
passing `{ autoSync: false }`, reintroducing duplicate debounced and immediate
sync for the same committed snapshot.

same commit window contains `autoSync: false`. Direct snapshot publishing paths
such as blur/import flows that do not use `updateData(...)` or
`updateProvider(...)` remain allowed.

Guard coverage: `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` now guards the generic
scanner, directory traversal, `autoSync: false` requirement, and clear violation
message. Fresh verification passed with `node --check
scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and a direct repository-health run.

Residual scope: this is Web/PWA service sync scheduling regression hardening. It
does not replace disposable live-sync release-pass evidence, hosted native CI,
native target runtime QA, live-provider full-capability evidence, or trusted
MSIX release evidence.

the committed AppData snapshot. Failed commits still preserve Provider data,
show Provider-list save feedback, keep stale diagnostics, and do not queue sync.

field-aware Provider controllers cleared results only after connection-affecting

helper. `src/services/providerSettingsController.ts` keeps the explicit
connection-affecting field filter, while

after model catalog patch commits succeed. Failed commits and non-connectivity
Provider field commits keep the previous diagnostic visible.

## 2026-06-30 Asia/Shanghai - Web Composer Drag State Generation Boundary

Root cause: Web image/audio source drag state was cleared on ordinary drag/drop
paths, but not on the generation-active transition itself. If generation began
while a file drag affordance was active or rejected, the hidden internal state
could survive the run and reappear as stale source-drop highlighting after
generation ended.

Fix: `src/services/audioComposerController.ts` and
`src/services/imageComposerController.ts` now invalidate active/rejected drag
state as soon as `generationActive` becomes true, then derive the visible drag
state from that invalidation until a new drag interaction starts. The
transition is expressed through focused helpers,
`audioSourceDragStateForGeneration(...)` and
`imageSourceDragStateForGeneration(...)`, so the behavior is testable outside
React hook rendering without synchronous state writes inside effects.
`scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the exported helpers, invalidation
marker, and hook call sites, so future edits cannot leave the tests green while
removing the generation-start cleanup.

now guard those current-source build steps and the updated operator docs.

Web/PWA and Windows MSIX-ready output before packaging and installing.

## 2026-06-29 Asia/Shanghai - Windows WebView Window Bounds Fix

Root cause: the Windows native shell initialized the WinUI window without a
usable desktop size floor. The WebView runtime smoke minimized the app to tray
and restored it, and Windows restored the window as `480x295`, which is too
small for a production desktop chat surface and produced a failed runtime QA
run.

Fix: `MainWindowTray.cpp` now enforces a `900x600` minimum track size through
`WM_GETMINMAXINFO`, corrects undersized launch/restore bounds with
`SetWindowPos`, and rechecks bounds after tray restore. `MainWindow.xaml.h`
declares the native-shell helper so the behavior stays owned by the Windows
window/tray integration instead of the Web/PWA layer. `scripts/windows-webview-shell-check.mjs`
now also statically requires the `900x600` floor, the `1280x735` default target,
the monitor work-area clamp, the restore-time bounds check, and the
`WM_GETMINMAXINFO` min-track hook so the regression fails before runtime smoke.

## 2026-06-29 Asia/Shanghai - Web Provider Audio Speech False-Pass Hardening

Root cause: `validateAudioResponse(...)` accepted any non-empty response body
as an audio-speech pass. That is too weak for release evidence: a provider or
relay can return HTTP 200 with a JSON or text error body, and the Web/PWA
full-capability check would mark speech synthesis as passed even though no audio
was produced.

`src/services/providerCapabilityChecks.ts` now treats audio-speech success as a
real audio response, not just a non-empty body. It accepts `audio/*` and
`application/octet-stream` responses, and accepts common audio signatures such
as ID3, MP3 frame headers, RIFF/WAV, OggS, fLaC, and MP4/ftyp. It rejects
JSON/text/html/xml responses and plain text-looking bodies with
`error.capabilityResponseInvalid`. This preserves HTTP error attribution while
closing the false-positive path for 200 OK error payloads.

Regression coverage: `src/services/__tests__/providerCapabilityChecks.test.ts`
now proves JSON and `text/plain` audio-speech impostors fail. Repository health
and completion audit guard the `audioBytesHaveKnownSignature` and
`bytesLookLikeText` validators plus the focused test markers.

## 2026-06-28 Asia/Shanghai - Web Provider full-capability readiness gate

Root cause: Web/PWA already knew when a provider capability was not runnable
from the browser, for example Realtime without an AI proxy needing a
server-side `/realtime/client_secrets` drill, but the full-capability action
still stayed clickable and the controller still allowed the aggregate check to
start. That mixed a known readiness blocker into a failed full-capability run
and made the UI look as if the user could prove release readiness from a
browser path that the state machine had already rejected.

`ProviderSettingsEditor` and `FirstRunGuideProviderFields` now derive
`fullCapabilityCheckDisabled` from the shared
`providerCapabilityCheckReadiness(...)` state. When readiness is not `ready`,
the Settings and first-run full-capability buttons are disabled and their
tooltip uses the readiness text, such as
`error.realtimeServerDrill · capability.realtime`. The controller entry point
also hard-stops `checkProviderFullCapabilities(...)` before any network request
when readiness is not `ready`; it reports the readiness text as a scoped
`provider-capabilities` warning instead of running a misleading aggregate
check. This keeps the product contract boring and single-sourced: if the shared
readiness state says the browser cannot run the full check, no UI or action
path gets to pretend otherwise.

Regression coverage was added in
`src/components/__tests__/ProviderSettingsEditor.test.tsx` and
`src/components/__tests__/FirstRunGuideProviderFields.test.tsx` for
`disables full-capability checks until server-drill capabilities are runnable`
and in `src/services/__tests__/providerConnectivityChecks.test.ts` for
`blocks full provider capability checks when a capability needs a server
drill`. The component tests prove both Settings and first-run disable the
misleading full-capability action with the readiness reason in the tooltip. The
controller test proves that
`executeProviderCapabilityRequestPlan`, `generateImage`, and `editImage` are
not called, and that the readiness warning is emitted without entering the
`p1:capabilities` checking state. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` now guard the UI disabled predicate,
tooltip/readiness binding, controller hard-stop, and the two regression test
names.

`aria-describedby={fullCapabilityCheckDescriptionIds}`, so the generic

and
`guide-provider-capability-check-hint-openai guide-provider-capability-readiness-openai`,

## 2026-07-01 Asia/Shanghai - Provider full-capability busy label scoping

Root cause: Settings and first-run used the global `checkingProviderId` as
both the disable predicate and the current button's active label predicate.
That correctly prevented concurrent provider checks, but it also let an
unrelated Provider check hijack the selected Provider's full-capability button
copy and tooltip. After switching providers during a check, the selected
Provider could show `button.checking` in visible text, native title, or app
tooltip even though its own full-capability check was not the running
operation.

`ProviderSettingsEditor` and `FirstRunGuideProviderFields` now keep the global
busy state for disabling the full-capability action, but the visible button
label, native title, and app tooltip are scoped to `fullCapabilityChecking`.
A different Provider's check can still block a second network probe, but it no
longer claims the selected Provider is the one being checked.

Regression coverage: `src/components/__tests__/ProviderSettingsEditor.test.tsx`
and `src/components/__tests__/FirstRunGuideProviderFields.test.tsx` both cover
`does not label the current full-capability action as checking when another
provider is busy`, including `title` and `data-tooltip` assertions for the
ready action guidance. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` require the scoped label/tooltip
predicate, both tests, and this QA marker.

## 2026-07-01 Asia/Shanghai - Provider connectivity busy label scoping

Root cause: Settings scoped the Provider connectivity button's visible label to
`providerCheckKey(selectedProvider.id)`, but still used the global
`checkingProviderId` for the connectivity check and retry native title and app
tooltip. The global lock is valid for request safety, but the copy was not
scoped: an unrelated Provider check or another Provider action could disable
the selected connectivity/retry actions and make them report `button.checking`.

`ProviderSettingsEditor` now splits the predicates. `providerChecking` still
drives global mutual exclusion, `providerConnectivityChecking` is the only
path that labels the connectivity check as checking, and `providerRetryChecking`
is derived from the retry target. Unrelated global checks use
`settings.waitForCheck`, so disabled check/retry actions explain that the user
must wait without claiming the selected action is the running check.

Regression coverage: `src/components/__tests__/ProviderSettingsEditor.test.tsx`
covers `does not label connectivity actions as checking when another provider
is busy` and `labels the active provider connectivity action as checking`,
including native title, app tooltip, visible text, and retry assertions.
`scripts/ui-accessibility-check.mjs`, `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs`,
and `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` require the scoped predicates, the
Settings wait translation key, focused tests, and this QA marker.

## 2026-07-01 Asia/Shanghai - Provider single-capability busy label scoping

Root cause: Settings used the per-capability check key for the visible button
copy, but left each single-capability check button's native title and app
tooltip fixed to the capability readiness text. That split the state owner:
the active capability check could show `button.checking` in the button while
the tooltip still described the model/route, and an unrelated Provider check
could disable the action without exposing a wait reason.

`button.checking`. A ready capability blocked only by another global Provider
check uses `settings.waitForCheck` and appends the stable
`provider-capability-check-busy-{providerId}` hidden description id to
`aria-describedby`.

## 2026-06-28 Asia/Shanghai - Live Provider Current-Source Capability Drill

Root cause: the active live-provider blocker had fallen back to no-credential
`skipped` diagnostics while the preserved credential-confirmed full-capability
attempt no longer matched the current source fingerprint. That is weak evidence:
it proves the release gate is still blocked, but it does not prove which current
provider capabilities are actually working or broken.

Using only temporary process environment variables, the live-provider drill was
rerun against the current source with explicit opt-ins for chat, image, audio,
low-cost capability, and realtime checks. The sanitized
`.manual-qa/live-provider-smoke-full-current.json` and
`.manual-qa/live-provider-smoke-attempt-current.json` reports were refreshed at
2026-06-28T07:08:09.333Z, 15,249 bytes, SHA-256
`C41666B9317BB74560D66966A05DE6E2E450625DADB2964872EF76C4E2ABE8DA`,
`releaseEvidence: false`. The current drill proves chat with `gpt-5-5` returned
HTTP 200 and all three image routes passed with `gpt-image-2`:
image-generation, image-edit, and masked inpaint each returned base64 image
data. The remaining live-provider full-capability blockers are external
provider/relay route or upstream failures: `/audio/speech` 404,
`/audio/transcriptions` 404, `/embeddings` 503, `/moderations` 404, and
Realtime `/realtime` plus `/realtime/client_secrets` 404. The refreshed
`.manual-qa/release-blockers-current.json` now selects the
`credential-confirmed-full-capability-attempt` source and reports
`capabilityFailureSummary.total = 5`, `routeHealthBlockers =
audio-speech / audio-transcription / embeddings / moderation / realtime`.

The drill also exposed a diagnostic blind spot: when image generation receives a
200 response without a usable image result, `scripts/live-provider-smoke.mjs`
used to report only "no usable image" and threw away the response shape needed
to distinguish a relay/tool-result problem from a parser gap. The smoke now
adds a sanitized shape summary containing only root keys, array lengths, item
types, and item key names; it never records provider URLs, payload text, or
base64. `scripts/live-provider-smoke-check.mjs` guards this summary path.

## 2026-06-28 Asia/Shanghai - Web Provider Capability Readiness Derives From Display

Root cause: after capability-chip display moved into
`providerCapabilityCheckDisplay(...)`, `providerCapabilityCheckReadiness(...)`
still recomputed the same missing-model/server-drill/ready state through
separate helper calls. That moved the drift risk from two UI components into one
service file, but it did not remove the drift risk. One product state machine
means one source of truth.

`providerCapabilityCheckReadiness(...)` now builds the provider's granular
capability display objects first, then aggregates readiness from
`display.state === 'missing-model'` and `display.state === 'server-drill'`.

chips, Settings disabled states, and the summary banner share the same state and
localized label derivation. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
`scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` now guard this shape explicitly, rejecting
readiness code that recomputes state away from the display helper.

## 2026-06-28 Asia/Shanghai - Live Provider UI Evidence Source Binding

Root cause: `scripts/release-blocker-report.mjs` already normalizes the selected
live-provider UI evidence into a top-level `browserProviderKeyInjected` boolean,
but `scripts/release-evidence-lines.mjs` printed
`requestedInputs.browserProviderKeyInjected` directly. That let the current
handoff line report the requested/input state instead of the selected evidence
fact whenever preserved browser-origin attempt evidence and current diagnostic
inputs diverged.

The shared evidence formatter now prefers the normalized top-level
`browserProviderKeyInjected` value and falls back to `requestedInputs` only when
the normalized field is absent. The current-evidence self-test intentionally
uses mismatched fixture values (`requestedInputs.browserProviderKeyInjected:
false` with top-level `browserProviderKeyInjected: true`) so the generated
handoff cannot regress to the wrong source. Repository health and completion
audit guard the formatter and fixture. This is evidence-handoff correctness
only; browser-origin release evidence still requires a browser-allowed
Worker/proxy pass with a sent message and captured assistant marker.

## 2026-06-28 Asia/Shanghai - Live Provider UI Key-Injection Evidence

Root cause: `scripts/live-provider-ui-smoke.mjs` correctly kept Worker-hosted
provider-key mode from injecting the provider key into the browser, but the
failure-report path then hardcoded `browserProviderKeyInjected: false` for every
browser-origin failure. A direct provider-key run that reached first-run setup
could therefore fill the browser API-key field, fail during the connection
check, and write a sanitized report that incorrectly claimed the browser did not
receive the key.

The browser-executed smoke now starts `browserProviderKeyInjected` as false,
sets it to `Boolean(browserApiKey)` only after filling the first-run key input,
and returns the observed boolean through both setup-failure and assistant-result
paths. The outer report copies `result.browserProviderKeyInjected === true`
instead of inventing a failure value. `scripts/live-provider-smoke-check.mjs`,
repository health, and completion audit now guard the browser-side assignment,
outer result copy, and sanitized report field. This is diagnostic correctness
hardening only; browser-origin release evidence still requires a passing
browser-allowed Worker/proxy run with a sent message and captured assistant
marker.

## 2026-06-28 Asia/Shanghai - Provider Connectivity Route-Health Guidance

Root cause: normal Provider connectivity checks and capability checks built
endpoint-failure copy on separate paths. Capability failures already appended
localized route-health guidance for endpoint-missing errors, but `/models` or
`/chat/completions` failures in the basic connectivity check only showed the
endpoint, model, HTTP status, and provider error. That made relay route gaps
look like generic model-list or network failures.

`providerConnectivityFailureNoticeMessage(...)` now appends the same
`error.providerCapabilityEndpointRouteHealth` guidance for endpoint-class
connectivity failures. Focused Vitest coverage proves `/models` HTTP 404
failures include the route-health guidance when no configured chat model can be
probed, and also when `/models` fails but the configured chat probe succeeds
through the fallback path. Repository health and completion audit guard the
final user-visible strings so the basic connectivity check cannot regress to a
bare 404. Validation: `D:\Node.js\pnpm.CMD exec vitest run
src/services/__tests__/providerConnectivityChecks.test.ts` passed 36/36, and
`node --check` passed for the touched script files. This is Web/PWA recovery UX
hardening only; it does not close live-provider full-capability,
browser-origin, or target-runtime release evidence.

## 2026-06-28 Asia/Shanghai - Web Provider Retry Action Fidelity

Root cause: after full provider capability failures started writing structured
Provider results, those results were marked retryable but the Settings retry
button still always called the basic provider connectivity check. Users could
therefore click a visible retry affordance and rerun `/models` plus chat probe
instead of the failed full-capability route set.

`ProviderConnectivityResult` now carries an optional retry action, full
capability failures mark `retryAction: "fullCapabilities"`, and
`ProviderSettingsEditor` dispatches the retry button to
`onCheckProviderFullCapabilities(...)` for those results while preserving normal
connectivity retries for ordinary provider checks. The retry button exposes
`data-provider-connectivity-retry-action` so browser smoke and future QA can
assert the selected action. Browser smoke now drives a deterministic ordinary
Provider connectivity failure and proves that the visible retry button keeps
`retryAction: "connectivity"` instead of accidentally dispatching the
full-capability path. `ProviderSettingsEditor` component coverage now calls the
retry button handler from the returned JSX tree and proves full-capability
retry results call only `onCheckProviderFullCapabilities(...)`, while ordinary
retryable failures call only `onCheckProviderConnectivity(...)`. Focused
Provider connectivity tests prove direct and proxied full-capability failures
carry the full-capability retry action. Repository health and completion audit
guard the result field, UI dispatch, stable selector, component behavior test,
and browser-smoke retry-action assertion. This is Web/PWA recovery UX hardening
only; it does not close live-provider full-capability or browser-origin release
evidence.

## 2026-06-28 Asia/Shanghai - Web Full Capability Result Attribution

Root cause: Web/PWA Settings already had a structured
`ProviderConnectivityResult` surface for provider checks, but the full provider
capability action only emitted a scoped `provider-capabilities` notice. A route
failure in the release-facing full capability check could therefore disappear
from the stable Provider status block and lose the actionable field attribution
that tells users whether to fix the Provider Base URL or the AI proxy URL.

`checkProviderFullCapabilities(...)` now writes the aggregate full-capability
result back to `providerConnectivityResults`: passing checks record
`field: "none"` with a success result, direct route failures record the Provider
Base URL field, proxied route failures record the AI proxy URL field, and
provider-key blockers keep the provider-key field. Focused coverage in
`src/services/__tests__/providerConnectivityChecks.test.ts` proves success,
direct image route failure, and proxied embeddings failure all update the
structured Provider result while still rendering the scoped capability notice.
Repository health and completion audit guard the attribution helper and tests.
This is Web/PWA Settings UX hardening only; live-provider full-capability
release evidence still requires a passing current-source drill.

already pointed users at the actual fix path, but the other Web locales still

same product failure in translated builds: a user whose native app or terminal
works but whose browser fails on CORS/preflight would not be told to fill the

`pnpm run check:i18n`, and `pnpm run check:copy` passed. This is UX/copy
hardening only; browser-origin release evidence still requires a browser-allowed
Worker/proxy run that sends a message and captures the assistant marker.

## 2026-06-28 Asia/Shanghai - Web Speech Delete Lifecycle

Root cause: Web/PWA assistant read-aloud playback is owned by
`useChatGenerationController`, while message deletion is owned by
`createChatGenerationMessageActions`. Deleting the assistant message currently
being read could save and sync the data change without stopping the `<audio>`
element, aborting the speech request, or revoking the object URL.

`chatGenerationMessageActions.deleteMessage(...)` now returns whether the delete
was saved, and `chatGenerationController` uses that result to silently stop
speech playback only when the deleted message is the current
`speakingMessageId`. Cancelled deletes and failed saves do not stop unrelated
playback, and the ref-reading playback cleanup stays in the event callback
instead of being passed into the render-time action factory. Focused coverage in
`src/services/__tests__/chatGenerationMessageActions.test.ts` proves delete
success is true only after a saved delete. Repository health, completion audit,
and lint guard the success result, shared cleanup path, and silent stop
behavior. This is Web/PWA UX and resource-lifetime hardening only; live
`/audio/speech` release evidence still depends on a passing provider route and
browser/native runtime evidence.

## 2026-06-28 Asia/Shanghai - Web Assistant-Only Speech Action

Root cause: the product and native implementations describe speech as
assistant-message read-aloud, but Web `MessageBubble` and `MessageContextMenu`
