same speech action, and the handler had no role-level backstop.

Added shared `messageCanSpeak(...)` eligibility in `src/services/messageRendering.ts`
and reused it from the visible message row, the context menu, and
`useChatGenerationController.speakMessage(...)`. The helper requires an
assistant role, non-empty text, and a non-streaming/non-queued status. Focused
tests in `src/services/__tests__/messageRendering.test.ts` cover user, blank,
streaming, and queued messages as ineligible. Repository health and completion
audit now guard the helper, UI consumers, handler enforcement, and tests. This
is Web/PWA UX boundary hardening only; provider `/audio/speech` release
evidence still depends on a passing live-provider route.

## 2026-06-28 Asia/Shanghai - Provider Proxy Upstream Root Normalization

Root cause: direct provider requests already normalize endpoint-suffixed Base

endpoint suffixes, but third-party compatible proxy roots can misroute when a
client sends `.../chat/completions`, `.../audio/speech`, or
`.../realtime/client_secrets` as the upstream base plus a separate proxy action.

Changed Web/PWA, Android, Apple, Linux, and Windows provider protocol helpers
so proxy headers send the same normalized provider API root used by direct
requests. Web provider request tests, Android JVM capability runtime tests,
Apple capability runtime tests, Linux protocol unit coverage, repository
health, completion audit, and native parity now guard the root-normalized
`x-zerochat-base-url` contract. This is proxy contract hardening only; it does
not convert the current external relay 404/503 capability failures into
live-provider release evidence.

## Success Criteria

- Web/PWA builds, runs, and has real-browser coverage for first run, chat,
  settings, sync warnings, skills, image mode, audio mode, sidebars, model menu, RTL, mobile,
  narrow desktop, and all interface languages.
- i18n coverage stays complete for the Web/PWA, and native clients at least use
  the same language-mode list and system-locale detection.
- Sync, skills, providers, models, secrets, and cloud cleanup stay aligned across
  Web/PWA and native protocol surfaces.
- UI issues found by visual review are converted into repeatable checks.
- Native platform claims are honest: controls that are not wired must not look
  like working release features.
- Release checks clean up their own temporary servers and artifacts. The
  interactive `5173` dev server may stay open only when the user is actively
  reviewing the app.

Local hardening note: on 2026-06-27 10:25 Asia/Shanghai the Android emulator QA
harness gained bounded child-process execution and failed-run reporting. Root
cause: `qa:android:current` can spend minutes inside `android-ui-smoke.mjs`,
Cloudflare sync smoke, or contact-sheet generation; the harness previously used
unbounded `spawnSync`, so an outer command timeout could leave `node`, `adb`, or
emulator child processes running outside the normal `finally` cleanup path. A
second-order problem appeared after adding timeouts: a failed run before the
summary object was built could leave the old `.manual-qa/android-emulator-qa.json`
pass report untouched. `scripts/android-emulator-qa.mjs` now runs checked child
commands with explicit timeout budgets, kills the child process tree on timeout,
and writes `passed: false` with the failing step, timeout flag, and cleanup
verification before exiting nonzero. Repository health guards the timeout
constants, failure report shape, `killProcessTree`, and Windows `taskkill /T /F`
behavior. This is QA harness reliability evidence only; it does not replace a
passing Android emulator or physical-device runtime QA report.

Local hardening note: on 2026-06-27 11:03 Asia/Shanghai the Android UI smoke
itself gained bounded ADB commands and failed-run reporting. Root cause:
`scripts/android-ui-smoke.mjs` previously gave many `adb` calls no per-command
timeout, so a stuck `input`, `uiautomator`, `cat`, or `screencap` command could
hang until the parent QA harness killed the whole smoke. That left stale
`.manual-qa/android-ui-smoke.json` pass evidence in place and made the current
failure step ambiguous. The smoke now applies a 30-second default ADB timeout,
a 30-second screenshot timeout, records the current major step, captures failure
artifacts, and writes `passed: false` with the step, message, timeout flag, and
partial screenshot list before exiting nonzero. Repository and completion
guards lock those timeout and failure-report invariants. This is diagnostic
reliability evidence only; Android runtime release evidence still requires a
fresh passing emulator or physical-device run.

Local hardening note: on 2026-06-27 11:25 Asia/Shanghai the Android UI smoke
parent/child timeout handoff was tightened after a real `qa:android:current`
rerun failed at the parent UI-smoke budget. The run reached the message-menu and
Android share-sheet section, refreshed `.manual-qa/android-emulator-qa.json` as
`passed: false` with cleanup verification, and left no emulator or ADB process
behind. Root cause: when the parent kills the child process tree on timeout, the
child cannot run its catch block, so `.manual-qa/android-ui-smoke.json` can
remain stale unless progress is persisted out of band. `android-ui-smoke.mjs`
now writes `.manual-qa/android-ui-smoke-progress.json` on each major step and
splits the final message-menu/share-sheet/delete sequence into focused steps.
`android-emulator-qa.mjs` now uses a 20-minute bounded UI-smoke budget and folds
the child progress into the parent failure report. This improves timeout
diagnostics and keeps the budget honest; it is not Android runtime release-pass
evidence.

### 2026-07-01 Asia/Shanghai - Current evidence Android contact sheet report hash hardening

- Root cause: `assertDocsContainCurrentEvidence(...)` required the
  `.manual-qa/android-current-contact-sheet.json` SHA-256, but
  `androidRuntimeEvidenceLine(...)` only rendered the regenerated contact sheet
  PNG bytes/hash. A fresh full Android emulator QA run therefore refreshed the
  contact sheet report and made `sync:current-evidence` fail after writing docs.
- Scope: `scripts/release-current-evidence-summary.mjs` now renders both
  `contact sheet report` and `contact sheet PNG` bytes/SHA-256 in the Android
  runtime evidence line. The fixture self-test locks both fragments, so the
  machine-readable report and reviewer-readable PNG cannot drift apart.
- Validation: full `D:\Node.js\pnpm.CMD run qa:android:current --
  --avd=ZeroChatPixelAscii` passed with 40 UI screenshots, 10 Cloudflare sync
  screenshots, and a 50-shot contact sheet. `D:\Node.js\pnpm.CMD run
  sync:current-evidence` passed after the generator fix.
- QA marker: Android contact sheet report hash stays in current evidence.
- Residual scope: this fixes current-evidence handoff completeness only. It
  does not close hosted native CI, Apple/Linux target runtime QA, Windows
  trusted MSIX release-pass, disposable live-sync release-pass, or
  live-provider release evidence.

### 2026-07-01 Asia/Shanghai - Current evidence live-provider full-current label hardening

- Root cause: the current evidence handoff hard-coded the aggregate hash label
  as `credential-confirmed live-provider full-current/attempt`. When the active
  blocker evidence had no credential-confirmed attempt and the canonical
  full-current report was only a no-credential skipped diagnostic, that label
  overstated the evidence and could make a reviewer read diagnostic context as
  credential-confirmed provider coverage.
- Scope: `scripts/release-current-evidence-summary.mjs` now derives the
  full-current hash label from blocker evidence with `liveProviderFullReportLabel(...)`.
  It prints `Live provider credential-confirmed full-capability attempt` only
  when blocker evidence reports a credential-confirmed attempt; otherwise it
  prints `Live provider canonical full-current diagnostic`.
- Guard coverage: `assertLiveProviderFullReportLabelSelfTest()` rejects
  no-credential diagnostics labeled as credential-confirmed, and both
  `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
  `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the helper, self-test, and current

race Kotlin incremental cache registration and fall back to non-daemon
compilation. `scripts/android-debug-build.mjs` now acquires a
`zerochat-android-build-locks` cross-process lock before invoking Gradle and
logs `Using Android Gradle execution lock=`; `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs`
and `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the lock markers. Validation ran
`D:\Node.js\pnpm.CMD run check:android-unit` and
`D:\Node.js\pnpm.CMD run build:android:debug` in parallel. Both passed, the debug
build waited on the unit-test lock, and the log scan for
`Using fallback strategy|Kotlin daemon|incremental cache|Failed to register|Could not connect to Kotlin compile daemon|analytics\.settings`
returned no matches. Evidence logs: `.manual-qa/android-unit-lock-verify.log`
is 2,348 bytes / SHA-256
`40DE1028592161744234D322BC57766A10636877FFAE587F9BEEF02BE348880F`;

`5D3E9568A074DBDF1E9ECA6C9576122421A3A9C795F803902F43D39F749C965A`.

`text-embedding-3-small` returned `/embeddings` 503 service-unavailable.
Moderation stopped after `omni-moderation-latest` returned `/moderations` 404
route-missing, which is a route blocker, not a retryable model choice. Audio
speech, audio transcription, and realtime remain route-missing. The root
provider blocker is relay endpoint coverage/upstream health, not frontend model
selection.

Current live-provider drill results: chat and image are still the passing parts
of the current full-capability evidence (`gpt-5-5` and `gpt-image-2`). The new
bounded model fallback proved embeddings did not fail merely because
`text-embedding-3-large` was selected: both `text-embedding-3-large` and
`text-embedding-3-small` returned `/embeddings` 503 service-unavailable.
Moderation stopped after `omni-moderation-latest` returned `/moderations` 404
route-missing, which is a route blocker, not a retryable model choice. Audio
speech, audio transcription, and realtime remain route-missing. The root
provider blocker is relay endpoint coverage/upstream health, not frontend model
selection.

### 2026-06-24 Asia/Shanghai - Web audio transcription direct/proxy access-key boundary

- Scope: audio transcription submit now uses
  `generationRequiresProxyToken(requestProvider)` before deriving a sync access
  key, matching the text/image generation submit boundary.
- UX behavior: direct browser-provider audio transcription passes an empty
  `proxyToken` into the capability request plan and no longer fails early
  because sync passphrase/access-key derivation is unavailable. Proxied
  transcription still derives the access key and surfaces
  `notice.audioTranscriptionFailed` before entering the sending lifecycle if
  derivation fails.
- Coverage: `src/services/__tests__/chatGenerationAudioTranscription.test.ts`
  covers direct transcription without `accessKeyFromPassword`, proxied
  transcription with token derivation, derivation failure before sending,
  missing source, offline blocking, abort notice, and transcript draft writeback.
  Web/PWA chatGenerationAudioTranscription tests now lock missing source,
  offline blocking, direct/proxied access-key boundaries, transcript draft
  writeback, and abort notices.
- Validation: `D:\Node.js\pnpm.CMD exec vitest run
  src/services/__tests__/chatGenerationAudioTranscription.test.ts
  --reporter=dot` passed 1 file / 6 tests. `D:\Node.js\pnpm.CMD exec tsc
  -b`, `D:\Node.js\pnpm.CMD run check:repo`, and `D:\Node.js\pnpm.CMD run
  check:completion-audit` passed after adding repository/completion guards for
  the direct/proxy source and test markers.
- Residual scope: this is Web/PWA audio transcription submit UX hardening. It
  does not close the live-provider audio-transcription endpoint release-pass,
  browser-origin live-provider evidence, native target runtime QA, hosted CI,
  disposable live sync, or Windows trusted MSIX release-pass.

### 2026-06-24 Asia/Shanghai - Web image submit preparation failure visibility

- Scope: image edit/inpaint submit now catches source-image file reads, mask
  canvas export, and mask data-URL preparation before local history mutation.
- UX/data-safety behavior: failed preparation emits localized
  `notice.imagePreparationFailed` as an `error` notice targeted at `chat`;
  the draft, selected source image, local message history, sending state, and
  image generation dispatch all remain untouched.
- Coverage: all 10 Web locales plus `src/locales/keys.ts` include the new
  notice. `src/services/__tests__/chatGenerationImageSubmit.test.ts` covers
  source-image preparation failure and inpaint mask preparation failure.
- Validation: `pnpm exec vitest run
  src/services/__tests__/chatGenerationImageSubmit.test.ts --reporter=dot`
  passed 1 file / 8 tests; `pnpm run check:i18n`, `pnpm exec tsc -b`,
  `pnpm run check:repo`, and `pnpm run check:completion-audit` passed.
  `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
  `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the localized notice, catch path,
  and focused regression tests.
- Residual scope: this is Web/PWA pre-submit reliability hardening. It does not
  close disposable live-sync release-pass, live-provider browser-origin or
  full-capability release evidence, native target runtime QA, hosted CI, or
  Windows trusted MSIX release-pass.

### 2026-06-24 Asia/Shanghai - Web managed AI proxy host failure visibility

- Scope: Cloudflare sync's managed AI proxy host-list maintenance now reports Worker `/proxy/hosts` update failures instead of silently swallowing them, while still attempting every endpoint in the batch.
- Data-safety behavior: `replaceManagedProxyHosts` treats fetch failures and non-2xx responses as failed maintenance and throws sanitized `ManagedProxyHostUpdateError` without Worker URLs, Provider Base URLs, or access keys. `managedProxyHostController` advances `previousGroups` only after `replaceHosts` succeeds, so a failed replacement does not make later cleanup/retry state look complete.
- UX coverage: `useManagedProxyHostController` now surfaces `notice.proxyHostSyncFailed` as an `error` notice targeted at `sync`; all 10 Web locales plus `src/locales/keys.ts` include the new message.
- Validation: `pnpm exec vitest run src/services/__tests__/providerProxyHosts.test.ts src/services/__tests__/managedProxyHostController.test.ts --reporter=dot` passed 2 files / 13 tests; `pnpm run check:i18n` and `pnpm exec tsc -b` passed. `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guard the sanitized error, non-2xx handling, sync notice, locale key, and focused regression tests.
- Residual scope: this is Web/PWA source-level reliability hardening. It does not close disposable live-sync release-pass, live-provider browser-origin/full-capability release evidence, native target runtime QA, hosted CI, or Windows trusted MSIX release-pass.

Current clipboard fallback reliability UX note: on 2026-06-23 19:49
Asia/Shanghai, the shared Web/PWA `writeClipboardText` helper now treats failed
copy attempts honestly. If the async Clipboard API rejects, it falls back to the
temporary textarea path; that fallback must return true from
`document.execCommand('copy')`, and the temporary textarea is removed in a
`finally` block even when the fallback fails. When every path fails, the helper
rejects instead of reporting success. Cloudflare access-key copy failures now
surface the localized `button.copyFailed` message as an `error` notice in the
Sync settings section rather than exposing a raw clipboard exception. Focused
coverage:

src/services/__tests__/syncSettingsController.test.ts` passed 2 files / 10
tests, including async Clipboard success, Clipboard rejection plus fallback
success, total fallback failure cleanup, and localized access-key copy failure
feedback. `pnpm exec tsc -b` and `pnpm run check:ui` also passed.
`scripts/repository-health-check.mjs`, `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs`,
and `scripts/ui-accessibility-check.mjs` guard the fallback source markers,
focused tests, and localized Sync notice. This is Web/PWA clipboard reliability
and failure-feedback hardening only; it does not close disposable live sync,
native target runtime, hosted CI, Windows trusted MSIX, live-provider
full-capability, or browser-origin live-provider UI release evidence.

  `apps/android/app/src/main/java/app/zerochat/ui/ChatScreen.kt` into
  `apps/android/app/src/main/java/app/zerochat/ui/chat/ChatGenerationRunner.kt`.
  `ChatScreen.kt` is now 707 lines and still owns pending-message insertion,
  localized notices, cancellation handling, snapshot commits, and UI state,
  while `ChatGenerationRunner.kt` owns `runStreamingChatGenerationWithRetry`,
  `streamChatGenerationWithRetry`, `runImageGenerationWithRetry`, and
  `generateImageWithRetry`. This keeps the PRD chat surface moving toward a
  thinner screen controller without changing provider protocol behavior.
  `apps/android/app/src/test/java/app/zerochat/ui/chat/ChatGenerationRunnerTest.kt`
  now locks transient streaming retry before visible text, no retry after
  partial output, cancellation propagation, and transient image retry. The
  Android README source map, `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs`,
  `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs`, and `scripts/native-parity-check.mjs`
  now guard the new runner boundary so retry execution cannot silently move
  back into `ChatScreen.kt`.
  Fresh validation passed `node --check scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs`,
  `node --check scripts/repository-health-check.mjs`,
  `node --check scripts/native-parity-check.mjs`,
  `pnpm run check:completion-audit`, `pnpm run check:repo`,
  `pnpm run check:native-parity`, and
  `pnpm run build:android:debug -- clean testDebugUnitTest --tests app.zerochat.ui.chat.ChatGenerationRunnerTest --tests app.zerochat.ui.ChatGenerationRetryTest`.
  A first non-clean targeted Android unit-test attempt hit the known Gradle
  incremental-cache issue where the temporary ASCII project path did not see
  existing `ui/chat` sources; the clean run compiled the new runner and tests
  successfully. A same-day follow-up hardened
  `scripts/android-debug-build.mjs` so Windows non-ASCII repository paths that
  run through the ASCII junction also pass `--no-daemon`, `--no-build-cache`,
  `--no-watch-fs`, and `--rerun-tasks` to Gradle. The rerun
  `pnpm run build:android:debug -- testDebugUnitTest --tests app.zerochat.ui.chat.ChatGenerationRunnerTest --tests app.zerochat.ui.ChatGenerationRetryTest`
  passed without `clean` in that stable junction mode, and the wrapper log made
  the mode visible.

- A 2026-06-09 Asia/Shanghai live AI relay capability pass used only
  process-local environment variables for the user-provided OpenAI-compatible
  relay and did not write the provider key to repository files. `/models`
  returned 14 model ids, `scripts/live-provider-smoke.mjs` passed a streaming
  `/chat/completions` request with `gpt-5.5` and the exact `ZeroChat OK` reply,
  while the explicit image opt-in selected `gpt-image-2` but exposed relay-level
  502 responses on the dedicated `/images/generations` and `/images/edits`
  routes. The smoke and Web/Worker image path now keep those dedicated Image API
  routes as the first attempt and fall back to the OpenAI Responses
  `image_generation` tool on `/responses` with the selected text model for
  route/server failures, returning only status/path and byte-length summaries
  without printing image payloads. `src/services/providerModels.ts` now prefers
  stronger fetched chat models such as `gpt-5.5` over older, compact, mini, or
  review-specialized variants, and it infers image generation/editing plus
  audio, realtime, embeddings, and moderation capabilities from fetched model
  families. Web/PWA fetched model refresh and first-run model backfill now use a
  fetched-list-specific patch that upgrades stale automatic defaults to the
  strongest chat/image choices while preserving explicit lightweight user
  selections. Android, Apple, and Linux model-refresh helpers now follow the
  same rule at source level; Android unit tests execute the automatic-default
  upgrade and explicit-lightweight-preservation cases, while native parity,
  repository health, and completion audit guard the Apple/Linux source markers
  until target runtime QA can run. Web provider request construction now also
  exposes direct/proxied endpoint and header builders for audio speech,
  audio transcription, embeddings, moderation, and low-level realtime transport
  metadata; the focused provider request tests lock all five
  `x-zerochat-proxy-action` values, while Settings blocks browser Realtime
  checks and the live provider Realtime drill owns WebSocket/WebRTC proof.
  `scripts/live-provider-smoke.mjs` keeps image endpoint checks behind
  `ZEROCHAT_LIVE_PROVIDER_IMAGE_CONFIRM=GENERATE_ONE_TEST_IMAGE`, while
  `scripts/live-provider-smoke-check.mjs`, `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs`,
  and `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` now guard the smoke safety and model
  selection/capability inference behavior. This pass verifies the supplied relay
  for chat and image capabilities, but it does not make the key safe to commit
  or close unrelated Apple/Linux/live-sync release blockers.

- A 2026-06-06 Asia/Shanghai Provider timeout UX pass closed the remaining gap
  between the PRD "network timeout retries three times" requirement and the
  real Web/PWA fetch layer. `src/services/chat.ts` now composes the caller
  `AbortSignal` with bounded first-response timers for Provider requests:
  `PROVIDER_MODEL_LIST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`,
  `PROVIDER_CHAT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000`, and
  `PROVIDER_IMAGE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 180_000`; it also guards stalled
  streaming reads with `PROVIDER_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 90_000`. Hung
  model-list, chat, image, and mid-stream reads now fail into the existing
  retryable generation flow instead of leaving the user stuck on a spinner after
  the request starts. `src/services/providerErrors.ts` now owns
  `providerTimeoutError()` as a retryable `timeout` Provider error, while
  user-triggered cancellation is still preserved as `AbortError` and does not
  masquerade as a retryable network failure. Focused coverage in
  `src/services/__tests__/chat.test.ts` proves a hung Provider request becomes
  a retryable timeout, a stalled streaming response times out after partial
  tokens, and user-cancelled Provider requests plus stream reads remain
  `AbortError`; repository-health and completion-audit guards now require this
  timeout layer and its tests. Fresh verification passed `pnpm exec tsc
  --noEmit`, targeted Vitest for `chat.test.ts` with 4 tests, `pnpm run
  check:unit` with 375 tests, `pnpm run check:repo`, `pnpm run
  check:completion-audit`, `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run check:security`, and
  `pnpm run check:bundle`. The current bundle gate reports first-load 83.78 KiB
  gzip, total static 281.53 KiB gzip, text static 227.32 KiB brotli / 266.34
  KiB gzip, and main 69.02 KiB gzip.

## Issues Found And Fixed In This Pass

- Apple chat rendering is now closer to the PRD source boundary instead of
  keeping every visible chat component inside one oversized `ChatView.swift`.
  `apps/apple/App/MessageBubble.swift` now owns the native message bubble,
  copy action, assistant `ShareLink`, Haptic Touch preview card, attachment
  preview, and platform image display/download helpers. The Xcode project adds
  that file to the app target sources, while SwiftPM still compiles it through
  the existing `App/` executable target path. `scripts/native-parity-check.mjs`
  and `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` now guard the focused source file and
  Xcode membership so the Apple chat surface cannot silently collapse back into
  a monolithic source file. This is source-structure progress only; real
  iPhone/iPad/macOS runtime visual QA still requires an Apple host.

- Apple composer input is now closer to the PRD source boundary as well.
  `apps/apple/App/ComposerView.swift` now owns the text/image mode segmented
  pickers, compact image generate/edit/inpaint labels with full accessibility
  names, source/mask file picker rows, editing-state cancel action, and
  Cmd+Enter send/stop button wiring. The Xcode project includes the new file in
  app target sources, and native parity, native i18n, completion audit, and
  repository health now guard the focused composer file. This is source-level
  progress only until iPhone/iPad/macOS runtime QA proves the layout and
  keyboard shortcut on real Apple targets.

- Apple onboarding empty state is now closer to the PRD source boundary.
  `apps/apple/App/OnboardingView.swift` now owns the native empty-state view and
  the iOS 17+/macOS 14+ TipKit first-use prompt helper, while `ChatView.swift`
  keeps the visible setup-path invocation and localized setup CTA/body. The
  Xcode project includes the new file in app target sources, and native parity,
  native i18n, completion audit, and repository health now guard the focused
  onboarding source file. This remains source-level progress until real
  iPhone/iPad/macOS runtime QA proves the prompt and empty state on device.

- Apple ProviderRegistry.swift now owns the PRD Provider preset boundary.
  `apps/apple/Sources/ZeroChatCore/ProviderRegistry.swift` now contains the
  first-run Provider catalog, custom OpenAI-compatible relay name normalization,
  OpenAI `gpt-image-2` image-model backfill, and shared model de-duplication.
  `ChatView.swift` now initializes the default snapshot from that core registry,
  while `SettingsView.swift` continues to use the shared `uniqueModels` helper
  for fetched and manually entered models. Native parity, completion audit, and
  repository health now guard the focused core file. This is source-level
  structure progress; Apple target runtime QA is still required before claiming
  the Provider setup flow is visually complete on iPhone/iPad/macOS.

- Apple CryptoEngine.swift now owns the PRD CryptoKit boundary. The AES-256-GCM
  and PBKDF2-SHA256 vault/object encryption implementation moved from the broad
  `SnapshotCrypto.swift` name into
  `apps/apple/Sources/ZeroChatCore/CryptoEngine.swift`, matching the core
  source layout requested in `docs/REQUIREMENTS.md`. `SnapshotCrypto.swift`
  remains as a one-line compatibility alias, while `ChatView.swift` and
  `SyncClient.swift` now instantiate `CryptoEngine()` directly. Native parity,
  completion audit, and repository health guard the new focused file, the
  shared crypto markers, gzip incremental-object read compatibility, and the
  alias so older references cannot silently drift.

- Android CryptoEngine.kt and KeyDerivation.kt now own the PRD crypto boundary.
  The AES/GCM vault/object implementation moved from the broad
  `SnapshotCrypto.kt` name into
  `apps/android/app/src/main/java/app/zerochat/sync/CryptoEngine.kt`, while
  PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 key derivation lives in
  `apps/android/app/src/main/java/app/zerochat/sync/KeyDerivation.kt`.
  `SnapshotCrypto.kt` remains as a compatibility typealias, and the main sync,
  auto-sync, and encrypted-backup UI paths now instantiate `CryptoEngine()`
  directly. Native parity, completion audit, and repository health guard the new
  focused files, AES-GCM/PBKDF2 markers, gzip incremental-object read
  compatibility, and alias. Android validation was refreshed after the split:
  native prerequisites passed, debug unit tests passed, debug and Release APKs
  built, the Release APK size check passed at 2.07 MiB, and `pnpm run
  qa:android` refreshed 34 UI screenshots plus 10 Cloudflare sync screenshots

- Live sync diagnostic reports and release-pass evidence now have separate
  runtime-artifact gates. `scripts/runtime-smoke-artifact-check.mjs` keeps
  `--require-live-sync-report=<path>` for skipped/blocked/failed diagnostic
  artifacts, and adds `--require-live-sync-passed-report=<path>` for release
  evidence that must be a passing live sync release drill report with
  `status: "passed"` and `passed: true` plus the full
  upload, second-device pull, edit, delete, remote-clear, cleanup, and
  secret-redaction checks. Skipped, blocked, and failed reports must now mark
  themselves as `evidenceType: "diagnostic"` with `releaseEvidence: false`,
  while passing reports must mark `evidenceType: "release-pass"` with
  `releaseEvidence: true`. This keeps a useful blocked/failed report from being
  mistaken for disposable live cloud-sync completion. `scripts/live-sync-release-drill-check.mjs`,
  `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs`, and `docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md` now
  guard and document that distinction.

- Current-page Web QA now binds the user-visible app icon and cloud-sync entry
  into the shared runtime-artifact gate. `scripts/browser-skill-smoke.mjs`
  writes `.manual-qa/web-current-icon-sync-dom.json` during
  `pnpm run qa:web-current`; `scripts/web-current-page-qa.mjs` records byte and
  SHA-256 evidence for that DOM report; and
  `scripts/runtime-smoke-artifact-check.mjs` now rejects current-page evidence
  unless the Chinese page proves a visible `favicon.svg` app logo plus both the
  sidebar `sync-pill` and chat-header `chat-sync-strip` entries with the exact
  `本地 · 开启云同步` action and
  `云同步: 本地 · 开启云同步 · 云同步关闭` accessible label. This keeps the two
  user-visible invariants from drifting into a stale sidecar report.

- The local Windows WebView QA command now requires the shared runtime artifact
  validator before it returns. `package.json` appends
  `node scripts/runtime-smoke-artifact-check.mjs --require-runtime-artifact=windows`
  to `pnpm run qa:windows-webview`, so the one-command local pass must both
  capture the real Release WebView window and prove the PNG/JSON pair is present
  and valid. `scripts/windows-webview-shell-check.mjs`,
  `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs`, `README.md`,
  `apps/windows/README.md`, `docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md`, and
  `docs/NATIVE_QA_CHECKLIST.md` now guard or document that local evidence chain.

- Windows hosted native CI now produces required WebView runtime visual
  evidence before packaging. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` builds the unpackaged
  Release shell, runs `scripts/windows-webview-runtime-smoke.ps1`, validates the
  captured PNG/JSON with `node scripts/runtime-smoke-artifact-check.mjs
  --require-runtime-artifact=windows`, then rebuilds the output with
  `-MsixReady` before MSIX packaging. The Windows artifact upload now includes
  `.manual-qa/windows-webview-runtime-smoke.png` and
  `.manual-qa/windows-webview-runtime-smoke.json`; `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs`
  guards the build/smoke/validate/MSIX-ready/upload order.

- Apple and Linux hosted runtime smoke validation is now explicitly required
  instead of relying on optional artifact discovery. `scripts/runtime-smoke-artifact-check.mjs`
  accepts `--require-runtime-artifact=<platform>` for `windows`, `apple`, or
  `linux` and fails if the named platform's PNG/JSON pair is absent. The Linux
  CI job now validates its Xvfb GTK screenshot with
  `--require-runtime-artifact=linux`, and the macOS CI job validates its app
  window screenshot with `--require-runtime-artifact=apple` before either job
  uploads screenshots/metadata. `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs`,
  `docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md`, and `docs/NATIVE_QA_CHECKLIST.md` now guard and
  document the required runtime evidence path.

- Hosted live-provider UI screenshots now have a required validation step before
  publication. `.github/workflows/live-drills.yml` runs
  `node scripts/runtime-smoke-artifact-check.mjs --require-live-provider-ui-screenshot=.manual-qa/web-live-ui-provider-smoke.png`
  after the browser UI smoke when that step actually ran, then uploads
  `web-live-ui-provider-smoke` only when the validation step succeeds.
  `scripts/runtime-smoke-artifact-check.mjs` now supports the required
  screenshot option and fails clearly if the expected PNG is missing or does not
  meet the provider UI screenshot quality checks; the live-provider and
  completion audit guards cover the hosted validation and upload outcome gate.

- Live provider UI smoke screenshots are now covered by the shared runtime
  artifact gate instead of existing only as uploaded files. `scripts/runtime-smoke-artifact-check.mjs`
  validates `.manual-qa/web-live-ui-provider-smoke.png` and
  `.manual-qa/web-live-ui-provider-smoke-current.png` when present, checking
  PNG bytes, dimensions, sampled color diversity, and blank/collapsed light or
  dark captures. The fresh local run passed with `live-provider-ui-smoke:
  758x482, 38689 bytes` and `live-provider-ui-smoke-current: 758x482, 26946
  bytes`; `scripts/live-provider-smoke-check.mjs` and
  `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` now guard this validation path.

- The manual live-drills workflow no longer lets browser-provider diagnostics
  disappear when the Web UI smoke fails. `.github/workflows/live-drills.yml`
  now runs provider API and browser UI smokes as separate steps, gates the UI
  step on API preflight success, and uploads `web-live-ui-provider-smoke` with
  `always()` when the UI step actually runs and either passes or fails. This
  preserves the captured CORS/provider failure screenshot for review while
  still avoiding a misleading screenshot requirement when credentials or API
  preflight fail before the browser smoke starts. `scripts/live-provider-smoke-check.mjs`,
  `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs`, and `docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md` now
  guard and document that hosted evidence flow.

- The manual live-drills workflow now validates live sync drill reports before
  publishing them as release evidence, and successful hosted sync drills must
  pass the stricter passed-only report gate. `scripts/runtime-smoke-artifact-check.mjs`
  accepts `--require-live-sync-report=<path>` and fails clearly when the named
  `live-sync-release-drill.json` is missing, malformed, internally inconsistent,
  or secret-bearing. `scripts/live-sync-release-drill.mjs` now writes sanitized
  blocked reports for missing confirmation/passphrase/provider credentials
  without touching remote storage, and marks runtime failures after the first
  remote sync attempt with `remoteTouched: true`. `.github/workflows/live-drills.yml`
  runs required validation with `if: always()` after the Cloudflare/Gist drill
  step, runs
  `--require-live-sync-passed-report=.manual-qa/live-sync-release-drill.json`
  when that drill step succeeds, and uploads `live-sync-release-drill-report`
  only when the diagnostic validation succeeds and the passed-only validation
  either succeeds or was skipped. This lets blocked/failed diagnostics stay
  reviewable while preventing a successful hosted disposable sync run from
  publishing non-passing release evidence. `scripts/live-sync-release-drill-check.mjs` and
  `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` now guard the workflow validation step,
  upload outcome gate, blocked/failed report markers, and CLI option. Fresh
  validation passed the required-report positive and missing-report negative
  runtime-artifact checks, plus the live-drill, completion, docs, repo, and
  runtime artifact gates.

- Hosted native CI prerequisite reports are now required, not merely optional
  scan targets. `scripts/runtime-smoke-artifact-check.mjs` accepts
  `--require-native-prereq=<path>` and fails if the named
  `native-prereq-*.json` report is missing, malformed, or internally
  inconsistent. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs that required-report validator
  with `if: always()` immediately after each Windows, Android, Linux, and Apple
  native preflight, so an SDK/toolchain blocker still leaves a validated JSON
  report before the job stops. The completion audit now guards the CLI option
  and all four CI validation steps. Fresh validation passed
  `node scripts/runtime-smoke-artifact-check.mjs

- Native prerequisite reports are now covered by the shared runtime artifact

- The Web/PWA composer did not match the PRD keyboard contract: the
  requirements specify `Ctrl+Enter` on Windows/Linux or `Cmd+Enter` on macOS to
  send, `Shift+Enter` to insert a newline, and the shortcut to be discoverable
  from the send-button tooltip. The prior handler sent on plain Enter, which
  made multi-line drafting too easy to submit accidentally. `src/App.tsx` now
  detects the platform shortcut, exposes the active action as
  `{action} ({shortcut})` / `{action}（{shortcut}）` through localized tooltip and
  `aria-label`, and only submits when Enter is combined with Ctrl or Cmd and

- Large uploaded Skills now avoid one IndexedDB transaction per chunk and one
  unbounded crypto burst per import/sync on the Web/PWA path. Skill import
  encrypts chunks with bounded concurrency, batches encrypted chunk writes,
  cloud-sync materialization batches stored chunk reads and decrypts with the
  same concurrency cap, Skill deletion batches local chunk cleanup, and
  single-request storage helpers resolve only after the IndexedDB transaction
  completes. `skill-system-check` guards these markers so future changes cannot
  silently reintroduce large-file stutter.

- Apple/macOS source parity now includes the shared Cloudflare incremental
  vault/object auto-sync path. `ZeroChatViewModel.commit` and Keychain secret
  edits enqueue a 700ms debounced sync; the vault uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256
  plus AES-256-GCM with provider keys inside `SyncVault`; existing cloud data is
  decrypted before any upload so a wrong data password cannot silently overwrite
  remote data; empty first devices accept remote data while first-sync
  local/cloud conflicts remain blocked. `native-parity-check` guards manifest,
  message chunk, Skill chunk, gzip read, and stale-object cleanup source
  markers, but Apple Swift/Xcode runtime and visual sync QA are still blocked on
  this Windows host.
- Linux source parity now includes the same shared Cloudflare incremental
  vault/object auto-sync core. `SnapshotCrypto` implements PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256
  plus AES-256-GCM, `SyncVault` carries provider keys, `SyncSecretStore`
  derives the Worker access key from the data password, and
  `AutoSyncCoordinator` coalesces local saves with a 700ms debounce, decrypts
  existing cloud data before upload, accepts remote data on an empty first
  device, and blocks first-sync local/cloud conflicts. GTK Data settings now
  source-wire Cloudflare remote clear through validation, a localized dangerous
  confirmation, and a background `SyncClient` call. Target Linux runtime and
  remote readback QA are still blocked on this Windows host.
- Visual audit now fails any captured state where a visible non-icon control or
  key control group clips its label, extending the earlier browser-smoke
  clipped-control guard into the current visual gallery.
- Visual audit now also measures rendered button content against the button box
  center, so centered-label regressions are caught by geometry instead of only
  by CSS-source markers.
- Visual audit now checks every captured visible action target for a minimum
  28px rendered box, extending the browser-smoke tap-target guard across the
  current full screenshot review set.
- Visual audit now checks visible buttons, fields, and file-upload labels for
  rendered overlap, extending the browser-smoke collision guard across the full
  current screenshot review set.
- Skill token-unit i18n polish: the Skill metadata line no longer leaves the
  `{tokens}` unit in English across non-English Web/native dictionaries. Web,
  Android, Apple, Linux, and Windows now use localized terms such as Chinese
  `词元`, Japanese `トークン`, Korean `토큰`, French `jetons`, and Russian
  `токенов`; `copy-consistency-check` rejects the old non-English
  `{tokens} tokens` fragments, and `browser-skill-smoke` now adds a zh-CN Skill
  and waits for the visible `词元` text.
- GitHub token wording is now localized in user-facing non-English sync copy,
  reset-data copy, and localized sync setup guides. Chinese Web/PWA and docs

  terms such as `GitHub トークン`, `GitHub 토큰`, `GitHub टोकन`,
  `Jeton GitHub`, and `токен GitHub`, and the copy/deploy gates reject old
  non-English `GitHub Token` fragments. `browser-skill-smoke` also opens zh-CN
  Settings > Sync > GitHub Gist and waits for visible `GitHub 令牌`.
- GitHub Actions are now pnpm-first to match the checked-in `pnpm-lock.yaml`
  and the documented local workflow. CI, GitHub Pages, live release drills, and
  the manual Windows Signed MSIX workflow use `pnpm/action-setup` pinned to
  `11.1.2`, pnpm cache keyed by `pnpm-lock.yaml`,
  `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, and pnpm package scripts; `package.json`
  pins `pnpm@11.1.2` through `packageManager`, while `package-lock.json`
  remains checked for npm compatibility.
- Cloudflare Pages direct deploy now has a safer beginner rehearsal path:
  `pnpm run deploy:cf -- --dry-run` runs the local TypeScript/Vite build and
  prints the Wrangler command without uploading. The deploy helper also has
  `--help` and passes extra arguments through to Wrangler for advanced use.
  The release gate now runs this dry-run automatically with guarded
  `--skip-build`, so it checks the direct-upload command against the already
  built `dist/` without paying for a second TypeScript/Vite build. Real uploads
  still always build fresh, and `--skip-build` is rejected unless it is paired
  with `--dry-run`. If the helper is run directly on a machine without `npx`,
  the dry-run tells the user to run it through pnpm before uploading instead of
  pretending an unavailable command will work.
- Closed mobile sidebar accessibility was tightened after a hands-on browser
  pass found that off-canvas sidebar controls stayed tabbable while hidden.
  The sidebar now follows the desktop/mobile breakpoint, remains interactive
  when docked, and becomes `aria-hidden` plus `inert` only while closed in the
  mobile overlay layout. Hidden sidebar buttons also receive `tabIndex=-1`, so
  older or inconsistent WebViews do not leave off-screen controls in the Tab
  order. Opening the mobile sidebar now moves focus to the close button, and
  backdrop/Escape close restores focus to the opener.
  `browser-skill-smoke` now verifies the closed sidebar cannot receive focus
  and has `0` tabbable sidebar buttons after backdrop or Escape close, while
  `ui-accessibility-check` guards the React markers.
- File upload buttons now expose a visible `:focus-within` ring, so keyboard
  users can see focus on the transparent file inputs used by choose-image,
  import-Skill, and import-backup actions. `ui-accessibility-check` guards the
  file-button focus ring alongside the hidden-input sizing rule.
- Busy Skill import now also marks the visible file-upload label with
  `aria-disabled` and a disabled class, so the visible control does not look
  clickable while its hidden file input is disabled.
- Keyboard-focused action buttons now share the same visible focus ring as form
  fields, including icon, ghost, primary, danger, and send buttons. This keeps
  keyboard navigation visible across browsers instead of relying on inconsistent
  default outlines.

- The compact-display preference now has explicit native parity coverage.
  Android, Apple, Windows, and Linux must preserve the shared preference field

- Korean model-list placeholder copy was visually unpolished and missed its

- Spanish, Arabic, Portuguese, Russian, and French Skill-content placeholders
  still contained the English word `prompts`. Replaced those visible strings

- Strengthened `i18n-completeness-check` so it also guards the "follow system"
  startup path and lazy locale chunk loading. Non-inline locales must stay

- Strengthened browser smoke so a fresh profile emulates a French browser via
  `navigator.languages`, verifies the first-run UI loads in French, then switches

- Re-audited the skill sync path against the user's cloud-cleanup requirement:
  the existing skill system check already simulates Cloudflare incremental sync,
  proves skill chunks are stored as separate encrypted objects, proves manifests
  carry only lightweight refs/previews, covers first-sync cloud/local/merge
  choices, and verifies deleting a skill removes stale remote skill objects.
  The check now also guards that skill add/import/edit/delete/settings changes

  triggers auto-sync.
- Added a synthetic large-skill stress path to `skill-system-check`: a 150KB+
  uploaded skill must split into many bounded chunks, keep full content out of

- Skill add, import, delete, and enable/fixed/auto-match toggles now queue cloud
  sync immediately after updating AppData. Numeric Skill settings keep the normal

- Added `node scripts/cloud-sync-e2e-check.mjs`, which routes the real Web sync
  service through the real Cloudflare Worker code backed by in-memory KV/R2. It
  uploads a skill, verifies a second empty device accepts the cloud data, edits
  the skill and verifies the old encrypted R2 object is replaced, deletes the
  skill, verifies no stale remote skill object remains, and verifies `/sync/clear`
  removes all incremental remote objects.
- Added `node scripts/gist-sync-e2e-check.mjs`, which routes the real Web sync
  service through a mocked GitHub Gist API. It verifies first-device private
  Gist creation, second-device restore, first-sync conflict protection, merge,
  wrong-password rejection without overwrite, Skill edit propagation, Skill
  delete cleanup from pulled cloud data, and clear-remote deletion of the
  ZeroChat Gist file.
- Added `node scripts/live-sync-release-drill.mjs` for the final disposable
  live-cloud release drill. It refuses to touch live storage unless the release
  engineer sets an explicit destructive confirmation value, then exercises
  upload, second-device pull, edit, delete, remote clear, post-clear readback,
  stale Cloudflare Skill-object checks, and disposable Gist cleanup against real
  Cloudflare or GitHub credentials.
- The localized sync setup files for Spanish, Hindi, Arabic, Portuguese,
  Russian, Japanese, Korean, and French still contained an English placeholder
  guide. Replaced them with concise localized setup instructions and added a

  boilerplate.
- Added `npm run verify:release` as the one-command release gate and updated all
  beginner Web deployment guides to use it instead of three separate commands.
  `deploy-readiness-check` now requires this simpler release path.
- Replaced nested `npm run` calls inside the release gate with
  `scripts/verify-release.mjs`, so the same ordered gate can be run through the
  package script or directly with `node scripts/verify-release.mjs --release`
  on machines where Node is present but `npm` is not on `PATH`.
- Added `pnpm run verify:all-platforms` for final all-platform release audits.
  It first runs `node scripts/native-build-prereq-check.mjs --platform=all`

- CI and GitHub Pages workflows now use pnpm install/cache plus

  Linux native preflight, executes `cargo check --locked`, builds the release
  binary, and uploads the artifact so Linux source, dependency, and release-build
  drift is caught before target-desktop runtime QA.
- Apple `Package.swift` now includes a `ZeroChatAppleApp` executable target that
  compiles the checked-in SwiftUI `App/` source against `ZeroChatCore`. CI now
  runs the Apple native preflight, builds that SwiftPM product on `macos-latest`,
  and builds the checked-in Xcode shared scheme without signing credentials,
  catching visible Apple source and project drift.
- Apple Xcode project now checks in a ZeroChat app target and shared scheme under
  `apps/apple/ZeroChat.xcodeproj`; source guards verify that it includes
  `App/` SwiftUI sources, supports iOS/iPadOS/macOS, and links the local
  `ZeroChatCore` package product. Apple simulator/device visual QA remains a
  release blocker until it runs on a Mac with Xcode.
- The native preflight now reports the Apple SwiftPM app compile target
  separately from the production Xcode app target, so losing either the
  CI-compiled SwiftUI source target or the checked-in Xcode bundle target cannot
  be hidden behind generic Apple source-file presence.
- CI platform jobs are configured with explicit timeouts: the Web release gate and Apple
  Swift/Xcode job cap at 20 minutes, while Windows, Android, and Linux native
  jobs cap at 30 minutes. The repository health check guards these caps so SDK
  downloads or native builds cannot hang PR feedback indefinitely.
- Strengthened `repository-health-check` so the release gate, AppData auto-sync
  markers, skill-content materialization before sync, and local skill chunk
  rebuild after remote/imported data remain guarded at source level.
- Added a direct AppData setter guard so future user-edit paths cannot silently
  bypass `updateData`; only initialization, remote-acceptance/import/reset, and
  cloud-clear state transitions may call `setData` directly.
- Expanded the repository secret scan to include unignored untracked files, so
  newly added docs/scripts/locales are checked before they are staged. A direct
  workspace scan also found no copy of the temporary API key or endpoint used
  during manual testing.
- Strengthened `native-parity-check` from broad marker checks to concrete
  source-contract checks across Android, Apple, Windows, and Linux. It now
  rejects native drift in Skill metadata/chunks/settings, incremental sync
  envelope fields, first-sync local/cloud/merge choices, cloud-clear cleanup
  fallbacks, Worker endpoint safety rules, and AI provider Base URL rules that
  reject credentials, query strings, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, local/private
  network hosts, and LAN suffixes.
- Image composer empty-state copy now follows the active mode. The central
  welcome panel says "start creating images" in image mode instead of reusing
  the chat title, and `ui-accessibility-check` guards that behavior.
- Added source-level native Skill management surfaces across Android, Apple,
  Windows, and Linux. Android/Apple now include state-backed import/add/edit/delete
  flows in source; Windows/Linux expose native controls that still need runtime
  event-handler QA. This prevents source-level schema parity from being mistaken
  for finished native UX parity.
- Expanded the visual audit from 40 to 83 screenshots, then later to 84, so Settings > Skills is
  now reviewed on both 390px mobile and 320px compact mobile, and the Web/PWA
  also gets explicit 300px ultra-compact, 280px tiny desktop, first-sync
  conflict, compact-display, light-theme settings/chat, 280px tiny desktop
  settings, and 260px/240px startup loading screenshots.
- Lowered the Web/PWA minimum usable width from 320px to 300px, added 300px
  browser smoke and visual audit coverage, and increased the ultra-compact
  textarea height so image placeholders wrap instead of clipping.
- Tightened the 300px short-height image edit/inpaint empty state after visual
  review showed the setup card and image tools competing for vertical space.
  The card now keeps the actionable Settings button visible while hiding
  repeated helper copy in ultra-compact image-tool mode.
- The visual audit now regenerates `visual-audit-contact-sheet.jpg` instead of
  leaving a stale overview image behind. Contact-sheet image loading is forced
  for the audit pass and has a timeout, so the QA helper cannot hang on lazy
  thumbnails.
- Localized the image inpaint mode label in non-English Web/PWA locales,
  shortened the inpaint placeholder text, and added a copy guard so non-English
  locale files cannot fall back to the English `Inpaint` label.
- Added `docs/NATIVE_QA_CHECKLIST.md` and linked it from the release/platform
  docs so native release claims require real SDK/device runtime and visual QA,
  not just source-level parity checks.
- Composer mode buttons now expose stable `data-compose-mode` selectors, and the
  UI guard checks them so browser QA cannot accidentally click matching sidebar
  text while trying to switch between chat and image mode. Browser smoke now uses
  the same stable selectors for Skills and image-mode navigation.
- Native backup copy now describes the actual Android/Apple/Linux native backup
  flow instead of a Web/PWA handoff. `copy-consistency-check` guards against the
  old disabled-control markers while still requiring honest Windows fallback
  copy.
- Windows and Linux Skill editing controls no longer look silently usable while
  their state/service wiring is unverified. They now show a localized Web/PWA
  handoff note and keep import/add/edit/delete/toggle controls disabled until
  runtime QA proves the native wiring.
- Windows and Linux native Skill handoff copy now avoids saying that unverified
  native screens already sync Skill data. The UI says Skill data is preserved and
  sends editing to Web/PWA until that native screen has runtime verification;
  `copy-consistency-check` now blocks the old overpromising phrases.
- Linux is a native desktop application, so `apps/linux/Cargo.lock` is now part
  of the required project files checked by `repository-health-check`; native QA
  should not float Rust dependency versions between machines.
- GitHub Actions now use pnpm, so `pnpm-lock.yaml` and the pinned
  `packageManager` field are the default CI install path. `package-lock.json`
  is still required and checked against `package.json` so npm users keep a
  working fallback instead of discovering lockfile drift late.
- Release and platform documentation now make the same distinction, and
  `copy-consistency-check` guards the wording so future native release notes do
  not accidentally market unverified native Skill management as complete.
- Strengthened `deploy-readiness-check` so the beginner docs must keep saying
  that encrypted sync does not require `dist/`, Web deployment, or a Web hosting
  provider. This guards the most common GitHub Pages vs Gist / Pages vs Worker
  confusion for new users.
- Cloudflare Worker setup mistakes now return beginner-actionable 501 messages:
  missing or unchanged `ZEROCHAT_ACCESS_KEY` reports setup incomplete, and
  missing `zerochat_kv` reports the exact binding name. The Worker security
  check covers both paths, and all localized sync setup guides include the
  troubleshooting wording.
- Updated all 10 Web deployment guides to use the Cloudflare Pages field wording
  `Build output directory / Build directory: dist`, and added a deployment
  readiness guard so new users are less likely to miss the `dist` setting when
  the dashboard wording varies.
- Updated all 10 Web deployment guides to say that the Cloudflare dashboard and
  GitHub Actions paths do not require local Node/npm. The cloud build installs
  dependencies and runs `npm run build`; local Node/npm is only needed for
  Wrangler or local testing. A later pnpm pass made the dashboard build command
  explicitly package-manager-neutral with `pnpm run build` or `npm run build`.
- Updated all 10 Web deployment guides to tell unsure beginners to choose the
  Cloudflare Pages dashboard path first, and split the docs index wording so
  sync setup guides are not confused with static Web hosting guides.
- Strengthened `native-build-prereq-check` so it validates required Android,
  Apple, Windows, and Linux project/source entry files in addition to external
  SDK/toolchain commands. Missing native project structure now fails before a
  release machine reaches platform-specific build steps.
- Strengthened Linux native preflight so it requires a Linux host or WSL distro
  before checking Rust/GTK dependencies. Windows or macOS `cargo` on `PATH` no
  longer counts as Linux build/runtime readiness.
- Added 180px, 192px, and 512px PNG install icons alongside the SVG favicon,
  linked the Apple touch icon, cached install icons in the service worker, and
  strengthened `deploy-readiness-check` so PWA install assets stay present in
  both `public/` and `dist/`.
- PWA `theme-color` now follows light, dark, and system theme changes so mobile
  browser chrome and installed Web/PWA windows match the active interface. The
  UI static guard and browser smoke test now both cover this behavior.
- Added `node scripts/pwa-offline-smoke.mjs` to the release gate so the built
  Web/PWA must be controlled by its service worker and survive an offline reload
  without rendering a blank page.
- Message action and model-chip icon buttons now expose `aria-label` in addition
  to `title`, and the UI guard rejects future titled buttons that omit an
  accessible label.
- Topmost dialogs now move keyboard focus inside the modal when they open, and
  trap Tab navigation inside that modal. Browser smoke verifies the Settings
  dialog receives focus and keeps focus after repeated Tab presses instead of
  leaving keyboard users behind the overlay. When the modal stack closes,
  focus is restored to the original opener when it is still in the document.
- Web/PWA now opts into `viewport-fit=cover` and applies safe-area inset padding
  to the mobile shell, sidebar, and modal bounds so installed iOS/iPadOS browser
  chrome and home indicators do not cover primary controls. The UI guard checks
  the safe-area contract.
- Notice messages now expose live-region semantics: normal feedback uses
  `role="status"` with polite announcements, while error feedback uses
  `role="alert"` with assertive announcements. The UI guard checks every notice
  surface uses the shared accessibility props.
- Startup load failures now show a localized failure title, a redacted error
  message, and a clear reload action in every interface language, instead of
  leaving new users at a raw dead-end error page.
- The HTML shell now includes a bilingual `noscript` fallback so users who open
  the Web/PWA with JavaScript disabled see a clear requirement instead of a
  blank page.
- Added a checked-in Android Gradle Wrapper and updated Android build docs so
  new contributors do not need to install Gradle separately.
- Android debug build was exercised from a Windows workspace whose path contains
  non-ASCII characters. Added `android.overridePathCheck=true` so Chinese paths
  do not stop the build before compilation starts.
- Android build was failing because Kotlin targeted the current JDK while Java
  compilation stayed at 1.8. Fixed the Android app module to use Java 17
  compile options and Kotlin `jvmToolchain(17)`.
- Android `SettingsCard` used `Column.() -> Unit` as a Compose slot receiver,
  which is not a type. Replaced it with `ColumnScope.() -> Unit`; the Android
  debug APK now builds successfully with a temporary local JDK/SDK.
- Android build preflight now recognizes the recommended local JDK/SDK tool
  cache as a valid Android build prerequisite, and
  `node scripts/android-debug-build.mjs` injects `JAVA_HOME`, `ANDROID_HOME`,
  and `ANDROID_SDK_ROOT` for that run so a new Windows contributor does not have
  to copy environment-variable commands before building the debug APK.
- After that helper was added, `node scripts\native-build-prereq-check.mjs
  --platform=all` reports Android and Windows prerequisites as present in this
  workspace without manual Android environment variables; the remaining
  prerequisite failures are the real Apple Xcode/Swift and Linux/WSL host
  blockers.
- Repository health now also guards the Android debug build helper behavior:
  it must keep the recommended `C:\ZeroChatAndroidTools` JDK/SDK discovery,
  inject `JAVA_HOME`/`ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`, default to `assembleDebug`, and use the
  Windows Gradle wrapper path through `cmd.exe`.
- Android emulator startup from the Chinese workspace path failed because QEMU
  received a corrupted SDK path and could not load `bios-256k.bin`. The runtime
  QA was rerun through an ASCII junction (`C:\ZeroChatAndroidTools`) while the
  checked-in project stayed unchanged.
- Android cold launch could look like a blank screen before the snapshot loaded.
  Added a lightweight `ZeroChat` loading state so a slow first frame no longer
  looks broken.
- Android Settings opened as a partial bottom sheet and the Appearance language
  controls could sit behind the system navigation bar. Settings now skip the
  partial state, add navigation/IME padding, use a shorter synchronized help
  sentence, and visually passed on the API 36 emulator.
- Android settings category navigation now uses wrapping chip controls instead
  of a scrollable tab row, so narrow screens show Appearance, AI providers,
  Models, Skills, Sync, and Data without clipping. Fresh API 36 screenshots
  were captured for first-run, settings, providers, Skills, Sync, and Data.
- Apple Settings replaced the six-item segmented picker with an adaptive
  wrapping icon grid, matching the same narrow-screen fix for long localized
  category labels without hiding later settings categories off-screen.
- Windows native preflight now discovers MSBuild through Visual Studio
  `vswhere`, but also requires a checked-in WinUI `.sln`/`.vcxproj` or packaging
  project so Windows cannot look build-ready while still requiring manual Visual
  Studio project recreation.
- Windows WebView builds now clean the output `web\` folder before copying the
  current Vite `dist` bundle. A package smoke caught stale hashed chunks in the
  MSIX stage after successive builds; the WinUI project now deletes the old
  bundle first, the MSIX package script refuses to package a copied `web\` tree
  that differs from current `dist`, and the Windows checks guard both rules.
- Windows now includes a checked-in WinUI/C++ solution that builds with MSBuild
  on this machine. The visible Windows app shell loads the same PWA bundle
  through WebView2 using a virtual HTTPS host mapping, which fixes the previous
  blank `file://` WebView load and keeps Windows UI/i18n/Skill/sync behavior
  visually aligned with the Web/PWA surface. A Windows screenshot was captured at
  `.manual-qa/windows-webview-main-clean3.png`.
- Windows Release configuration was also built with MSBuild using the same
  ASCII build root, so the desktop shell no longer has only Debug compile
  evidence. MSIX installation/update/uninstall QA remains the release blocker.
- After the latest Web/PWA UX and accessibility fixes, Windows Release was
  rebuilt again with `ZeroChatBuildRoot=C:\ZeroChatWindowsBuild`; the build
  copied the current hashed `dist` assets into `output\x64\Release\web`, then
  produced fresh unsigned and self-signed MSIX packages. The unsigned and
  signed-but-untrusted install QA dry-runs remained non-mutating.
- After the mobile-landscape chat spacing fix, Windows Release was rebuilt from
  the same repository path, recopied the current hashed `dist` assets into
  `C:\ZeroChatWindowsBuild\output\x64\Release\web`, and repackaged
  `.manual-qa\ZeroChat_0.0.1.0_x64.msix`. A disposable self-signed dry-run
  exposed a real Windows trust nuance: adding a local signer only to
  TrustedPeople is not enough for self-signed MSIX installation because Windows
  also requires the signing root to be trusted. The install QA helper now fails
  quickly with a plain explanation instead of hanging or surfacing a raw
  `Add-AppxPackage` certificate error, and `-RemoveTrustedCertificate` cleans up
  the temporary TrustedPeople entry.
- After the Web/PWA empty-Skill button fix, Windows Release and Debug were
  rebuilt again from `E:\项目\ZeroChat` with the ASCII
  `C:\ZeroChatWindowsBuild` root. Both builds recopied the latest hashed
  `dist` assets into their `web\` folders. A fresh unsigned
  `.manual-qa\ZeroChat_0.0.1.0_x64.msix` was produced with `makeappx`, and the
  install QA helper inspected it in dry-run mode without installing, trusting a
  certificate, or mutating the Windows profile.
- Added `scripts\build-windows.ps1` for the beginner Windows path. It finds
  MSBuild through `vswhere` when `msbuild.exe` is not on PATH, builds the
  Web/PWA bundle unless `-SkipWebBuild` is passed, uses
  `C:\ZeroChatWindowsBuild`, and verifies that `ZeroChat.exe` plus
  `web\index.html` exist for each requested configuration. The Windows WebView
  shell check now guards those helper behaviors, not just the script's
  existence.
- A fresh Release build from the Chinese workspace path `E:\项目\ZeroChat`
  exposed a C++/WinRT `mdmerge` path-encoding failure when intermediate files
  lived under the repository. The WinUI project now defaults to the same ASCII
  `C:\ZeroChatWindowsBuild` root used by the MSIX package script, the Windows
  README documents that default, `windows-webview-shell-check` guards it, and
  both Debug and Release were rebuilt successfully from the non-ASCII repo path.
- Added a checked-in Windows MSIX manifest, package visual assets, and a
  `makeappx`-based packaging script. The script successfully produced an
  unsigned local MSIX from the Release output, excludes `.pdb` files by default,
  and requires the copied `web\index.html` bundle before packaging.
- Extended the Windows packaging script with optional PFX signing. SignTool
  successfully signed a local MSIX as `CN=ZeroChat`; the expected verification
  status remains untrusted because the temporary QA certificate was not installed
  into the system trust store.
- Added a guarded Windows MSIX install QA helper. Its default mode only inspects
  package identity and signature status; installing, trusting a certificate, or
  uninstalling all require explicit switches so release QA cannot mutate a user
  profile by accident.
- The Windows MSIX install QA helper now inspects the newest generated
  `ZeroChat_*.msix` when no package path is passed, so a fresh package is never
  hidden behind an older signed artifact.
- Unsigned Windows MSIX packages now produce a non-mutating dry-run report with
  a clear signing next step instead of an exception. Install and update actions
  still reject unsigned packages.
- The unsigned Windows MSIX dry-run now reports a plain package-signing next
  step instead of exposing a misleading PowerShell execution-policy status
  message to new users.
- Signed-but-untrusted Windows MSIX dry-runs now also use plain wording that
  says the signing certificate is not trusted on this Windows profile.
- Signed Windows MSIX dry runs now also report `SignatureTrusted` and
  `TrustRequired`, making untrusted local signing certificates visible before
  install/update QA.
- A later Windows package pass created a separate one-off signed QA artifact at
  `.manual-qa\ZeroChat_0.0.1.0_x64_trustedqa.msix` using a disposable
  `CN=ZeroChat` code-signing certificate stored under `%TEMP%`. The signed
  dry-run reported identity `ZeroChat`, version `0.0.1.0`, signer
  `CN=ZeroChat`, `Signed=True`, `SignatureTrusted=False`, `TrustRequired=True`,
  and no install/profile mutation. Running the helper with `-Install` before
  root trust failed quickly with the intended explanation that TrustedPeople is
  not enough and the signing root must be trusted. Attempting the OS Root trust
  path in this non-disposable Windows profile hung in the platform certificate
  trust flow, so it was stopped; the temporary certificate was removed from
  CurrentUser My/TrustedPeople/Root, the temp certificate directory was deleted,
  and `Get-AppxPackage -Name ZeroChat` returned no installed package. Trusted
  install/update/uninstall QA therefore remains a release blocker that must run
  in a disposable QA profile or with a certificate chain that is already trusted
  by that profile.
- Strengthened the Windows MSIX install QA helper with explicit `-Update` mode.
  Upgrade QA now requires a previous signed build to already be installed,
  rejects non-incrementing package versions, and verifies the installed version
  after `Add-AppxPackage`; dry-run remains non-mutating.
- Added `node scripts/windows-webview-shell-check.mjs` to the release gate so
  the Windows shell cannot silently drift away from the shared PWA contract:
  WebView2 reference, copied `dist` bundle, virtual HTTPS host mapping,
  missing-bundle recovery page, and documented Release build path are all
  checked statically.
- Removed temporary Windows native startup logging and set the Windows title to
  `ZeroChat`; the Windows build now also copies the generated `dist` assets into
  `web\` beside the executable and shows an in-window recovery message if the
  web bundle is missing.
- The native app index now tells new contributors to run
  `npm run check:native-prereqs -- --platform=<platform>` before opening a
  platform IDE or running platform builds, so SDK/tooling failures are caught
  before the slower native path. A later pnpm pass added the equivalent
  `pnpm run check:native-prereqs -- --platform=<platform>` path everywhere.
- The Windows native QA checklist now runs a Web/PWA build before MSBuild and
  MSIX packaging, which prevents a new tester from packaging stale or missing
  Web/PWA assets. A later pnpm pass made that command `pnpm run build` or
  `npm run build`.
- Android, Apple, Linux, and the fallback Windows native strings now avoid
  over-claiming unverified automatic native cloud sync. Their sync copy says
  settings stay on the device, encrypted sync data is encrypted before upload,
  and Gist settings are compatibility fields while Cloudflare is the native
  auto-sync path after target runtime QA; `copy-consistency-check` now rejects
  the old "Gist/Cloudflare upload from native" wording.
- Android and Apple runtime saved-locally notices now also avoid promising that
  native edits will sync through the selected mode before final native sync QA.
  Android, Apple, Linux, and fallback Windows `app.localFirst` taglines now use local-first encrypted-sync copy,
  and `copy-consistency-check` rejects the older encrypted-sync/cloud-sync
  short phrases.
- Native sync-password change warnings now say future verified cloud sync uses
  the new password instead of implying the unverified native app will immediately
  encrypt future cloud sync itself. The copy guard requires the new wording on
  Android, Apple, Linux, and fallback Windows.
- Native README and platform docs now scope clear-cloud-data as core/source
  support until disposable platform QA verifies upload, restore, clear, and
  post-clear readback. The copy guard rejects the old unqualified native
  Cloudflare remote-clear wording.
- Android and Apple clear-cloud danger dialogs now include the restart-fresh detail4 paragraph
  in the visible native i18n body, so users know the sync
  target starts fresh after remote ciphertext is deleted. The copy guard now
  checks both the translated text and the Android/Apple dialog body builders
  that render the new `detail4` paragraph.
- Linux preview-only controls that do not yet write to `SnapshotStore`,
  `AiClient`, `SyncClient`, or Secret Service are now disabled instead of
  looking interactive. The copy guard checks the disabled Linux preview markers

- Android and Apple composer send buttons now disable until the current request
  is actually submittable: text must be non-empty, a usable provider/model must
  exist, image mode must not target Anthropic, and edit/inpaint requests must
  include the required source and mask images. `native-parity-check` guards the
  disabled-send contract in source.
- Android and Apple Skill add/save buttons now stay disabled until trimmed
  Skill content is non-empty, so blank or whitespace-only Skills cannot look
  submittable. `native-parity-check` now guards both native implementations.
- Web/PWA Skill add now follows the same empty-content rule. The Skills settings
  page no longer shows an active accent action for an empty draft, and
  `ui-accessibility-check` guards the disabled state.
- Web/PWA, Android, and Apple Skill creation now use localized fallback Skill
  names and localized default chunk headings instead of leaking English
  `Skill`/`Overview` into non-English interfaces or synced Skill metadata.
  `skill-system-check` and `native-i18n-check` guard those fallback paths.
- The current Windows Release output was repackaged into
  `.manual-qa\ZeroChat_0.0.1.0_x64.msix` after the latest Web/native changes.
  The install QA helper inspected the package in dry-run mode, confirmed

  certificate trust.

- A manual 390px browser pass caught that Settings > Sync kept the user near the

### 2026-06-08 Asia/Shanghai - Web/PWA Inpaint mask disabled tooltip target pass

- Scope: Image inpainting composer mask actions and streaming-safe automatic
  cloud sync. `ImageComposerPanel` now derives separate `maskUndoTooltip` and
  `maskClearTooltip` strings, wraps the disabled "撤销上一笔" / "清除涂抹"
  actions in `.mask-action-tooltip-target`, and keeps each button's `title`,
  `data-tooltip`, `data-mask-action`, and `aria-describedby="mask-keyboard-help"`
  aligned with the visible localized reason. With no mask strokes, the disabled
  controls now explain `notice.maskRequired`; while generation is active they
  switch to the streaming reason instead of looking inert.
- Layout and pointer-event contract: `src/App.css` gives
  `.mask-action-tooltip-target` an inline-flex wrapper, preserves full-width
  ghost-button behavior inside the compact image tool row, and sets
  `.mask-action-tooltip-target .ghost-button:disabled { pointer-events: none; }`
  so the wrapper receives hover/focus testing even when the native button is
  disabled.
- Cloud-sync hardening found during the same browser pass: the full CDP smoke
  exposed a real race where a silent automatic Cloudflare sync could begin from
  a pre-generation snapshot, then write `manifest` / `/sync/head` while an
  assistant message was still streaming and before the user clicked Stop.
  `syncShared` now owns `shouldDeferRemoteWrite`,
  `SyncRemoteWriteDeferredError`, and `assertRemoteWriteAllowed`. `syncRuntimeController`
  skips or swallows silent automatic remote writes while
  `hasPendingGenerationMessage` is true, avoids queuing those stale uploads, and
  passes a live `dataRef` deferral callback into sync transports. `syncCloudflare`
  and `syncGist` call `assertRemoteWriteAllowed(context)` immediately before
  snapshot, incremental, POST, or PATCH remote writes, so already-started
  automatic sync work cannot publish partial streaming turns.
- Guard updates: `scripts/browser-skill-smoke.mjs` now chooses visible tooltip
  targets, scrolls them into view, dispatches pointer and mouse hover events
  with real viewport coordinates, proves Settings fetch-model busy tooltips,
  proves the disabled inpaint mask undo/clear tooltip targets, and re-runs the
  Cloudflare streaming/stop path to verify no sync writes occur before the turn
  reaches a terminal state. `scripts/ui-accessibility-check.mjs` now requires
  the mask-action tooltip wrappers and the pending-generation sync runtime
  deferral guards. `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` now requires the mask
  tooltip source/CSS/smoke evidence, the syncShared deferral primitive, Gist and
  Cloudflare pre-write assertions, focused transport tests, runtime queue
  deferral tests, and this QA heading.
- Focused test coverage added: `syncRuntimeController.test.ts` now covers not
  queuing silent uploads while a generation is pending and silently deferring a
  mid-sync remote write when generation starts. `syncCloudflare.test.ts` now
  proves pending-generation deferral stops before any incremental PUT/head
  write. `syncGist.test.ts` now proves pending-generation deferral stops before
  any new Gist POST/PATCH write.

### 2026-06-09 Asia/Shanghai - Provider Base URL mapped-address safety hardening

- Scope: closed a Provider credential exfiltration edge case across the Web/PWA,
  live-provider smoke scripts, Android, Apple, Linux, and Windows source
  surfaces. User-supplied Provider Base URLs already rejected plaintext HTTP,
  credentials, query strings, fragments, localhost, and private IPv4/hostnames;
  this pass now also rejects URL-parser-normalized decimal/hex/octal loopback
  IPv4 inputs, IPv6 loopback/unspecified/ULA/link-local hosts,
  IPv4-compatible and IPv4-mapped IPv6 hosts that embed private/loopback IPv4,
  NAT64 mapped private/loopback IPv4 such as `64:ff9b::7f00:1`, and 6to4
  private/loopback IPv4 such as `2002:c0a8:0101::1` before any API key can
  leave the device. Public HTTPS IPv6, public NAT64 mappings, and public 6to4
  mappings remain allowed.
- Cross-platform implementation: `src/services/providerSafety.ts`,
  `scripts/live-provider-smoke.mjs`, `scripts/live-provider-ui-smoke.mjs`,
  Android `AiProtocol.kt`, Apple `AiProtocol.swift`, Linux `ai_protocol.rs`,

### 2026-06-09 Asia/Shanghai - Windows fallback SSE streaming parity

- Scope: Windows fallback SSE streaming parity now requests text/event-stream
  and stream=true for native fallback chat. The Windows native fallback
  `AiClient::StreamChatAsync` no longer buffers a full provider response before
  invoking the token callback: it sets `Accept: text/event-stream`, sends
  request bodies with `stream=true`, uses `HttpCompletionOption::ResponseHeadersRead`,
  reads partial `DataReader` chunks behind `WindowsAiStreamIdleTimeout`, and
  feeds each SSE data event through `ReadSseWithTimeoutAsync` before calling
  `onToken(delta)`. Retry behavior now stops after any token has been emitted,
  avoiding duplicated partial assistant text on mid-stream failure.
- Protocol coverage: `apps/windows/ZeroChat/AiClientProtocol.cpp` and
  `apps/windows/ZeroChat/AiClientProtocol.h` now expose
  `ChatDeltaFromSseData` alongside `ChatTextFromResponse`. The delta parser
  covers OpenAI-compatible chat completion `choices[0].delta.content`, the
  fallback `choices[0].message.content` shape, Responses API `delta` and
  `response.delta` payloads, and Anthropic `content_block_delta` /
  `delta.text` events.
- Guard coverage: `scripts/native-parity-check.mjs` now requires `stream=true`,
  `HttpMediaTypeWithQualityHeaderValue(L"text/event-stream")`,
  `HttpCompletionOption::ResponseHeadersRead`, partial SSE chunk reads,
  `ProcessSseLine`, `ProcessSseEvent`, `ReadSseWithTimeoutAsync`,
  `ChatDeltaFromSseData`, and the `emittedToken` retry guard.
  `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs` and
  `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` now enforce the same Windows fallback
  SSE contract and require this QA audit evidence to stay visible.
