### 2026-06-11 Asia/Shanghai - Live provider Realtime WebSocket drill correction

- Scope: `scripts/live-provider-smoke.mjs` no longer treats Realtime as a
  one-shot JSON `POST /realtime` body check. The opt-in Realtime drill now
  builds `wss://.../realtime?model=<selected realtime model>`, performs a TLS
  WebSocket upgrade with the bearer authorization header, sends a minimal
  text-only `conversation.item.create` plus `response.create`, and waits for
  both `session.created` and `response.done` before reporting Realtime
  evidence.
- Safety: the report remains summary-only. It records selected model id,
  `transport: "websocket"`, `endpointPath: "/realtime"`, the 101 handshake
  status, booleans for session/request/response milestones, event-type names,
  server byte counts, and timeout. It does not print provider payload text,
  URLs, endpoints, or credentials, and still requires
  `ZEROCHAT_LIVE_PROVIDER_REALTIME_CONFIRM=CHECK_ONE_REALTIME_SESSION`.
- Guard coverage: `scripts/live-provider-smoke-check.mjs` now locks the
  WebSocket URL builder, upgrade headers, bearer header, Realtime client
  events, `response.done` wait, and summary fields. The runtime artifact gate
  now requires passing provider reports with requested Realtime evidence to
  include WebSocket transport, a 101 handshake, `session.created`,
  `response.done`, and summarized byte/event counts.
  `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` guards the same boundary.
- Residual scope: no live provider credentials were used in this pass and no
  provider request was sent. This removes a false-positive Realtime release
  drill shape, but it does not close the live-provider full capability release
  drill, disposable live sync release-pass, Apple target runtime QA, Linux
  target runtime QA, or first hosted native CI artifact blockers.

- Scope: moved the hosted native CI handoff one step closer to release-grade by
  adding a `hosted-native-ci-evidence` job to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. The
  job depends on `windows-native`, `android-native`, `linux-native`, and
  `apple-core`, and only runs when all four native jobs succeeded, so it cannot
  claim `--jobs-success` after a failed native build. The workflow now grants

  job can download same-run artifacts without broad repository write access.

  `android-native-prereq`, `android-debug-apk`, `android-release-apk`,
  `linux-release-binary-and-runtime-smoke`, `apple-runtime-smoke`, and
  `apple-ios-simulator-build` into the artifact-name directories expected by
  `scripts/hosted-native-ci-evidence-report.mjs`, preserving the Apple
  Simulator bundle under
  `.manual-qa/hosted-native-ci/apple-ios-simulator-build/ZeroChat.app`. It then
  generates `.manual-qa/hosted-native-ci-evidence.json` from `${{ github.repository }}`,
  `${{ github.run_id }}`, `${{ github.run_attempt }}`, and `${{ github.sha }}`,
  validates that report with

### 2026-06-19 Asia/Shanghai - Provider special-use IP URL safety hardening

- Scope: tightened Provider Base URL and live-drill endpoint safety across
  Web/PWA, Android, Apple, Linux, Windows, live-provider API/UI smoke scripts,
  and the disposable live-sync drill. In addition to HTTP, credentials,
  query/hash URLs, localhost, private IPv4, LAN names, IPv6 ULA/link-local, and
  embedded private IPv4 forms, the shared safety intent now rejects
  documentation ranges such as `192.0.2.1`, `198.51.100.2`, `203.0.113.8`,
  benchmarking ranges such as `198.18.0.1`, multicast/reserved IPv4 such as
  `224.0.0.1`, IPv6 documentation hosts such as `2001:db8::1`, IPv6 multicast
  such as `ff02::1`, and NAT64/6to4 forms that embed those special-use IPv4
  addresses before any provider key or disposable live-sync resource can be
  touched.
- Cross-platform implementation: `src/services/providerSafety.ts`,
  `apps/android/app/src/main/java/app/zerochat/ai/AiProtocol.kt`,
  `apps/apple/Sources/ZeroChatCore/AiProtocol.swift`,
  `apps/linux/src/ai_protocol.rs`,
  `apps/windows/ZeroChat/AiClientProtocol.cpp`,
  `scripts/live-provider-smoke.mjs`,
  `scripts/live-provider-ui-smoke.mjs`, and
  `scripts/live-sync-release-drill.mjs` now share the same special-use IPv4/IPv6
  rejection markers. The Linux helper now passes the full parsed IPv4 octets to
  `is_disallowed_ipv4`, so third-octet-specific documentation ranges cannot be
  flattened away.
- Guard coverage: focused tests were extended in
  `src/services/__tests__/providerSafety.test.ts`, Android `AiProtocolTest.kt`,
  Apple `ProviderRequestTests.swift`, Linux `ai_protocol.rs` unit tests, and
  the live-provider/live-sync drill check scripts. `scripts/repository-health-
  check.mjs` and `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` now guard the source,
  tests, and docs so this URL-safety boundary cannot silently regress.
- Residual scope: this is a Provider/live-drill safety hardening pass. It does
  not close Apple/Linux target runtime QA, Windows trusted MSIX release-pass,
  disposable live-sync release-pass, hosted native CI evidence, or live-provider
  full-capability release evidence.

### 2026-06-24 Asia/Shanghai - Synced provider secret persistence failure safety

- Scope: Web/PWA cloud sync now applies Provider secrets from an accepted
  remote vault without first clearing all local provider/proxy secrets.
  `applySyncedSecrets` in `src/services/syncRuntimeController.ts` copies the
  synced key map, persists incoming keys first, then clears only stale provider
  ids with `clearProviderSecretsById(staleProviderIds)` and updates visible
  `providerKeys` after persistence succeeds. If local secret storage rejects a

  visible and the broad all-provider secret wipe is not invoked, so users can

### 2026-07-14 Asia/Shanghai - Cross-platform AI Provider response body limits

- Root cause: Provider success bodies, error bodies, and SSE streams did not
  share cross-platform total byte budgets. Several native HTTP convenience APIs
  could also prebuffer the complete body before application-level checks, so an
  abnormal or hostile upstream could cause unbounded memory growth before JSON,
  text, audio, image, or SSE parsing began.
- Contract: all clients now cap error bodies at 16,384 bytes, text/JSON and SSE
  totals at 8,000,000 bytes, and image JSON/audio bodies at 32,000,000 bytes.
  Each transport rejects an oversized declared content length before reading,
  counts actual streamed bytes, and cancels or drops the body on overflow.
- Web/PWA: `providerErrors.ts` owns bounded byte/text/JSON readers and the shared
  accumulator. Chat SSE readers preflight declared lengths and share the 8 MB
  total counter; speech, transcription, image, model-list, and capability paths
  use endpoint-specific budgets. Direct `Response.text()`, `json()`,
  `arrayBuffer()`, and `blob()` reads are guarded out of Provider transports.
- Android: `AiClient.kt` uses Ktor `prepareGet`/`preparePost` statements so
  headers are available before body collection. `AiHttpBody.kt` owns declared
  length checks, bounded channel reads, cancellation, and a raw-byte SSE line
  reader with the existing idle timeout. Focused tests cover declared overflow,
  actual streamed overflow, line parsing, total SSE overflow, and AiClient model
  and stream integration.
- Apple: `CredentialBoundURLSession.swift` owns reusable expected-length and
  streamed-byte checks. `AiClient.swift` uses bounded non-stream reads and counts
  raw SSE bytes before UTF-8 line decoding. Source tests lock budgets and
  accumulator overflow; this Windows host has no Swift/Xcode toolchain, so Apple
  compilation and target-runtime behavior remain unverified here.
- Linux: `ai.rs` reuses the existing bounded HTTP body helpers for non-stream
  responses, checks SSE content length, and counts each raw chunk before line
  decoding. Rust formatting and packaging checks passed on this host; Linux GTK
  target compilation/runtime remains separate target-host evidence.
- Windows: `AiClient.cpp` defaults Provider sends to `ResponseHeadersRead`, then
  enforces declared and actual byte limits through bounded buffer/text helpers.
  The current Release x64 native build passed with zero warnings and zero errors.
- Focused validation before guard integration: Web Provider/chat tests passed 2
  files / 25 tests after declared SSE coverage; the wider affected Web set passed
  5 files / 45 tests, TypeScript and focused ESLint passed, Android JVM tests
  passed 214 tests, Linux formatting/packaging checks passed, and Windows Release
  x64 compiled successfully.
- Guard coverage: `scripts/native-parity-check.mjs`,
  `scripts/repository-health-check.mjs`, and
  `scripts/completion-audit-check.mjs` require the shared budgets, declared and
  streamed limit paths, overflow tests, and headers-first APIs while rejecting
  the old unbounded convenience reads.
- Post-integration validation: native parity, repository health, completion
  audit, documentation links, production build, and bundle checks passed. The
  full release verification passed 143 test files / 1,156 tests, 100% focused
  service coverage, Lighthouse 100/100/100, browser/locale/PWA and focused UI
  smokes, and the 118-screenshot release visual audit. Windows WebView runtime
  QA passed against the current 39-file / 1,021,914-byte `dist`; the refreshed
  unsigned MSIX candidate is 1,307,252 bytes and its staged Web tree matches the
  same `dist`. The release command still exits nonzero only for the current
  external Windows AppX deployment cleanup blocker, so trusted MSIX install,
  update, and uninstall remain unproven.
- QA marker: AI Provider response bodies enforce declared and streamed byte limits across Web and native clients.
- Residual scope: this is memory/liveness hardening only. It does not prove
  Provider trust or DNS-rebinding resistance, Apple/Linux target runtime QA,
  hosted native CI, trusted MSIX, disposable live sync, live-provider full
  capability, or browser-origin live-provider release evidence.

## 2026-07-14 Asia/Shanghai - Cross-platform encrypted sync decompression limits

- Root cause: encrypted incremental objects were bounded while compressed in transit, but authenticated gzip output was unbounded before JSON decoding. A small valid encrypted object could therefore bypass the transport budget and expand until process memory was exhausted.
- Web `src/services/crypto.ts` now collects transform output with a bounded stream reader, cancels on overflow, applies the same `32,000,000`-byte budget to `gzip` and `none`, and no longer uses `Response(stream).arrayBuffer()`.
- Android `CryptoEngine.kt` now reads `GZIPInputStream` through a fixed buffer and checks the total before every `ByteArrayOutputStream.write`; `readBytes()` is absent.
- Apple `CryptoEngine.swift` now checks every zlib output chunk before `Data.append` and exposes a typed decompression-limit error.
- Linux `crypto.rs` now uses a fixed-buffer bounded reader; the previous unbounded `read_to_end` path is absent.
- Focused validation: Web gzip boundary tests passed 3/3; Android JVM tests passed 218/218 across 32 suites, including the new 3/3 decompression tests; Linux rustfmt and packaging checks passed. Apple and Linux runtime tests remain target-host evidence and are not claimed on Windows.

QA marker: Encrypted sync gzip output stays bounded before JSON decoding across Web and native clients.

## 2026-07-14 Asia/Shanghai - Cross-platform user-selected file limits

- Root cause: backup, Skill, and image picker paths buffered the complete selected
  file before any business validation. Web used `File.text()`/`FileReader`,
  Android used `readText()`/`readBytes()`, Apple used one-shot
  `Data`/`String(contentsOf:)`, and Linux used `fs::read*`. A hostile, damaged,
  or accidentally selected large file could therefore exhaust memory before
  parsing or request construction.
- Contract: encrypted backup files are capped at 50,000,000 bytes, Skill files
  at 2,000,000 bytes, and image files at 20,000,000 bytes. The same decimal-byte
  budgets and localized MB messages are used across Web, Android, Apple, and
  Linux. Every platform also checks the final serialized encrypted backup before
  creating or writing an export, so newly generated backups remain importable.
- Web: `localFileLimits.ts` validates immutable `File.size` before invoking
  `File.text()` or constructing `FileReader`. Focused tests cover all budgets,
  the exact boundary, overflow, invalid limits, and proof that an oversized
  image never constructs `FileReader`. Backup export checks the pretty-printed
  JSON Blob byte length before download.
- Android: `LocalFileLimits.kt` reads `ContentResolver` streams through a fixed
  buffer and rejects before `ByteArrayOutputStream.write`. Backup, Skill, and
  image imports use it; backup export checks the serialized UTF-8 envelope before
  opening the output stream. Image picker failures now become localized inline
  notices, preserve the previous selection, and picker cancellation no longer
  clears an existing image.
- Apple: `LocalFileLimits.swift` preflights available file metadata and still
  reads through bounded `FileHandle` chunks so unknown or changing lengths
  cannot bypass the limit. Backup, Skill, and image paths use the shared reader;
  export checks the final document `Data.count`, and typed overflow errors are
  localized by `NativeI18n`.
- Linux: `local_file.rs` combines metadata preflight with a bounded `Read` loop.
  Backup, Skill, and image paths no longer call one-shot `fs::read*` APIs, and
  backup export checks ciphertext length before `fs::write`.
- Validation: Web focused tests passed 5/5, production build and full ESLint
  passed, Android `check:android-unit` passed 34 suites / 226 tests / 0
  failures, and Linux rustfmt plus packaging checks passed. Apple source tests
  were added, but this Windows host has no Swift/Xcode toolchain, so Apple
  compile/runtime evidence remains target-host work.
- Guard coverage: native parity, repository health, and completion audit lock
  the three budgets, bounded-reader primitives, integration call sites,
  boundary tests, localized error key, and absence of the former unbounded
  convenience APIs.
- Residual scope: Windows WebView uses the Web file picker path; the native
  Windows fallback currently exposes no separate backup, Skill, or image file
  picker. This hardening does not close Apple/Linux target-runtime QA, trusted
  MSIX release-pass, hosted native CI, disposable live-sync, or live-provider
  release evidence.

QA marker: User-selected backup, Skill, and image files stay bounded before full buffering across platforms.

## 2026-07-14 Asia/Shanghai - Cross-platform native local snapshot limits

- Root cause: every native client trusted its app-owned `snapshot.v1.json` and
  buffered the complete file before JSON decoding. Android used
  `readText()`, Apple used `Data(contentsOf:)`, Linux used
  `fs::read_to_string`, and Windows used `FileIO::ReadTextAsync`. External
  corruption, restore residue, or abnormal growth could therefore exhaust
  memory before parsing. Android and Linux also overwrote the live file
  directly, exposing crash-partial JSON.
- Contract: Android, Apple, Linux, and Windows cap the native local snapshot at
  64,000,000 bytes. Load paths combine metadata preflight with an actual
  streamed-byte limit, so unknown or changing lengths cannot bypass the cap.
  Save paths enforce the same serialized or UTF-8 byte budget before publishing
  a file.
- Android: `SnapshotFileIO.kt` performs bounded buffered reads and writes a
  same-directory temporary file before `fd.sync()` and atomic move. Repository
  load/save/clear operations share one `Mutex`, valid temporary files recover
  when the live file is absent, and startup load failures become localized
  notices before the app falls back to its default snapshot. Tests cover the
  exact boundary, streamed overflow, preservation of the current file after an
  oversized write, and temporary-file recovery.
- Apple: `SnapshotStore.swift` uses the shared bounded file reader, checks the
  encoded `Data.count` before save, and retains atomic `Data.write` publication.
- Linux: `storage.rs` reads through the bounded local-file helper and publishes
  a mode-0600 temporary file with `sync_all`, same-directory `rename`, and
  parent-directory sync. Tests cover oversized-write preservation and valid
  temporary-file recovery.
- Windows: `StorageService.cpp` preflights file properties, reads partial
  16 KiB chunks into a byte buffer with an actual accumulated limit, validates
  the encoded UTF-8 save buffer, and retains temporary-file
  `MoveAndReplaceAsync` publication.
- Validation: Android `check:android-unit` passed 34 suites / 226 tests / 0
  failures / 0 errors / 0 skipped. Windows Release x64 compiled with 0 warnings
  and 0 errors. Linux rustfmt and packaging checks passed. Apple source tests
  were added, but this Windows host has no Swift/Xcode toolchain, so Apple
  compile/runtime remains target-host evidence.
- Guard coverage: native parity, repository health, and completion audit lock
  the shared budget, bounded load/save paths, Android serialization and startup

## 2026-07-14 Asia/Shanghai - Linux local snapshot startup write protection

- Root cause: `LinuxAppState::load()` converted both `SnapshotStore::new()` and
  `store.load()` failures with `.ok()`. A clean first run, unavailable data
  directory, corrupted snapshot, and oversized snapshot therefore all became
  the same default-data state. A later edit or sync could overwrite the only
  recoverable local file with defaults.
- Startup state now distinguishes a missing snapshot from storage setup and
  snapshot decoding/read failures. A clean first run remains writable. Failure
  states keep the default UI available but block local save, auto sync, first
  sync, and manual sync while preserving the existing snapshot.
- Recovery is explicit: encrypted-backup import must atomically persist its
  replacement before clearing the blocker, and local reset clears the blocker
  only after `SnapshotStore::clear()` succeeds. Failed recovery leaves write
  protection active.
- `SnapshotStore` accepts only an absolute `XDG_DATA_HOME`, otherwise it falls
  back to an absolute `HOME/.local/share`. Missing or relative values fail
  closed instead of creating `.local/share` under the current working
  directory.
- Chat and Data settings render localized recovery guidance for unreadable
  snapshots and unavailable storage. Sync errors reuse the same ten-language
  copy instead of exposing raw internal messages.
- Source tests cover clean first run, load failure remaining distinct, corrupted
  snapshot preservation, absolute XDG/HOME resolution, and fail-closed missing
  data homes. Linux rustfmt, packaging, and native-i18n checks passed on this
  host. GTK compilation and runtime remain Linux target-host evidence and are
  not claimed here.
- Repository health, completion audit, and native parity lock the explicit
  failure state, write/sync blockers, recovery boundaries, visible warnings,
  absolute data-directory resolution, source tests, and absence of the former
  `.ok()` error erasure.
- Residual scope: this startup protection does not replace Linux or Apple

## 2026-07-14 Asia/Shanghai - Active native local snapshot load-failure write protection

- Root cause: Android, Apple, and Linux all legitimately use defaults when no
  private snapshot exists, but their failure paths also collapsed an existing
  unreadable, oversized, or unavailable snapshot into the same default state.
  Subsequent save or sync actions could then replace the only recoverable local
  data with defaults.
- Android now routes every app-level snapshot write through a mutex-backed
  `LocalSnapshotRecoveryGate`. After startup load failure, ordinary writes do
  not invoke the repository writer, normalization does not save, and auto,
  first, and manual sync cannot start. Four focused tests prove normal writes,
  writer suppression, failed recovery remaining blocked, and successful
  recovery unblocking.
- Android encrypted-backup import and local reset are the only recovery writes.
  They replace the snapshot first; provider keys or local secrets are changed
  only after that write succeeds. Failed recovery keeps the original file and
  blocker. Chat and Settings render a separate persistent notice that transient
  notices cannot replace.
- Apple now distinguishes `snapshotLoadFailed` from `storageUnavailable`.
  `commit`, provider/secret mutation auto sync, first sync, manual sync, and the
  auto-sync scheduler all share the same blocker. `recoverLocalSnapshot` saves
  atomically before clearing the issue; backup import and reset update Keychain
  state only after recovery succeeds. Chat and Settings show the persistent
  localized notice independently of ordinary notices.
- Linux retains its explicit startup issue, blocked local/auto/manual sync
  paths, encrypted-backup and reset recovery boundaries, and absolute
  XDG/HOME fail-closed data-directory resolution from the preceding audit.
- Validation: Android `check:android-unit` passed 35 suites / 230 tests / 0
  failures / 0 errors / 0 skipped. Native i18n passed for all ten languages.
  This Windows host has no Swift/Xcode or Linux GTK runtime, so Apple and Linux
  target-host compile/runtime evidence is not claimed.
- Scope: Windows WebView uses the Web storage path. The native Windows fallback
  has no writable snapshot UI wired to `StorageService`, so it is not falsely
  claimed as an affected active client.
- Native parity, repository health, and completion audit lock the recovery
  gates, writer suppression, sync blockers, recovery-before-secret ordering,
  persistent notices, ten-language copy, focused tests, and documentation
  marker.
- Residual scope: this data-loss prevention does not replace native target-host
  runtime QA, trusted MSIX release-pass, hosted CI, disposable live sync, or
  live-provider release evidence.

QA marker: Android, Apple, and Linux local snapshot load failures stay write-protected until explicit recovery.

## 2026-07-14 Asia/Shanghai - Web local AES-GCM cross-context key installation

- Root cause: local key creation used a readonly existence check followed by
  candidate generation outside IndexedDB and an unconditional `put`. Two fresh
  tabs could both observe no key, generate different non-extractable keys, and
  overwrite the persistent key while each retained its own in-memory key.
  AppData, Skill chunks, or Provider secrets encrypted by the losing in-memory
  key would become undecryptable after restart.
- `localCrypto.ts` keeps the readonly fast path for an existing key, then uses a
  single `readwrite` transaction to re-read `local-aes-gcm-v1`. It adopts a key
  installed by another context and calls `add`, never `put`, only when the
  transaction still observes an empty store. IndexedDB write-transaction
  serialization makes key installation single-winner across tabs and windows.
- Focused tests simulate another context installing a winner after the readonly
  check and prove encryption uses that winner without calling `add`. A second
  test proves a genuinely empty readwrite transaction installs and uses the
  generated candidate. The related AppData/local-secret set passed 3 files / 25
  tests. Full Web validation passed 146 files / 1,167 tests with 100% focused
  coverage (394 statements, 377 branches, 125 functions, 383 lines), TypeScript,
  focused ESLint, production build, bundle, and real Chromium browser smoke.
  Bundle evidence remained within budget at 97.56 KiB first load and 271.93 KiB
  total static gzip.
- Repository health and completion audit guard the second transactional read,
  `add` semantics, absence of the former overwrite path, both race tests, and
  this evidence marker.
- Residual scope: this prevents divergent local encryption keys. It does not
  recover records already encrypted by a previously lost key, and it does not
  replace trusted MSIX, native target-runtime, hosted CI, disposable live-sync,
  or live-provider release evidence.

QA marker: Web local AES-GCM key creation stays single-winner across browser contexts.

## 2026-07-14 Asia/Shanghai - Web AppData cross-tab compare-and-set writes

- Root cause: AppData encryption protected confidentiality but not write
  ownership. Every save unconditionally replaced the `app` IndexedDB record,
  while the local queue only serialized work inside one page and requeued the
  hydrated snapshot on mount, page hide, and visibility changes. A stale tab
  could therefore overwrite a newer tab without making a new edit.
- Each page now records the random IV of the encrypted AppData record it loaded
  as its local revision. `saveAppData` captures that expected revision before
  asynchronous encryption, then opens one serialized `readwrite` transaction,
  re-reads `app`, and calls `put` only when the current revision still matches.
  A mismatch aborts with `AppDataWriteConflictError`; the winning record is not
  touched, and the page revision advances only after transaction completion.
- A successful full local-data clear rebases the current page to an empty
  revision. Legacy plaintext migration uses a dedicated legacy revision; when
  another page wins migration first, the losing page reloads the encrypted
  winner instead of remaining permanently stale.
- The local save queue records the first hydrated snapshot, the latest
  successfully persisted snapshot, and the active snapshot. It suppresses
  duplicate hydration/background writes and duplicate active flushes, but
  still queues a revert to the previous persisted object when an intermediate
  write is already in flight.
- The conflict message is localized in all ten Web languages. The focused
  storage, queue, and message suites pass 3 files / 35 tests. TypeScript,
  focused ESLint, and i18n completeness pass.
- Full Chromium browser smoke passed in 85.1 seconds. The smoke waits for the
  current encrypted record to stabilize, installs a distinct competing IV,
  changes the real Appearance setting, and proves the localized Chinese
  conflict notice appears while the competing record remains unchanged. It
  then restores the expected revision, changes the setting again, and proves
  the save queue recovers with a new encrypted revision.
- Repository health and completion audit lock the CAS ordering, revision
  lifecycle, duplicate-write suppression, migration rebase, focused tests,
  browser fault injection, and this marker.
- Residual scope: this prevents silent lost updates; it deliberately does not
  guess how to merge two independent local edits. The stale page asks the user
  to reload. This evidence does not replace trusted MSIX, native target-runtime,
  hosted CI, disposable live sync, or live-provider release evidence.

QA marker: Web AppData writes stay compare-and-set across tabs and suppress passive duplicate saves.

## 2026-07-14 Asia/Shanghai - Durable backup import and atomic local reset

- Root cause: backup import and local reset published replacement AppData and
  success notices before `queueLocalSave(...)` completed. That API returned
  `void`, and its queue converted persistence failures into detached notices,
  so a CAS conflict or storage failure could leave visible data, Provider
  secrets, and the durable AppData record on different versions.
- The local save queue now exposes `persistLocalSnapshot(...)`. It discards
  obsolete queued snapshots, drains the active write, skips an already durable
  object, and awaits the requested save. A replacement failure rejects to the
  caller, is never added to background retry before publication, and always
  unlocks the queue in `finally`; routine detached saves keep their existing
  retry and centralized error-reporting behavior.
- Backup import first durably commits the current post-pause snapshot. After
  isolated external Skill content and the Provider secret snapshot are staged,
  it durably commits imported AppData before changing `dataRef`, React state,
  selected Provider, auto-sync, or success copy. A failed imported commit rolls
  back the exact secret application and deletes unpublished imported Skill
  refs while current data remains visible.
- Local reset now clears canonical secrets before opening the documents
  replacement transaction. That transaction clears the shared documents store
  and writes fresh AppData together; transaction construction or fresh `put`
  failure rejects or aborts the whole operation and triggers exact Provider key,
  GitHub token, and sync-passphrase compensation. After both stores commit, the
  page adopts the new revision and marks the queue snapshot as persisted, so
  React publication cannot issue a duplicate save.
- TypeScript and 3 files / 64 focused tests pass. Coverage includes active-save
  drain, exclusive commit failure, queue unlock after rejection, import secret
  and Skill rollback, successful atomic replacement, fresh-write abort, and
  transaction-construction failure. Repository health and completion audit
  lock the implementation order, tests, root wiring, and both markers.
- Residual scope: IndexedDB AppData/Skill documents and the separate secret
  database cannot share one browser transaction. The controller therefore
  uses explicit staging and exact secret compensation around the durable
  documents commit. This
  evidence does not replace trusted MSIX, native target-runtime, hosted CI,
  disposable live sync, or live-provider release evidence.

QA marker: Backup import and local reset publish only durably persisted AppData.

  process had exited, so `first_party_sets.db` remained locked and converted a
  successful three-sample Lighthouse run into a cleanup failure.

  stops the launched process tree, attempts profile deletion first, and only on
  a real deletion failure performs a case-insensitive exact-profile browser
  sweep. It derives descendants from one process snapshot, stops them child
  first, rechecks the bounded PID set, retries deletion, and returns failure if
  the profile still cannot be removed. This keeps the normal path fast without
  weakening the final zero-residue condition.

  the original failure modes. An isolated Chrome/profile benchmark improved
  from about 6.8 seconds to about 1.0 second. The final Lighthouse run exited 0
  in 45.4 seconds with three performance samples of 100 and category medians
  performance/accessibility/best-practices `100/100/100`, FCP `378ms`, and TTI
  `563ms`. Axe exited 0 with zero violations in all seven desktop, mobile, RTL,
  and alert-dialog states.
- `check:repo`, `check:completion-audit`, focused ESLint, and
  `check:local-cleanup` passed. Cleanup printed
  `NO_ZEROCHAT_RUNTIME_PROCESSES` and `NO_ZEROCHAT_BROWSER_PROFILES`; no

## 2026-07-24 Asia/Shanghai - Skill content rows use a durable publication barrier

- Root cause: draft creation, multi-file import, and content editing wrote encrypted
  Skill chunks before publishing an in-memory AppData row, then queued cloud sync
  without waiting for the AppData record to commit. A durable write failure could
  leave orphan chunks and expose a memory-only Skill to sync.
- Fix: all three content-writing actions now pass through
  `commitSkillContentRows(...)`. Sync, success UI, row reveal, and draft clearing
  occur only when `persistPublishedLocalSnapshot(...)` returns a snapshot that
  contains the exact candidate id, content hash, and ordered refs. Failure restores
  only rows still matching this mutation and deletes only candidate refs absent
  from current visible AppData, preserving old or concurrently adopted content.
- Validation: focused TypeScript and ESLint checks passed. The settings Skill
  controller suite passed 1 file / 26 tests, including durable failure rollback
  for draft creation, batch import, and edited content replacement.

QA marker: Skill content rows commit durably before sync or success UI.

- Fix: `apps/linux/src/chat_send_actions.rs` now takes an active stream only when
  its `assistant_message_id` matches the completion. Chat and image completion
  paths share that identity check.
- Regression evidence: the focused Rust test

## 2026-07-25 Asia/Shanghai - Windows trusted navigation recovery owns completion

- Root cause: the Windows WebView host ignored `NavigationCompleted` arguments
  and always applied the startup route. A failed main navigation, stale callback,
  or host-cancelled external navigation could therefore be treated as success and
  leave a blank/error surface. Startup routes were also marked complete before a
  CoreWebView2 instance accepted script submission.
- Fix: each WebView session captures an independent optional trusted navigation
  ID. Only trusted `NavigationStarting` events update it. Completion first checks
  session and ID ownership, resets that ownership, and then checks `IsSuccess`.
  Failure reads `WebErrorStatus` only as an internal category and immediately
  enters the native read-only recovery surface after invalidating the session.
  Initialization and navigation recovery copy contains no URL, status value, or
  HRESULT. External cancellation never replaces trusted ownership. Startup route
  state commits only after the current CoreWebView2 accepts script submission.
- Regression evidence: the focused lifecycle contract passes 6/6, all Windows
  native contracts pass 20/20, the Windows shell gate passes, and Release x64
  builds with 0 warnings and 0 errors while copying the same 42-file `dist` tree.

QA marker: Windows trusted navigation failures enter sanitized native recovery.
QA marker: Windows startup routes commit only after script submission.

## 2026-07-25 Asia/Shanghai - Apple and Linux Provider-key commits are compensating transactions

- Root cause: Apple silently ignored Provider-key rollback failures during
  backup import and sync acceptance. Linux saved a synced snapshot and then
  ignored every Secret Service replacement error. Both paths could expose a
  snapshot whose Provider configuration no longer matched its durable keys.
- Apple fix: Provider-key rollback is throwing, attempts every applied key in
  reverse order, and reports the primary and compensation failures together.
  Backup import, local reset, and accepted sync keep snapshot compensation
  explicit. One published recovery gate owns each whole import/reset operation,
  and Data settings disables duplicate destructive entry while it is active.
- Linux fix: Provider-key replacement uses compare-exchange against captured
  values, flushes Secret Service before publication, and conditionally restores
  only keys still equal to the transaction candidate. `SnapshotStore` now owns
  a locked compare-and-save operation; auto/manual sync and encrypted-backup
  import reject a changed snapshot and run the same credential compensation.
- Validation: `check:native-parity`, `check:repo`, `check:completion-audit`,
  `check:native-i18n`, and `check:linux-fmt` pass. Focused Rust transaction tests
  cover partial replacement, flush failure, concurrent newer-key preservation,
  and snapshot compare-and-save rejection. This Windows host cannot link the
  GTK crate because `pkg-config/libadwaita-1` is unavailable, and it has no
  macOS/Xcode toolchain; target runtime/build evidence remains open.

QA marker: Apple and Linux Provider-key compensation rejects stale or partial snapshot commits.

## 2026-07-26 Asia/Shanghai - Linux local reset commits secrets and snapshot through compensation

- Root cause: `reset_local_data()` ignored Provider-key clear failures, called a
  non-fallible aggregate secret clear, removed the snapshot opportunistically,
  and then published defaults and navigated to chat regardless of Secret
  Service or disk failure. The UI could therefore claim success while durable
  credentials or the previous snapshot remained.
- Secret-store fix: sync passphrase, GitHub token, and Provider keys now expose
  compare-exchange mutations whose in-memory cache is restored if enqueue
  fails. `clear_secrets_transactionally(...)` captures every previous value,
  clears under ownership checks, waits for the Secret Service worker flush, and
  conditionally rolls back in reverse order. A newer concurrent secret is
  preserved rather than overwritten by stale compensation.
- Snapshot fix: reset observes the durable snapshot before clearing secrets and
  writes defaults through the locked `save_if_unchanged` boundary. A changed or
  failed snapshot commit compensates the secret transaction. Visible and
  committed GTK state, plus the storage-recovery blocker, change only after both
  durable sides report success.
- UX fix: failed reset remains on Data settings and shows localized recovery
  guidance. It no longer navigates to chat as if reset succeeded.
- A disposable pure-Rust harness directly referenced the production
  `secret_store.rs`, compiled it on the current host, and passed 4/4 focused
  transaction tests: restoration of sync passphrase, GitHub token, and Provider
  keys; partial clear failure; worker flush failure; and preservation of a newer
  concurrent secret. The harness and target directory were removed afterward.
  Rustfmt, native i18n, and native parity also pass. The complete GTK crate still
  stops at the missing `pkg-config`/`libadwaita-1` host prerequisite before
  project compilation, so full Rust and Secret Service runtime remain open for
  a Linux GTK/libadwaita target host.
- Scope: this is a compensating boundary for in-process errors and races. It is
  not a claim of crash-level ACID across Secret Service and the snapshot file.

QA marker: Linux local reset compensates Secret Service clears when snapshot commit fails.

## 2026-07-26 Asia/Shanghai - Linux Provider credential edits no longer report false success

- Root cause: sync-passphrase, GitHub-token, and Provider-key callers discarded
  Secret Service mutation results. Provider-key save and Provider deletion also
  changed the visible snapshot independently, so a keyring or snapshot failure
  could still be presented as a successful edit.
- All three setters now restore their in-memory cache when command enqueue fails
  and return the failure. Data, Sync, and Provider settings keep the input or
  current card visible and show localized keyring guidance instead of success.
- Provider-key save stages a rollback-capable compare-exchange mutation, commits
  the timestamped candidate through `save_if_unchanged`, and only then publishes
  visible/committed state and queues auto-sync. Snapshot rejection compensates
  only a key still owned by that mutation.
- Ordinary key save deliberately does not wait for worker flush: Linux retains
  its documented session-memory fallback when Secret Service rejects a queued
  write, and the existing issue monitor reports the non-durable state. Provider
  deletion has stricter privacy semantics and uses the flush-requiring mutation
  path before committing the deletion snapshot.
- The focused secret-store test
  `staged_provider_key_commit_preserves_session_fallback_without_flushing`
  locks the no-flush stage and rollback boundary. A disposable compile harness
  then type-checked the production `models.rs`, `secret_store.rs`, and
  `provider_state.rs` together against the real transaction signatures; it and
  its target directory were removed afterward. The focused secret-store harness
  passed 10 tests across Provider-key and reset transaction filters. Native
  parity and repository guards require Result handling, snapshot CAS,
  compensation, durable deletion, and localized failure copy. Linux target
  runtime evidence remains open.

QA marker: Linux Provider credential edits publish only after snapshot CAS.

## 2026-07-26 Asia/Shanghai - Apple Provider deletion binds Keychain to snapshot CAS

- Root cause: the Provider editor cleared its Keychain value synchronously and
  then called the ordinary asynchronous snapshot commit path. A later snapshot
  write failure could therefore retain the Provider configuration while its
  credential had already disappeared.
- `SnapshotStore.saveIfUnchanged` now reads, compares, and atomically writes
  inside the actor. Deterministic JSON comparison rejects a stale durable
  observation without replacing the current file.
- The ViewModel drains prior snapshot writes, captures the source revision,
  clears the key, and runs snapshot CAS. It publishes the deleted Provider and
  migrated conversations only after CAS and revision revalidation. Rejection or
  failure conditionally restores only a still-empty transaction-owned key. A
  revision that changes after CAS restores the latest snapshot before returning.
- Focused evidence includes a real SnapshotStore stale-CAS test and source
  contract assertions that reject direct Keychain clearing from ProviderEditor.
  Windows has no Swift/Xcode toolchain, so Apple target compilation and runtime
  remain required on macOS and are not claimed by this source-level evidence.

QA marker: Apple Provider deletion publishes only after snapshot CAS and conditionally compensates Keychain.

## 2026-07-27 Asia/Shanghai - Apple and Linux cross-process local-data recovery

- Root cause: Apple reset/import and Linux reset/import coordinated a snapshot
  file with Keychain or Secret Service only through current-process rollback.
  Exiting between stores could permanently pair old data with new credentials,
  or a reset snapshot with credentials that had not actually been cleared.
- Both native stores now atomically stage a bounded typed journal before any
  cross-store mutation. Reset journals contain a source fingerprint and target
  snapshot. Import journals retain the already-encrypted backup envelope,
  target timestamp, and complete Provider-id set; no Provider key, GitHub token,
  or sync password is written to the journal in plaintext.
- Apple stores a backup-specific recovery password under a transaction UUID in
  a separate Keychain service. Startup recovers before normal hydration. The
  operation drains old snapshot writers and blocks new commits/secret edits so
  a queued save cannot overwrite the recovered target. Source/target
  fingerprints reject unrelated files, and journal cleanup occurs after the
  target snapshot and Keychain state are installed. If startup recovery leaves
  the app in a persistent fault state, the user's explicit destructive reset
  first discards that unrecoverable journal and its temporary Keychain
  passphrases before staging a fresh reset intent; ordinary import never does so.
- Linux loads journal Provider ids before Secret Service hydration, then runs
  the same recovery function before resolving the initial snapshot. Snapshot
  publication accepts only the journal source or target fingerprint. CAS
  rejection rolls secrets back; a reported write failure re-reads durable data,
  and an unreadable result retains the journal without guessing. Finalization
  removes the journal only while the exact target remains durable.
- Added Apple SnapshotStore round-trip/overlap/malformed-record tests and source
  boundary tests for startup ordering and stale-writer quiescence. Added Linux
  production-recovery tests for interrupted reset, interrupted encrypted import,
  and unrelated-snapshot rollback with journal retention. Linux rustfmt passes.
  This Windows host has no Swift executable, and Linux `cargo check --all-targets`
  stops at missing host `pkg-config/libadwaita-1`; therefore this is source and
  protocol evidence, not Apple/Linux target build, Keychain/Secret Service, UI,
  visual, or runtime release evidence.

## 2026-07-26 Asia/Shanghai - Android local reset survives cross-store process crashes

- Root cause: Data settings cleared `EncryptedSharedPreferences` before saving
  the fresh snapshot. A process exit between those writes permanently removed
  credentials still referenced by the durable old snapshot, and all encrypted
  preference work ran from the Compose action path.
- `SecretStore.stageLocalReset` now captures every supported encrypted value,
  including Provider deletion intents, and atomically replaces active values
  with one encrypted pending-reset record. The repository then commits the
  monotonic default snapshot through compare-and-set before credential cleanup
  can finish. Automatic sync ownership and queued snapshot persistence are
  drained around that boundary.
- Startup hashes the exact loaded snapshot and restores the encrypted backup
  when it still matches the source, finishes deletion when it matches the reset
  candidate, and blocks an unrelated snapshot instead of guessing. An in-memory
  backup also preserves compensation material when a preference commit reports
  an uncertain failure.
- Corrupt-snapshot recovery keeps the recovery gate closed through credential
  finalization. A replacement write failure restores credentials; a cleanup
  failure after replacement leaves the encrypted intent for startup. Compose
  only awaits the root transaction and prevents duplicate reset actions.
- Production and test Kotlin compilation pass. Android lint passes, and the
  complete JVM suite passes 51 files / 360 tests / 0 failures. Eleven focused
  tests cover stable fingerprints, source/candidate/unknown recovery decisions,
  CAS ordering and rejection, revision drift, snapshot and credential failures,

## 2026-07-26 Asia/Shanghai - Android backup import binds Provider keys to the durable snapshot

- Root cause: encrypted-backup import replaced Provider keys one at a time and
  only then asked the root to save the imported snapshot. Its rollback existed
  only in the current process, so a process exit between stores permanently
  paired the old snapshot with imported credentials. The controller also based
  credential cleanup on a Compose-captured snapshot rather than the latest
  serialized root state.
- The document controller now performs bounded file input and decryption only,
  then hands the decoded snapshot and Provider-key map to `ZeroChatApp`. The
  root drains automatic-sync ownership, enters the process-lifetime snapshot
  queue, derives a monotonic candidate from the latest source, and includes
  source, candidate, and default Provider ids in one replacement map.
- `SecretStore.stageProviderKeyImport` atomically writes normalized replacement
  keys and an encrypted durable intent containing previous/replacement keys and
  source/candidate snapshot fingerprints. Repository CAS then commits the
  candidate before intent finalization. CAS rejection, visible revision drift,
  snapshot failure, and finalization failure compensate both stores without
  overwriting an unrelated snapshot.
- Startup reconciles the intent against the exact raw durable snapshot before
  Provider deletion recovery or normalization: source restores previous keys,
  candidate retains replacement keys, and an unrelated fingerprint fails
  closed. If the snapshot cannot be loaded, previous keys are restored; during
  explicit corrupt-snapshot recovery, a post-save finalization failure leaves
  the intent so the next startup can finish deterministically.
- Production and test Kotlin compile. Android lint reports `No issues found`.
  The complete JVM suite passes 52 files / 369 tests / 0 failures / 0 errors.
  Eleven focused import tests cover source/candidate/unknown recovery,
  source-less recovery, stage/CAS/finalize ordering, stale CAS, snapshot failure,
  revision drift, finalization compensation, cancellation precedence, and both
  sides of corrupt-snapshot replacement.
